[Definition 5 of arXiv:2608.08242, 'Bang--bang representation of $3\times 3$ embeddable stochastic matrices'] The set $R_n\subseteq\mathcal M_+$ consists of the matrices $A$ for which
	\[
	A\sim
	X_{i_nj_n}(t_n)\cdots X_{i_1j_1}(t_1)
	\]
	for some $i_\ell\neq j_\ell$ and some $t_\ell\geq0$. Put
	$R_\infty=\bigcup_nR_n$.
	
	The threshold region $\T$ consists of matrices $A\in R_\infty$ with at least one zero entry.
	
	
	The vestibule $\V$  consists of the matrices $A>0$ such that $A\sim B X_{ij}(t)$
	for some $B\in\T$, some $i\neq j$, and some $t>0$.
	
	The narrow hall $\NH$ consists of the matrices $A\notin\T\cup\V$ such that $A\sim B X_{ij}(t)$
	for some $B\in\V$, some $i\neq j$, and some $t>0$.
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2608.08242

body: Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a measure space, let g be a nonnegative mu-integrable function on X, and let f_1, f_2, ... be measurable functions with |f_n| <= g pointwise almost everywhere for every n. Then liminf_n f_n and limsup_n f_n are integrable, and the integral over X of liminf_n f_n dmu <= liminf_n of the integral of f_n dmu <= limsup_n of the integral of f_n dmu <= the integral over X of limsup_n f_n dmu. This chain follows from applying Fatou's lemma to g - f_n and to g + f_n, and it yields the dominated convergence theorem whenever f_n converges pointwise a.e.
title: Fatou-Lebesgue theorem

body: [Corollary 2.4 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] For any $t>0$ and any $0<a\leq b\leq 1$, the probability distribution $P^{\varepsilon}_{c}(\cdot\,:\,t,a,b)$ over $\mathbb{N}_{0}$ converges in law to a Poisson distribution with parameter $f(0)\,t\,\lambda_{*}([a,b])=f(0)\,t\,\int_{a}^{b}\cfrac{dx}{x^{2}}=f(0)\,t\,(a^{-1}-b^{-1})\ .$ Furthermore, we have that, for any $n\geq 0$, the function $\Phi_{n}^{\varepsilon}:r\in[0,\infty)\mapsto\mathbb{P}(e_{1}^{\varepsilon}\geq r,N^{\varepsilon}_{(0,r]}([a,b])=n)\in[0,1]$ converges uniformly on any compact interval $[0,t]$, $t>0$, as $\varepsilon$ vanishes to $\Phi_{n}:r\in[0,\infty)\mapsto e^{-rf(0)}e^{-rf(0)\lambda_{*}([a,b])}\frac{(rf(0)\lambda_{*}([a,b]))^{n}}{n!}\in[0,1]\ ,$ where $\lambda_{*}([a,b])=\int_{a}^{b}dx/x^{2}=a^{-1}-b^{-1}$ as in the first part. [The paper prints this limit as $e^{-rf(0)}e^{-r\lambda_{*}([a,b]}\frac{(r\lambda_{*}([a,b]))^{n}}{n!}$; the factor $f(0)$ and the closing parenthesis are restored here: the limit is forced by Proposition 2.2, whose generating function $Z(z,\sigma:a,b)=\sum_{n}z^{n}\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-\sigma r}\Phi_{n}(r)\,dr=1/(\sigma+f(0)+(1-z)f(0)(1/a-1/b))$ inverts to it, and the paper derives the first part, Poisson with parameter $f(0)\,t\,(a^{-1}-b^{-1})$, from it.] Notation from the paper: $e_{1}^{\varepsilon}=\inf\{t\geq 0:X_{t}^{\varepsilon}>y_{*}^{\varepsilon}\}$ is the first jump time; $N^{\varepsilon}_{(0,r]}([a,b])$ is the number of pre-spikes in $(0,r]\times[a,b]$; and $P^{\varepsilon}_{c}(n,t:a,b)$ is the probability of exactly $n$ pre-spikes in $(0,t)\times[a,b]$ given no jump in $(0,t)$, i.e. the no-jump probability of that event divided by $\mathbb{P}(e_{1}^{\varepsilon}\geq t)$.

[Proposition 125 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] In the setting of Theorem~\ref{proposition_FFF_conditioning}, let $\mu^X$ be the equilibrium measure of the ensemble $X$, $\mu^Y$ the equilibrium measure of $Y$. Let $h \in [H]$ and set $\amsmathbb{A}_h^{Y} = \amsmathbb{A}^Y \cap [\hat{a}_h',\hat{b}_h']$. For any $\delta > 0$, there exists constants $C_1,C_2 > 0$ depending only on $\delta$ and the constants in the assumptions such that, for any $z \in \amsmathbb{C}$ at distance at least $\delta$ from $\amsmathbb{A}_h^Y$, we have
\[
\bigg|\int_{\amsmathbb{A}^{Y}_h} \frac{\mu_h^X(x) - \mu^{Y}_h(x)}{z - x} \dd x \bigg| \leq \frac{C_1}{\N}.
\]
The upper bound is actually
\[
\bigg|\int_{\amsmathbb{A}^{Y}_h} \frac{\mu_h^X(x) - \mu^{Y}_h(x)}{z - x} \dd x \bigg| \leq \frac{C_2}{\N^2}.
\]
in case the following three conditions hold simultaneously
\begin{itemize}
\item the endpoints $\hat{a}_h'$ and $\hat{b}'_h$ are in a void, or $\theta_{h,h} = 1$;
\item $\iota_h^{-,X} = 0$, or $\rho_{h,j}^{-,X} = \theta_{h,h}$ for every $j \in [\iota_h^{-,X}]$;
\item $\iota_h^{+,X} = 0$, or $\rho_{h,j}^{+,X} = \theta_{h,h}$ for every $j \in [\iota_h^{+,X}]$.
\end{itemize}
Similar results hold in the setting of Theorem~\ref{proposition_fluct_conditioning}, provided we take $\mu^X$ to be the measure obeying fixed filling fractions constraints and compare it with $\mu^Y$ corresponding to the same constraints. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited), claim T381-C002 v1. Let n(lambda) be polynomial, efficiently computable and positive. A stateless polynomial-time watermark for the n-bit uniform binary model yields a secret-key zero-bit PRC for exactly the same binary channel C if it has (i) undetectability for polynomially many samples under one key, (ii) uniformly negligible key-averaged acceptance of every fixed key-independent string, and (iii) negligible robust-completeness error on outputs whose original-model empirical entropy exceeds b_lambda(n), with b_lambda(n)<=n. Encode by watermark sampling and decode by keyed detection. With a deterministic termination token use b_lambda(n+1)<=n, strip that token on encoding and restore it on detection. Malformed outputs can be replaced by 0^n, adding only their negligible probability to completeness error. For independent fair-bit refresh rate s the exact inherited bit-flip rate is s/2. This gives no unconditional impossibility from one-way functions; only applicable black-box separation classes transfer.
Stateless randomized watermark; polynomial length and running time
Repeated-query computational undetectability under a common key
Uniform pointwise key-averaged negligible soundness
Robust completeness for the specified exact channel
Attainable original-model empirical-entropy threshold

Let W be a real symmetric n by n matrix whose entries W_{ij} for i <= j are independent standard Gaussians, and let H = W / sqrt(n) with eigenvalues lambda_1, ..., lambda_n. Let f be Lipschitz with constant ||f||_L. Then for every t > 0, P( | (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n f(lambda_i) - E (1/n) sum_i f(lambda_i) | >= t ) <= 2 exp( - n^2 t^2 / (4 ||f||_L^2) ). The exponent scales like n^2 t^2, not n t^2: linear eigenvalue statistics are FAR more concentrated than an average of n independent samples would be, and their fluctuations are of order 1/n rather than 1/sqrt(n). This is a consequence of the eigenvalue repulsion built into the matrix model, and it is one of the few places where a naive independence heuristic gives the wrong exponent by a whole power of n. The result needs only Lipschitz f - no smoothness, no boundedness - and it is a statement about concentration around the MEAN, not about identifying the mean, which is the separate content of Wigner's theorem. The constant 4 in the denominator is tied to the stated normalisation (independent standard Gaussians for the free entries, then divided by sqrt(n)); a different convention rescales it. [standard; the argument is Hoffman-Wielandt plus Gaussian Lipschitz concentration, e.g. Anderson, Guionnet and Zeitouni, An Introduction to Random Matrices, Theorem 2.3.5]
free entries independent standard Gaussian, H = W/sqrt(n)
f Lipschitz; no other regularity
the bound is around the mean, which is not identified here

Let H and H' come from free-entry vectors w and w' in R^N with N = n(n+1)/2. The Hoffman-Wielandt inequality gives sum_i ( lambda_i(H) - lambda_i(H') )^2 <= || H - H' ||_{HS}^2 when the eigenvalues of both are listed in the same order. Hence | sum_i f(lambda_i(H)) - sum_i f(lambda_i(H')) | <= ||f||_L sum_i |lambda_i(H) - lambda_i(H')| <= ||f||_L sqrt(n) ( sum_i (lambda_i(H) - lambda_i(H'))^2 )^{1/2} <= ||f||_L sqrt(n) || H - H' ||_{HS}, the middle step being Cauchy-Schwarz. Now || H - H' ||_{HS} = || W - W' ||_{HS} / sqrt(n), and || W - W' ||_{HS}^2 = sum_i (w_{ii} - w'_{ii})^2 + 2 sum_{i<j} (w_{ij} - w'_{ij})^2 <= 2 || w - w' ||_2^2 because off-diagonal free entries are counted twice in the Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Combining, | F(w) - F(w') | <= sqrt(2) ||f||_L || w - w' ||_2 where F(w) = sum_i f(lambda_i(H)). So F is Lipschitz with constant sqrt(2) ||f||_L as a function of the standard Gaussian vector w. [Proposition prop:two-example of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $B:=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1\}$ be the unit disk centered at the origin
and, for $\tau>0$, set
\[
  F_\tau(z):=z+\tau z^3,
  \qquad D_\tau:=F_\tau(B).
\]
Then
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] For every $\tau\in(0,1/3)$, the domain $D_\tau$ is a bounded,
simply connected, noncircular domain with analytic boundary.
\item[(ii)] There exist $\tau_0\in(0,1/3)$ and a family
$\{r_\tau\}_{0<\tau<\tau_0}\subset(0,1)$ such that
\[
  r_\tau\longrightarrow r_0:=\sqrt{\sqrt5-2}
  \quad\text{as }\tau\to0,
\]
and, for every $\tau\in(0,\tau_0)$ and every $\mu>0$, the function
$W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}$ corresponding to
$\kappa_1=\mu=-\kappa_2$ has a strict nondegenerate local minimum point at
\[
  \bigl(F_\tau(r_\tau),F_\tau(-r_\tau)\bigr).
\]
\end{itemize}

body: Let W_t be a standard Brownian motion on [0,T] under a probability measure P, and let theta_t be an adapted process satisfying Novikov's condition E[exp((1/2) integral_0^T theta_t^2 dt)] < infinity. Define Z_t = exp(-integral_0^t theta_s dW_s - (1/2) integral_0^t theta_s^2 ds) and a new measure Q with dQ/dP = Z_T. Novikov's condition makes Z_t a true martingale, and Girsanov's theorem states that under Q the process W~_t = W_t + integral_0^t theta_s ds is again a standard Brownian motion. So an equivalent change of measure removes or adds a drift theta. Due to Igor Girsanov.

[Theorem 12 of arXiv:2512.01483, 'Scaling Limits of Line Models in Degenerate Environment'] For $T>0$, let $\hat{X}^{(T)}(t) := (\hat{X}^{(T)}_1(t), \hat{X}^{(T)}_2(t))$, $t \geq 0$, where 
\[ \hat{X}^{(T)}_1(t) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}} \hat{X}^T_1(Tt), \quad \hat{X}^{(T)}_2(t) := T^{-\frac{1}{2\delta}} \hat{X}^T_2(Tt), \qquad t \geq 0. \]
Then, for $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $\omega$, as $T \to \infty$, the process $(\hat{X}^{(T)}(t))_{t \geq 0}$ converges in distribution, in $D \times D$, to  
$\mathcal{X}(t) = (\mathcal{X}_1(t), \mathcal{X}_2(t))_{t \geq 0}$, where 
\begin{equation}

\mathcal{X}_1(t) = B_1(t), \quad \mathcal{X}_2(t) = B_2( \Delta^{-1}(t)), \qquad t \geq 0,
\end{equation}
where $B_1$ and $B_2$ are two independent Brownian motions with diffusion coefficient $\sqrt{2}$,  $\Delta(t) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} L^{B_2}_t(x) \, \mathcal{H}(dx)$, $t \geq 0$, and $(\Delta^{-1}(t))_{t \geq 0}$ denotes the inverse of $(\Delta(t))_{t \geq 0}$ (note that, by Lemma \ref{lem:delta_increasing}, the paths of $(\Delta(t))_{t \geq 0}$ are strictly increasing). body:
Recall that a real function g on a topological space Z is of BAIRE CLASS ONE if it is the pointwise limit of a sequence of continuous real functions on Z. THEOREM (Baire for R x R; Rudin in this generality): let X be a METRIC space, let Y be a topological space (in particular a metric space), and let f: X x Y -> R be SEPARATELY CONTINUOUS, i.e. for each fixed y the map x -> f(x,y) is continuous on X and for each fixed x the map y -> f(x,y) is continuous on Y. Then f is of Baire class one on X x Y: there is a sequence of continuous functions f_n: X x Y -> R with f_n(x,y) -> f(x,y) for every (x,y). CONSEQUENCE (Baire's theorem on functions of the first class): if in addition X x Y is a Baire space - for instance if X and Y are both complete metric, or both locally compact Hausdorff - then the set of points at which f is JOINTLY continuous is a dense G_delta subset of X x Y, and its complement is meagre. So a separately continuous function is jointly continuous at 'most' points, in the sense of category. CLASSICAL EXTENSION: a function of n variables that is separately continuous in each variable is of Baire class n - 1 (Lebesgue); the case n = 2 is the theorem above. SHARP EDGES. (a) Separate continuity does NOT give joint continuity: f(x,y) = xy/(x^2 + y^2) with f(0,0) = 0 is separately continuous on R^2, indeed continuous on each line through the origin, and is discontinuous at the origin (it equals 1/2 on the diagonal). The theorem therefore cannot be strengthened to continuity anywhere in particular, only to a residual set of continuity points. (b) The metric structure of the first factor is essential to the proof, which builds a locally finite partition of unity on X; for arbitrary topological factors the statement requires extra hypotheses and should not be quoted in that generality. (c) The consequence about continuity points needs X x Y to be a Baire space; on a non-Baire domain 'dense G_delta' carries no information, and the conclusion is vacuous. (d) Baire class one is a statement about POINTWISE limits; it gives no uniform convergence, and the limit functions f_n constructed in the proof are not monotone in n. (e) The converse is false and is not being claimed: plenty of Baire class one functions on a product are not separately continuous.
X is a metric space
Y is a topological space (metric suffices, and is the usual case)
f: X x Y -> R is separately continuous: continuous in each variable with the other held fixed
for the residual-set-of-continuity-points consequence, X x Y is a Baire space (e.g. X, Y complete metric)
values are real (or in a metric space in which the partition-of-unity averaging makes sense, e.g. a locally convex space)

Work as d->infinity with integers N=N(d)->infinity and M=M(d)>=1. Let (X_d,nu_d) and (Omega_d,tau_d) be probability spaces and sigma_d in L2(nu_d times tau_d). Use its singular expansion sigma_d(x,theta)=sum_j sqrt(mu_j) psi_j(x) phi_j(theta), with ordered nonnegative mu_j, sum_j mu_j<infinity, positive mu_(M+1) and positive denominators in the displayed tail conditions, and orthonormal families psi_j in L2(nu_d), phi_j in L2(tau_d). Let D_d be the closed span of the psi_j and P_<=M its orthogonal projection onto the first M modes. Define the feature kernel U_d(theta,thetaprime)=E_x~nu_d sigma_d(x,theta)sigma_d(x,thetaprime), its spectral tail U_>r=sum_(j>r) mu_j phi_j phi_j^T, and kappa_r=sum_(j>r)mu_j>0 for each cutoff used. Draw theta_1,...,theta_N independently from tau_d and let K_ij=U_d(theta_i,theta_j). All stochastic rates below are as d->infinity. (H) There is one sequence u(d)>=M(d) such that, for every fixed real q>=1, all g in span{phi_1,...,phi_u} satisfy ||g||_(L2q(tau_d))<=C_q||g||_(L2(tau_d)), with C_q independent of d and g. (E) For the same u there is a fixed delta_E>0 such that N^(2+delta_E)<=kappa_u^2/sum_(j>u)mu_j^2 eventually. (Sa) There is a fixed delta_a>0 with N^(1+delta_a)<=kappa_M/mu_(M+1) eventually. With Lambda=diag(U_>M(theta_i,theta_i)/kappa_M), Proposition2 gives K>=kappa_M(Lambda+Delta) in positive-semidefinite order, where Delta is symmetric and E||Delta||_op=O(N^(-delta_prime)) for some fixed delta_prime>0. If in addition (Dlower) For every epsilon>0, min_i U_>M(theta_i,theta_i)/kappa_M=Omega_P(N^(-epsilon)), where Omega_P means that the reciprocal divided by N^epsilon is stochastically bounded. then K is invertible with probability tending to1 and kappa_M||K^(-1)||_op=O_P(N^epsilon) for every fixed epsilon>0. The diagonal lower condition is required for this inverse-control conclusion, not for the preceding PSD inequality.

Let (X, Y) be a jointly Gaussian random vector in R^a x R^b with means mu_X, mu_Y and covariance blocks A = Cov(X), B = Cov(X, Y), C = Cov(Y), so its covariance matrix is M = [[A, B], [B^T, C]], possibly singular; A^+ is the Moore-Penrose inverse, and a value x is compatible when x - mu_X lies in the range of A (the support of X). For every compatible x, the support of the conditional law of Y given X = x is an affine subspace of dimension rank K = rank M - rank A, where K = C - B^T A^+ B; it does not depend on x.

With rare total mass epsilon=n^-6, the paired atoms a=+/-nt, b=n^2 t^2/2, w=n^2 t u cancel pointwise. Main mass q=1-epsilon has w=0, a=A, b=A^2/2 and A_prime=(1-q A exp(A^2/2))exp(A^2/2)/2. On [0,1/8], A<=2/31, main action B=q(1+A^2)A_prime^2>1/10, loss dissipation is 2B, and rare action H=n^-4+(1+t^2)n^-2<=69/1024<1/10. Meanwhile E_mu gamma^2=n^-4 t^2 tends to zero and rare absolute coefficient mass is t n^-5 exp(n^2 t^2/2), which diverges. These are RELAXED PATHS, NOT ACTUAL GRADIENT FLOW: the rare w derivative at zero is n^2 u although actual gradient flow requires w_prime=0 when a=0. [Defn 6 of arXiv:2605.25762, 'Brownian Convergence of Planar Domains and Stability of the Planar Skorokhod Embedding Pro'] The Hilbert transform of a real valued $2\pi$- periodic function
$f$ is defined by 
\[
H\{f\}(x):=PV\left\{ \frac{1}{2\pi}\int^{\pi}_{-\pi}f(x-t)\cot(\frac{t}{2})dt\right\} =\lim_{\eta\rightarrow0}\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\eta\leq|t|\leq\pi}f(x-t)\cot(\frac{t}{2})dt
\]
where $PV$ denotes the Cauchy principal value. The Hilbert transform
does exist a.e whenever $p\geq1$. However, it is a bounded operator
on $L^{p}_{2\pi}$ only when $p>1$. The case $p=1$ is irregular,
and $H$ becomes unbounded. For all proofs and properties of the Hilbert
transform, we refer the reader to \cite{butzer1971hilbert,king2009hilbert}.

Let lambda be the security parameter and let lambda<=n(lambda)<=poly(lambda). Start with a binary secret-key zero-bit PRC: polynomial-time KeyGen, randomized Enc and Dec, uniformly negligible false acceptance of every fixed key-independent input, and computational indistinguishability against probabilistic polynomial-time oracle adversaries of fresh encodings under one fixed key from fresh independent uniform n-bit strings. There exist absolute constants C0,Crob>=1 such that the following holds. Fix0<p0<1/(10*Crob), and assume the base code is robust to every(1/2-p0)-substitution-bounded channel: for each randomized channel C satisfying d_H(x,C(x))<=(1/2-p0)*n almost surely for every x, decoding the corrupted fresh encoding accepts except with negligible probability in lambda, averaged over key, encoder, channel and decoder coins. Fix an integer rho>=C0/p0. Put q=rho*n and m=ceil(n*ln2). The new secret key is(k,psi), where k is the base key and psi:[q]->[n] is an independent uniform map with exactly rho preimages per label. To encode, draw b from the base encoder, draw U uniformly from[n]^m, and let S0={i:b_i=1},S1=Unique(U). If |S0 minus S1|>=|S1 minus S0|, choose a uniform injection from S1 minus S0 into S0 minus S1 and relabel its domain in U by its image. Otherwise choose a uniform injection tau:S0 minus S1->S1 minus S0 and replace each occurrence of tau(a) by a. Call the result Y, and independently lift each Y_j to a uniform Z_j in psi^{-1}(Y_j). Decode any received q-ary word w by applying the base decoder to the binary occupancy vector D_psi(w), whose ith bit is1 iff some symbol of w maps to i. This is a zero-bit PRC on[q] with block length m<=n. It is robust to every polynomial-time sampleable channel E that, for every input x, changes x by a total of at most(1-Crob*p0)*|x| insertions, deletions and substitutions almost surely. The channel receives the input word, not the secret balanced map. This is the zero-bit, fixed integer-rho implementation of Theorem4.1.
Binary secret-key zero-bit PRC with repeated-encoding oracle security, soundness and the stated substitution robustness; lambda<=n<=poly(lambda).
Fixed p0>0 below1/(10*Crob); fixed integer rho>=C0/p0. All fresh encoder and lift coins are independent.
Uniform balanced psi is secret and independent of the base key. Edit channels are efficiently sampleable and see the word alone.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.01996, 'Baumslag--Solitar Subgroups Obstruct Model Companions for Fields with Group Actions'] Let \(\pi:\Gamma\twoheadrightarrow Q\) be a surjective group homomorphism and let \(K\) be a \(Q\)-field.
  Let \(K_\pi\) denote the \(\Gamma\)-field with the same underlying field and action
  \[
    \gamma\cdot a:=\pi(\gamma)(a).
  \]
  Then:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item \(K\) is \(\aleph_0\)-saturated as a \(Q\)-field if and only if \(K_\pi\) is \(\aleph_0\)-saturated as a \(\Gamma\)-field;
    \item \(K\) is p.e.c. as a \(Q\)-field if and only if \(K_\pi\) is existentially closed in every regular \(\Gamma\)-field extension of \(K_\pi\) on which \(\ker(\pi)\) acts trivially.
  \end{enumerate}

[Definition 21 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Given an equilibrium measure $\boldsymbol{\mu}$, we will use the following terminology for each $h \in [H]$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[$\bullet$] A \emph{void} is a maximal (for the inclusion) and closed interval in $[\hat{a}'_h,\hat{b}'_h]$ where
$\mu_h(x) =0$.
\item[$\bullet$] A \emph{saturation} is a maximal closed interval in
$[\hat{a}'_h,\hat{b}'_h]$ where $\mu_h(x) = \frac{1}{\theta_{h,h}}$.
\item[$\bullet$] A \emph{band} is a maximal open interval in $[\hat a'_h,\hat b'_h]$ where $0<\mu_h(x)<\frac{1}{\theta_{h,h}}$.
\end{itemize}
We denote by $\amsmathbb{V}_{h}$ (respectively $\amsmathbb{S}_{h}$, $\amsmathbb{B}_{h}$) the union of voids (respectively saturations, bands) in $[\hat{a}'_{h},\hat{b}'_{h}]$. If we speak of a \emph{saturated segment} (respectively, a \emph{void segment}), we mean a segment included in a saturation (respectively, in a void) but not necessarily maximal.

For a finite free zero-field Potts graph with N vertices and integer q>=3, let S=sum_v(1{sigma_v=1}-1/q), H_j=sum_FK_components |C|^j, c2=(q-1)/q^2 and c4=(q-1)(q^2-6q+6)/q^4. Independent uniform cluster colors conditional on FK give kappa4(S)=c4*E H4+3*c2^2*Var(H2). At q=3 the omitted mixture term is (4/27)*Var(H2). For P(h)=N^-1 log E exp(hS), chi=P''(0)>0 and local Legendre I, I'''(0)=-P'''(0)/chi^3 and I''''(0)=3*(P'''(0))^2/chi^5-P''''(0)/chi^4. P'''(0)>0 alone does not provide a uniform magnetization cubic. Passing to criticality requires controlled ratios and a remainder on a fixed magnetization interval. The corresponding actual-lattice potential input is unproved.

AUTHOR-CHECKED FULL CANDIDATE, not an independently audited solution: for compactly supported initial probability laws with support diameter D>0, the strict Cauchy-profile minimum bound rules out more than two roots at every level 1/t<=1/D^2. The sufficient Hasebe-Ueda Lemma 3.1 was checked in the cached primary text with semicircle variance t and yields the candidate conclusion of unimodality for t>=D^2. A point mass handles D=0. The symmetric endpoint law fails just below D^2, giving candidate sharp constant C=1. Independent blind KEEP, full proof check, and literature novelty remain outstanding.

body:
In the spiked covariance model with noise level $\sigma^2$ and ratio $\gamma = p/n$, let $\hat\lambda$ be a sample eigenvalue lying above the bulk edge, $\ell := \hat\lambda / \sigma^2 > (1 + \sqrt{\gamma})^2$. Then the unique $\theta > \sqrt{\gamma}$ with $(1 + \theta)(1 + \gamma/\theta) = \ell$ is $$\hat\theta = \tfrac{1}{2}\Big( (\ell - 1 - \gamma) + \sqrt{(\ell - 1 - \gamma)^2 - 4\gamma} \Big),$$ and $\sigma^2 (1 + \hat\theta)$ is the consistent estimate of the population eigenvalue behind $\hat\lambda$. The discriminant is nonnegative exactly when $\ell \ge (1 + \sqrt{\gamma})^2$, so the formula is defined precisely for eigenvalues at or above the edge. The population value $\sigma^2(1 + \hat\theta)$ is always strictly less than $\hat\lambda$ (a sample spike is debiased downward), by the amount $\sigma^2 \gamma (1 + 1/\hat\theta)$.
the spiked covariance model with a detected spike, i.e. a sample eigenvalue above the Marchenko-Pastur edge
gamma = p/n in (0, 1]

[Theorem contracted of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $\mathcal{E} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{X}$ is a smooth irreducible Cartier divisor, where $\mathcal{X}$ is a smooth, separated Deligne--Mumford stack of dimension $n > 1$.
    Suppose also that there exists a contraction $\pi : \mathcal{X} \to Z$ to a smooth irreducible variety of dimension $n$ such that $\pi(\mathcal{E}) = p \in Z$ and $\pi : \mathcal{X} \setminus \mathcal{E} \xrightarrow{\sim} Z \setminus p$ is an isomorphism. 
    Then, $\mathcal{E}$ is algebraically simply-connected, i.e., $\pi_1^{\text{\'et}}(\mathcal{E}) \simeq 1$.

DRAFT author-derived material; independent review pending; no novelty or parent-solved claim. For N independent fair signs, let S=a_N sum_{i=1}^N sigma_i with a_N>0. Its MGF is cosh(a_N h)^N, variance V=N a_N^2, and first imaginary zero y_1=pi/(2a_N). Thus r=sqrt(V)y_1=pi sqrt(N)/2, while 3-E(S/sqrt(V))^4=2/N and S/sqrt(V) converges to N(0,1). Choosing a_N=N makes y_1 tend to zero even though normalized zeros escape and the limit is Gaussian. This refutes the generic inference from axis location or raw zero collapse to non-Gaussian scaling. It is not a counterexample to critical nearest-neighbor 3D Ising.

S is a metric space

Define h(D)=N^(-1) sum_i ell_i(b_i+(<G_ij,D>)_(j=1..K)), where each ell_i:R^K->R is convex, nonnegative and twice continuously differentiable. This is the exact affine/NTK model, not an error bound for a nonlinear network. Let lambda>=0 and suppose h(D)+lambda||D||_* has a global minimizer. Let r>=1 satisfy r(r+1)/2>KN. For U in R^(m by r), V in R^(n by r), Q=[U;V], and P in S_+^(m+n), set F_P(U,V)=h(UV^T)+(lambda/2)(||U||_F^2+||V||_F^2)+<P,QQ^T>. The same almost-sure conclusion holds for any perturbation law absolutely continuous with respect to that measure, including laws supported in an arbitrarily small PSD ball. The conclusion does not cover deterministic P=0, a measure supported on a lower-dimensional face, or finite-iteration convergence of GD.

[Defn contFV of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] For $\alpha>0$, an \emph{$\alpha$-good potential} is a
    function $V:\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$,  $(h,\varphi)\mapsto V_h(\varphi)$ 
    which is twice continuously differentiable 
    
    with 
    \[
        \sup_{\substack{|h|\le C \\ \varphi\in\mathbb{R}}}
        \left| \frac\partial{\partial h} V_h'(\varphi)\right| < \infty
    \]
    for all $C>0$ and $V_h''(\varphi)\in[\alpha,\alpha^{-1}]$
    for all $h,\varphi\in\mathbb{R}$ (where  $V_h'$ and $V_h''$ are the first and
     second  derivatives of $V_h$ with respect to $\varphi$). In other words, this family of potential
    functions is smooth and uniformly strongly convex with Lipschitz
    gradient, and furthermore $V_h'$ is Lipschitz in $h$. For
    $\text{\boldmath $h$}\in\mathbb{R}^N$, we define the potential

    \begin{align*}
V_\text{\boldmath $h$}(\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}):=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{h_i}(\varphi_i)\, .
\end{align*}

    Given an $\alpha$-good potential $V$ and
    a weighted graph $G=(\text{\boldmath $B$},\text{\boldmath $h$})$ on $[N]$ with $\text{\boldmath $B$}\succ-\alpha\text{\boldmath $I$}$,
    we consider the Gibbs measure on $\mathbb{R}^N$ with base measure
    $e^{-V_\text{\boldmath $h$}(\text{\boldmath $\varphi$})}{\rm d}\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}$ and quadratic Hamiltonian
    $-\frac12\<\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}, \text{\boldmath $B$}\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}\>$ and denote its free energy density
    by

    \begin{align*}
F_V(G)=F_V(\text{\boldmath $B$},\text{\boldmath $h$})=\frac1N \log \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \exp\left( -\frac12
\<\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}, \text{\boldmath $B$}\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}\> \right) e^{-V_\text{\boldmath $h$}(\text{\boldmath $\varphi$})} {\rm d}\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}.
\end{align*}

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma app-L-1 of arXiv:2608.30548, 'Finite speed of propagation and waiting time phenomena for stochastic porous media equatio'] Let $ 1 \le r \le \infty$, $0< q <p$, $ m \in \mathbb{N}_+$
such that
\[
\frac 1r - \frac mN < \frac 1p \,.
\]
If $\mathcal{O} \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is bounded with piecewise smooth boundary,
then positive constants $c_1$ and $ c_2$ depending only on $\mathcal{O},
r, p, m$ and $q$ exist such that for any $u \in L^q (\mathcal{O})$
satisfying $ D^m u \in L^r (\mathcal{O})$, the following inequality holds:
\begin{equation}
\| u \|_p \le c_1 \|D^m u\|^a_r \| u \|^{1-a}_q + c_2 \| u \|_q

\end{equation}
where $a = \frac{\frac 1q - \frac 1p}{\frac 1q + \frac m N - \frac
1r}$.

Especially, if $\mathcal{O}=\mathbb{R}^N$,  then ((eq-GN of the paper)) holds
with constant $c_1=c(r,p,m,q)$ and $c_2=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma app-L-1 of arXiv:2608.30548

[Theoremb 2 (Positive-time heat-flow Schur convexity) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $1\le p<2$ and $t>0$. The map
\[
 \theta\mapsto \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(\theta)
\]
is strictly Schur-convex as a function of $s(\theta)$. In particular, with
\[
 \diag=\frac1{\sqrt n}(1,\ldots,1),
\]
one has
\[
 \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(\diag)
 \le \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(\theta)
 \le \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(e_1),
 \qquad \theta\in\sphere,
\]
with equality only for the corresponding signed-permutation orbits. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

d\in\mathfrak D_{\xi,n}^{\mathrm{osc}}\), and set \(m=m_{\xi,d}\). Let
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{pre}}(d)
=
\left\{
(\ell,I,J):
0\le \ell<m,\ 
I\in\mathcal D_\ell^\circ,\ 
J\in\mathcal D_{\ell+1}^\circ,\ 
J\subset I
\right\},
\]
and choose a deterministic ordering \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{pre}}(d)=\{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_N\}\), by increasing generation, with any deterministic order within each generation, where \(\gamma_r=(\ell_r,I_r,J_r)\). With respect to the filtration \((\mathcal H_r^{\mathrm{pre}})\) generated by revealing the variables \(U_{J_r}\) in this order,
\[
S_r^{\mathrm{pre}}
:=
\sum_{q=1}^r
\mathbf 1_{\{\tau_n>\ell_q\}}
X_{J_q,n}^{\mathrm{cap}}(\xi,d,\ell_q),
\qquad
0\le r\le N,
\]
is a complex-valued martingale and \(S_N^{\mathrm{pre}}=\widehat F^{\mathrm{pre,cap}}_{\xi,d,n}\).

Moreover, for every \(L>m\), an analogous deterministic ordering of
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{post}}(d,L)
=
\left\{
(\ell,I,J):
m\le \ell<L,\ 
I\in\mathcal D_\ell^\circ,\ 
J\in\mathcal D_{\ell+1}^\circ,\ 
J\subset I
\right\}
\]
produces a complex-valued martingale whose terminal value is \(\widehat F^{\mathrm{post,cap}}_{\xi,d,n,L}\).

[Teo 9 of arXiv:2608.02103, '$p$-Adic Diffusion and Random Walks on $[0,1]$'] There exists a probability measure $p_t(x,\cdot)$, $t\geq 0$, with $x\in [0,1] $, on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $[0,1]$, such that the Cauchy problem (\ref{CauchyProblem}) has a unique solution of the form 
\[u(x,t)=\int_0^1 u_0(y)p_t(x,dy).\]
In addition, $p_t(x,\cdot)$ is the transition distribution of a strong Markov process, whose paths are right-continuous and have no discontinuities other than jumps.

body:
Small raw drift of derivative-power Loewner probes does not identify a Brownian variance if their positive exponents tend to zero. With deterministic driver W=0 and alpha_n=1/n, on a local interval with bounded derivative jets and h-prime bounded away from zero, (h-prime)^alpha_n tends uniformly to 1. For slit probes (x,s)=(1,1),(-1,1),(1,3), the initial raw relative drifts are alpha_n times (9/8,9/8,33/32), yet the variance rate is zero. At n=128 the maximum raw drift is 9/1024<1/100, while division by alpha_n leaves 9/8. Require a fixed positive common limiting exponent or exponent-normalized error control. Author-derived obstruction; independent review pending.

[Theorem 8 (Gaussian partial coloring relative to a subspace) of arXiv:2606.16005, '\bfseries An Algebraic Matrix Spencer Theorem'] There are absolute constants \(c,\eta,C>0\) with the following property. Let
\(H\subseteq\mathbb R^s\) be a linear subspace satisfying $\dim H\ge (1-\eta)s$, and let \(K\subseteq H\) be a symmetric convex set satisfying $\gamma_H(K)\ge \exp(-\eta s)$.
Then for every \(y\in(-1,1)^s\), there exists an increment \(x\in CK\) such that $y+x\in[-1,1]^s$ and $|\{i\in[s]: |y_i+x_i|=1\}|\ge cs.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:ergo of arXiv:2505.14012, 'Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations'] \phantom{ }
\begin{enumerate}
\item An invariant measure $\mu\in{\mathcal M}_1(H)$ for the semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ is called \emph{ergodic} if
\[Q_T(v,\cdot) \rightharpoonup \mu\]
as $T\to\infty$ for any $v\in H$ in the sense of weak convergence of probability measures.
\item An invariant measure $\mu\in{\mathcal M}_1(H)$ for the semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ is called \emph{strongly mixing} if
\[P_t(v,\cdot)\rightharpoonup \mu\]
as $t\to\infty$ for any $v\in H$ in the sense of weak convergence of probability measures.
\item An invariant measure $\mu\in{\mathcal M}_1(H)$ for the semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ is called \emph{exponentially ergodic} if there exists $\beta>0$ and a positive function $c:H\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for any $\varphi\in\operatorname{Lip}_b(H)$, all $t>0$, and all $v\in H$,
\[\left|P_t\varphi(v)-\int_H\varphi(z)\,\mu(dz)\right|\le c(v)e^{-\beta t}\operatorname{Lip}(\varphi).\]
\item An invariant measure $\mu\in{\mathcal M}_1(H)$ for the semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ is called \emph{exponentially mixing} if there exists $\beta>0$ and a positive function $c:H\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for all $t>0$, and all $v\in H$,
\[\|P_t(v,\cdot)-\mu\|_{F-M}\le c(v)e^{-\beta t},\]
where
\[\|\nu\|_{F-M}:=\sup\left\{\left|\int_H\varphi(z)\,\nu(dz)\right|\;\colon\;\varphi\in \operatorname{Lip}_b(H),\;\|\varphi\|_{\operatorname{Lip}_b}\le 1\right\}\]
is the \emph{Forter-Mourier norm} (also called \emph{bounded Lipschitz norm}) of a signed measure $\nu$ on ${\mathcal B}(H)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Ergodicity and mixing

[Lemma lem_collision of arXiv:2608.15344, 'A Harris recurrent continuous-time Markov process without wide-sense regenerative structur'] Let $Y$ be an $\mathcal{S}$-valued random variable, and let
\[
U=(U_1,\dots,U_N)
\]
be a random sequence of vertices in $\mathcal{V}$, where $N<\infty$ almost surely.
Conditional on $Y$, let $U^{(1)}$ and $U^{(2)}$ be independent copies of $U$. Suppose that\[
P(v\text{ occurs in }U)=0
\]
for every fixed $v\in\mathcal{V}$. If $Z$ is a $\mathcal{V}$-valued random variable independent of $Y$, then
\[
P(Z\text{ occurs in both }U^{(1)}\text{ and }U^{(2)})=0.
\]
No independence between $Z$ and the two sequences is required.

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.31008, 'Stability of gravitational instantons with a bounded Killing vector field'] On a Ricci-flat four-manifold, we have
\begin{align}
 dF=0,\qquad\delta F&=0,\quad \text{ and } \quad\iota_KF=-dV,\\
 \nabla^2V&=\frac12F\circ F-2\Rm(\,\cdot\,,K,\,\cdot\,,K),
 \\
 \Delta V&=-|F|^2,
 \\
 \cE_g(\kappa\otimes\kappa)&=\nabla^2V-F\circ F,
 
\end{align}
and for every smooth function $f$, we find
\begin{equation}
 \cE_g(\nabla^2f)=\nabla^2(\Delta f),\qquad
 \cE_g(fg)=(\Delta f)g.
\end{equation}

[Lemma gammaR of arXiv:2411.06838, 'Generalized Wasserstein Barycenters'] Let $(\eta_k)_{k\in \mathbb{N}}$ and $\eta$ be Borel probability measures on $X=(\mathcal{P}_2(H),W_2)$, such that $\eta_k \to \eta$ narrowly and
\begin{equation}

	\lim_{k\to \infty} \int_{X}m_2^2(\nu)\,{\rm d}\eta_k(\nu) = \int_{X}m_2^2(\nu)\,{\rm d}\eta(\nu) < \infty.
\end{equation}
Then, for all $(\mu_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $\mu$ in $\mathcal{P}_2(H)$ such that $\mu_k \to \mu$ with respect to the weak topology of $P_2^w(H)$,
\[
	\lim_{k \to \infty} \int_X \mathcal{R}(\nu,\mu_k){\rm d}\eta_k(\nu) = \int_X \mathcal{R}(\nu,\mu){\rm d}\eta(\nu).
\]

body: In mathematics, the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means, or more briefly the AM–GM inequality, states that the arithmetic mean of a list of non-negative real numbers is greater than or equal to the geometric mean of the same list; and further, that the two means are equal if and only if every number in the list is the same.
title: AM–GM inequality

[Thm 14 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] Suppose that \(\beta, W\) and $\theta_k$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{assumption12}. Then, for every
\(m\geq1\) and every
\(\bm x_1,\ldots,\bm x_m\in\mathbb R^n\), the conditional law of
\(
    \bigl(
        \mathcal P_k^a(\bm x_1),\ldots,
        \mathcal P_k^a(\bm x_m)
    \bigr)
\)
given \(A_k\) converges weakly in probability to
\(\mathcal N_m(\boldsymbol 0,\bm K)\), where
\[
    \bm K_{bc}
    =
    K_{\beta,a}(\bm x_b,\bm x_c),
    \qquad 1\leq b,c\leq m.
\]
Consequently, the unconditional finite-dimensional distributions of
\(\mathcal P_k^a\) converge to those of the centered Gaussian
process with covariance kernel \(K_{\beta,a}\). In particular, for
every \(\bm x\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
    \mathcal P_k^a(\bm x)
    \xrightarrow{d}
    \mathcal N\left(
        0,
        \operatorname{Var} 
            a(\bm Z^\top\bm x)
        +
        q_\beta
            \mathbb E^2
                a(\bm Z^\top\bm x)
    \right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:heavy-parent-children of arXiv:2608.26707, 'An Exponential Lower Bound for the Permanent\\of Random Bernoulli Matrix'] Fix $0\leq k<n$, condition on $\mathcal{F}_k$, and let $A\in\binom{[n]}{k}$ be $\lambda$-heavy.
Let $I\subseteq[n]\setminus A$.
After exposing row $k+1$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbb{P}\!\left(
   \text{no }A\cup\{i\},\ i\in I,
   \text{ is }\lambda\text{-heavy}
   \,\middle|\,\mathcal{F}_k
 \right)
 &\leq2^{-\left\lvert I\right\rvert},
 \\
 \mathbb{P}\!\left(
   \#\set{i\in I:A\cup\{i\}
        \text{ is }\lambda\text{-heavy}}<\frac{\left\lvert I\right\rvert}{3}
   \,\middle|\,\mathcal{F}_k
 \right)
 &\leq e^{-\left\lvert I\right\rvert/18}.
 
\end{align}

[Theorem 19 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $\emptyset\ne \Omega \subset \RR^d$ be an open and bounded subset.
  Let $A_1,A_2\in \{B,F\}$.
  Let $s_1,s_2\in \RR$ and let $0<p_1,q_1,p_2,q_2 \le \infty$ (with $p_i<\infty$ if $A_i=F$).
  Assume that 
  \begin{equation*}
     s_1 > s_2 
     \quad \text{and} \quad
      s_1 - \frac{d}{p_1} > s_2 -\frac{d}{p_2}.
  \end{equation*}
  Let $\SC$ denote the unit ball of $(A_1)^{s_1}_{p_1,q_1}(\Omega)$
  and let $\XX = (A_2)^{s_2}_{p_2,q_2}(\Omega)$,
  endowed with the \mbox{(quasi-)}\allowbreak metric induced by
  $\norm{\cdot\mid (A_2)^{s_2}_{p_2,q_2}(\Omega)}$.
  Then $\md(\SC) = \frac{d}{s_1-s_2}$ and there exists a Borel probability measure on
  $\XX$ that is critical for $\SC$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 19 of arXiv:2608.30549

[Lemma lem:cauchy-positive of arXiv:2605.26688, 'Absolute moment inequalities under quadratic-form positivity'] Let \(D\in\mathcal B(\mathbb{R})\), let \(\mu\) be a measure on \(\mathcal B(D)\), let \(c:D\to(0,\infty)\) be measurable, and let \(\eta:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be measurable. If
\[
   \iint_{D^2}\frac{\left\lvert \eta(x)\eta(y)\right\rvert}{c(x)+c(y)}\mu(\,\mathrm{d} x)\mu(\,\mathrm{d} y)<\infty,
\]
then
\[
   \iint_{D^2}\frac{\eta(x)\eta(y)}{c(x)+c(y)}\mu(\,\mathrm{d} x)\mu(\,\mathrm{d} y)\ge0.
\]

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2605.09372, 'Sharp weighted norm estimates for martingale square functions'] The functions $\{\gamma(n,m)\}_{n,m\in \mathbb N}$
satisfy the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
\item For every $n,m\in \mathbb N$,  $\gamma(n,m)$ is adapted to $\mathcal F_{n\vee m}$.

\item For every $n\in\mathbb N$, there exists a constant $C_\gamma$ such that for every   $A\in\mathcal F_n$,
		$$\mathbb P\Big(A\cap\{\sup_{m>n}\gamma(n,m)>C_\gamma\}\Big)\leq\mathbb P\Big(A\cap\{\sup_{m>n}\gamma(n,m)\leq C_\gamma\}\Big). $$
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma 9 of arXiv:2605.09372

body:
[Lemma lem:cole-hopf-plateau of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Let $0\le s<t\le1$, assume $\zeta((s,t))=0$, and set $\alpha:=\zeta([0,s])$.  Then
		\[
		U(r,x):=\exp\{\alpha\Phi_\zeta(r,x)\}
		\]
		solves the backward heat equation on $[s,t]$,
		\[
		\partial_r U(r,x)+\frac12\xi''(r)\partial_{xx}U(r,x)=0 .
		\]
		Hence, with
		\[
		p^{\mathrm{BM}}_{s,t}(x,y)
		:=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi(\xi'(t)-\xi'(s))}}
		\exp\left\{-\frac{(y-x)^2}{2(\xi'(t)-\xi'(s))}\right\},
		\]
		we have
		\begin{equation}
			e^{\alpha\Phi_\zeta(s,x)}
			=\int_\mathbb{R} e^{\alpha\Phi_\zeta(t,y)}p^{\mathrm{BM}}_{s,t}(x,y)\,\mathrm{d} y .
		\end{equation}
		Equivalently, conditionally on $X_s=x$, the transition density of the Auffinger--Chen process on the plateau is
		\begin{equation}
			p_{s,t}(x,y)
			=\frac{e^{\alpha\Phi_\zeta(t,y)}}{e^{\alpha\Phi_\zeta(s,x)}}
			p^{\mathrm{BM}}_{s,t}(x,y).
		\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cole--Hopf identity on a plateau

[Proposition eq:Wulff-def of arXiv:2605.15545, 'Crossover from subcritical to critical decay: \\ random walk, self-avoiding walk, percolat'] Let $d\ge 1$.
Suppose that Assumptions~(ass:Omega of the paper) and~(ass:J of the paper)
hold, but without requiring that $h^{(\mu)},J^{(\mu)}$ satisfy
(equation eq:Q_d-1 of the paper).
For nonzero $x \in {\mathbb R^d}$,
define its \emph{surface tension} by $\sigma(x) = m_S  \abs x_S
= \mu_{\hat x} \cdot x $.
Then the \emph{Wulff shape} for $\sigma(x)$, defined by
\begin{equation}

\mathcal{W}
= \bigl\{ \mu \in {\mathbb R^d}    :     \mu \cdot x \le  \sigma(x)
	\text{ for all nonzero } x\in {\mathbb R^d}   \bigr\} ,
\end{equation}
coincides with $\overline \Omega$.

For real factors B of size m-by-r and A of size r-by-p, and differentiable product loss F(BA), put G_B=grad F(BA) A^T, G_A=B^T grad F(BA), and D=AA^T-B^TB. Simultaneous factor gradient descent with step eta has the exact identity D_next-D=eta^2(G_A G_A^T-G_B^T G_B); the first-order terms cancel. Thus ||D_next-D||F<=eta^2(||G_A||F^2+||G_B||F^2). If a fixed eta>0 additionally satisfies the sufficient-decrease inequality f_next<=f-a eta ||grad f||F^2 for f(B,A)=F(BA), some a>0, and f is bounded below by f_star along the iterates, summation gives ||D_t-D_0||F<=(eta/a)(f_0-f_star). This implication assumes descent; it does not establish it or prove arbitrary-step convergence. The trace identity (||B||F^2+||A||F^2)^2<=r[||AA^T-B^TB||F^2+4||BA||F^2] then converts bounds on imbalance and product into a factor bound. Du-Hu-Lee, Algorithmic Regularization in Learning Deep Homogeneous Models: Layers are Automatically Balanced, arXiv:1806.00900, Theorem 2.2 gives continuous-time Gram invariance; Appendix B, Claim B.1 expands the discrete square-loss update. The conditional constant-step summation and trace inequality here are elementary method consequences, not their full GD convergence theorem. Their Theorem 3.1 instead uses small Gaussian initialization of both factors and decreasing steps.
Real compatible factors; differentiable loss depending only on the product
Constant-step summation is conditional on the stated sufficient decrease and lower bound

body: For independent Bernoulli bond percolation with common parameter p, the conditional probability that an edge is open given all other edge states equals p almost surely. Hence the strict finite-energy hypothesis 0<P(edge open | other edges)<1 holds exactly for 0<p<1. At p=0 or p=1 that hypothesis fails; uniqueness conclusions at those endpoints can be checked directly. This corrects the application sentence that all Burton-Keane hypotheses hold for every p, without refuting its interior-parameter uniqueness conclusion. Correction draft: independent review pending.
title: Bernoulli finite energy requires an interior parameter

[Theorem 29 (Geometric estimates from initial data) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] \bse
Fix an admissible Navier--Stokes triple $(\mathscr F,\chi,\mathscr B)$ as defined in \autoref{def-pot-admissible-triple}.
Let $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ with $\Phi=(\Jperp,\Jpar,\Pbb,\Qbb)$ and $\Psi=(\ell,\log\Omega,\Kpar)$ be a sufficiently regular dissipated-energy or particle-production Einstein--Navier--Stokes areal flow $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ on $[t_0,t_1]\times\Tbb^3$.  Denote the values at time $t=t_0$ by
\be
(\mathring\Phi,\mathring\Psi,\mathring\zeta) \coloneqq (\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)(t_0,\cdot) \quad \text{on } \Tbb^3 .
\ee
Then the following estimates hold, where implied constants depend on the Navier--Stokes potential $\chi$ and on $t_0,t_1$, but not on the relaxation structure~$\mathscr B$ nor on the solution $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$.
\bei
\item \emph{Spatial energy.} The fluid variables, and the first-order geometric variables $\Pbb,\Qbb$ have
  \bel{estimate-SE}
    \int_{\{t\}\times \Tbb^3} \Bigl( T_\chi^{00} + \Ebf_0(\Pbb,\Qbb) \Bigr) \dVtrois
    \lesssim \|\mathring\Phi\|_{\mathrm{energy}} , \qquad t\in[t_0,t_1] .
  \ee

\item \emph{Conformal length and volume.}
  \bel{estimate-LV}
  \aligned
  & \mathcal L(t) \leq \mathcal L(t_0) , \quad \mathcal V(t) \leq |t/t_0|^{3/4} \mathcal V(t_0) , \qquad t_0 \leq t \leq t_1 < 0 \quad \text{(future-contracting regime)},
  \\
  & \mathcal L(t) \geq \mathcal L(t_0) , \quad \mathcal V(t) \geq |t/t_0|^{3/4} \mathcal V(t_0) , \qquad 0 < t_0 \leq t \leq t_1 \quad \text{(future-expanding regime)}.
  \endaligned
  \ee
  Furthermore, the minimum conformal length $\mathcal L_{\min}=\min_{t\in[t_0,t_1]} \mathcal L(t)\geq 0$ is reached at $t=t_1$ in the future-contracting regime and at $t=t_0$ in the future-expanding regime.
\eei
In the future-contracting regime, subsequent estimates require the assumption that $\mathcal L_{\min}>0$ and depend on $1/\mathcal L_{\min}$, which is \emph{not bounded} by the initial data.  In the future-expanding regime $\mathcal L_{\min}>0$ is part of the initial data.
The constants $C_1,C_2,\dots$ below depend on $\mathcal L_{\min}$ and on the finite-energy and bounded-variation norms of initial data.
\bei
\item \emph{Both-sided bounds on conformal length and volume.}
  \bel{both-sided-LV}
  (C_1)^{-1} \leq \mathcal L(t) \leq C_1 , \qquad (C_2)^{-1} \leq \mathcal V(t) \leq C_2 .
  \ee

\item \emph{Bounded variation in space.} The lapse, twist and conformal length measure satisfy
  \bel{spatial-bv}
    \|\ell\|_{\BVac(0,1)} + \|(\log\Omega,\Kpar)\|_{\BVac(\Tbb^3)}
    \leq C_3 , \qquad t \in [t_0,t_1] .
  \ee

\item \emph{Temporal integrals.} The (not necessarily positive) spatial stress~$T_\chi^{11}$ admits integrals on constant-$x$ slices
\bel{temporal-stress}
\biggl| \int_{[t_0,t_1]\times\Tbb^2} \Bigl( T_\chi^{11} + E_0(\Pbb,\Qbb) \Bigr) \dVundeux \biggr|
\leq C_4 , \quad x\in\Sbb^1 .
\ee
\eei
Assume further that the potential~$\chi$ is torus-adapted (\autoref{def-NS-torus-adapted}) and the stress-tensor satisfies the \emph{coercive stress condition} (\autoref{def-Tchi-coercive}, below), and assume that the parallel momentum per particle is bounded at initial time in the sense that $2|T_\chi^{02}|+2|T_\chi^{03}|\leq C^\parallel\Numb_\chi^0$ for some constant~$C^\parallel>0$.
Then \eqref{temporal-stress} are completed to an $L^2$~control of the whole fluid momentum~$\Jbb$ along timelike slices, and the following estimates are satisfied.
\bei
\item \emph{Bounded variation in time.} The lapse, twist and conformal length measure satisfy
  \bel{bv-time-bound}
    \|\ell\|_{\BVac(\Interval)} + \|(\log\Omega,\Kpar)\|_{\BVac(\Interval\times\Tbb^2)}
    \leq C_5 , \qquad x \in \Sbb^1 .
  \ee
\eei
Altogether, under the assumed coercive stress condition, the finite-energy and bounded-variation norms \eqref{equa-flow-energy-norm}--\eqref{equa-flow-variation-norm} of the areal flow are bounded by a function of its initial data and, in the future-contracting regime, of~$\mathcal L_{\min}$.
\ese (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Geometric estimates from initial data

[Lemma lem:capture-disjoint-blocks of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Fix integers $B\ge1$ and $K\ge1$, and real $\lambda>2$. Let $r$ be a positive integer and $n_0=\lceil\lambda r\rceil$. Assume
\[
(8\lambda)^{2B}\le K,
\qquad
K\log K\le \frac r2.
\]
Let $J$ be a set of size $n_0$ and assume there are pairwise disjoint subsets
\[
\mathcal W_1,\dots,\mathcal W_K\subseteq J,
\]
each of size at most $B$. If $\Omega\subseteq J$ is chosen uniformly from $\binom Jr$, then
\[
\mathbb P\big(\forall s\in[K]:\mathcal W_s\not\subseteq\Omega\big)
\le
\exp(-\sqrt K).
\]

The condition $K\log K\le r/2$ keeps the sequential exposure of the $K$ blocks from depleting the sample. The condition $(8\lambda)^{2B}\le K$ ensures that the capture probability of one block, repeated $K$ times, gives exponent at least $\sqrt K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Capturing one of many disjoint witness blocks

[Prop upper bound for the giant of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] Let $(X_n)_{n \geq 1}$ be a sequence of $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes with $s_{d-1}(X_n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$. Assume that $X_n$ converges locally weakly in probability to $(X, o) \sim \mu$. Let $\zeta := \mathbb{P} \left( s_{d-1} \left( \mathcal{C}(o) \right) = \infty \right)$, the survival probability of the $d$-dimensional connected component of the root $o$ in $X$. \mathbb{P} \left( s_{d-1} \left( \mathcal{C}_{\max} \right) \leq s_{d-1}(X_n) (\zeta + \epsilon) \right) \to 1
\]

[Corollary 14 (Examples: averaged macroscopic-loop bounds) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item \textbf{Random regular graphs.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the random \(d\)-regular graph on \([n]\), with law \(p_{d,n}\).
    If $d>2c_{\theta,u}$, then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    p_{d,n}\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs.}
    Let \(G_n\sim G(n,\lambda/n)\). If $\lambda>2c_{\theta,u}$,
    then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Simple bounded-degree configuration model.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the simple graph obtained from the configuration model with
    degree sequence \((d_i^{(n)})_{i=1}^n\). Assume that
    \[
    1\le d_i^{(n)}\le \Delta
    \qquad\text{for all }i,n,
    \]
    and $\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^{(n)}\to \rho$. If $\rho>2c_{\theta,u}$,
    then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Examples: averaged macroscopic-loop bounds

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph of degree at most $\Delta$. Assume that Assumption \ref{primaryassumptionpaper} is satisfied for some $p_0\in(0,1)$, then with $\mathbb{P}_h$- probability at least $1-O_{\beta,\Delta,p_0}(\frac{1}{|V|})$ over the external field (here $O_{\beta,\Delta,p_0}$ denotes constants that may depend on $\beta$, $\Delta$ and $p_0$), the spectral gap of RFIM measure $\mu_G$ satisfies
    $$
    \mathbf{gap}_G\geq |V|^{-1}\exp\left(-\frac{16\beta\Delta\ln|V|}{\alpha_*}\right),
    $$
    and the $\epsilon$- mixing time of Glauber dynamics for $\mu_G$ is $$t_{mix}(P,\epsilon)=O\left(|V|^{1+\frac{16\beta\Delta}{\alpha_*}}\left(\beta\Delta|V|+\|h\|_1+\log(1/\epsilon)\right)\right).$$
Here $\|h\|_1:=\sum_{x\in V}|h_x|.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.02002

[Proposition middle terms strategy of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] Let $n$ be even. Then, $I_{\frac{n}{2}}^*=I_{\frac{n}{2}+1}^*=\{n-1,n\}$, i.e. the player should guess card $n-1$ or card $n$ in positions $\frac{n}{2}$ and $\frac{n}{2}+1$. If $n$ is odd, card $n-1$ or card $n$ should be guessed in position $\frac{n+1}{2}$.
    \begin{proof}
        By Proposition $(guessing strategy symmetry of the paper)$ and Lemma $(last two rows are equal of the paper)$, it suffices to show that $n\in I_{\frac{n}{2}}^*$ and $k\notin I_{\frac{n}{2}}^*$ for $k\leq n-2$. We compute 
        \[p_{i,\frac{n}{2}}=\frac{\binom{i-1}{\frac{n}{2}-1}+\binom{i-1}{\frac{n}{2}}}{2^i}=\frac{\binom{i}{\frac{n}{2}}}{2^i}\]
        where the second equality is a consequence of Pascal's identity. Consider the sequence 
        \[a_i=\frac{\binom{i}{\frac{n}{2}}}{2^i}\]
        We note that $a_i=0$ for all $i\leq \frac{n}{2}-1$ and $a_i>0$ for all $i\geq \frac{n}{2}$. Now we examine the ratio of consecutive terms. Canceling factorials, we obtain
        \[R_i:=\frac{a_{i+1}}{a_i}=\frac{i+1}{2(i+1-\frac{n}{2})}\]
        Immediately, we have $R_{n-1}=1$ and $R_{i}<1$ for all $i\leq n-2$. This shows that $a_i$ is strictly increasing for all $\frac{n}{2}\leq i\leq n-1$ with $a_{n-1}=a_{n}$. This implies $a_{n-1}$ and $a_n$ are the unique maxima. But $a_n=p_{n,\frac{n}{2}}$, and the result follows. The construction for odd $n$ is nearly identical.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition middle terms strategy of arXiv:2507.10294

body:
Let d>=2 be an integer, let X=(a,b) have the standard Gaussian law on R^(2d), and let H_d={h_U(a,b)=sign(a^T U b): U in O(d)}. Define rho(h,g)=Pr[h(X)!=g(X)], and let D(H_d,rho,t) be its t-packing number. There is an absolute c>0 such that D(H_d,rho,t)>=(c/t)^(d(d-1)/2). Consequently any learner which, for each h in H_d, achieves disagreement error at most epsilon with probability at least 1-delta from n independent labeled examples must satisfy n >= (d(d-1)/2) log_2(c/(2epsilon)) + log_2(1-delta). This is useful for 0<epsilon<c/2 and fixed delta in (0,1). The class H_d is contained in the orthogonal orbit of f(x)=sign(sum_{i=1}^d x_i^2-sum_{i=d+1}^{2d} x_i^2). Thus an orthogonally equivariant learner of this single target under the standard Gaussian law has a fixed-confidence Omega(d^2 log(1/epsilon)) lower bound as epsilon decreases below an absolute constant. With expected disagreement risk epsilon, the corresponding explicit bound is (d(d-1)/2) log_2(c/(4epsilon))-1. This is an existing result of Li, Zhang and Arora, not new research; it concerns classification, not square-loss regression.
d is an integer >=2

Local escape bound (proof unaudited; no novelty or global burn-in claim). Fix n,m,d>=1, deterministic data ||x_i||<=1, y_i in {-1,1}, and a unit separator with margin gamma>0. Let phi be C1, phi(0)=0, alpha<=phi prime(z)<=1 for alpha>0, and phi prime beta-Lipschitz with beta>=0. For f_i=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j dot x_i) and averaged logistic loss, train both layers simultaneously with actual GD step m eta, eta>0. Put v=phi prime(0) sum_i y_i x_i/(2n), b=||v||>=alpha gamma/2, h=eta b, Delta=min(h,2), and Lambda=1+h-Delta/4>1. Let P project each neuron block onto (1,v/b)/sqrt(2), Q=I-P, and R=||theta||. The GD map is M theta+E with expanding eigenvalue 1+h on P, complementary operator norm at most max(1,|1-h|), and ||E||<=eta(beta R^2/2+R^3/(8m)). For k>=1 and r>0 satisfying eta(beta r/2+r^2/(8m))sqrt(1+k^2)<=Delta/4, any theta_0 with 0<||Ptheta_0||, ||theta_0||<=r, ||Qtheta_0||<=k||Ptheta_0|| exits the closed radius-r ball by floor(log(r/||Ptheta_0||)/log Lambda)+1; the cone is invariant until exit. For delta in (0,1), put rho=(delta/2)^(1/m)/sqrt(exp(1)), k=sqrt(2(d+1)/delta)/rho, and choose such an r. If theta_0 has iid N(0,sigma^2) coordinates, sigma>0, sigma<=r sqrt(delta/(2m(d+1))), then with probability >=1-delta the exit time is <=floor(log(r/(sigma sqrt(m)rho))/log Lambda)+1. The probability proof uses an unconditional chi-square lower tail and a union bound. This does not cover unit-variance initialization in general or guarantee loss reduction or absence of returns after exit.

  and $\pi=(\pi_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a sequence of partitions of $[0,T]$ satisfying Assumptions \eqref{ass:partitioncond}, \eqref{ass:partitioncond2}.  Let $(h_m)_{m\geq1}\subset L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be a sequence of nonnegative finite-valued Borel functions  such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\|h_m\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}\to 0$ as $m\to\infty$;
\item for every compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$,
$$
\int_K\int_K \frac{|h_m(x)-h_m(y)|}{|x-y|^d}\,dx\,dy<\infty.
$$

Then there exists a polar set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ and a subsequence $(h_{m_k})_{k\geq1}$ such that, for every $x_0\notin E$,
$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\ \limsup_{n\to\infty}\|h_{m_k}\|_{n,1,B}=0,
\qquad \mathbb{P}_{x_0}\text{-a.s.},
$$
where
$$
\|h\|_{n,1,B}
:=
\int_0^T
\sum_{i=0}^{m(n)-1}
\bigl(|h(B(t_i^n))|+|h(B(t_{i+1}^n)|)\bigr)(t_{i+1}^n-t_{i}^n)
$$

body:
Let f ∈ C^2(R) be uniformly convex, f''(s) ≥ θ > 0 for all s, and let u0 ∈ L^∞(R). Put L := f* (the Legendre transform of f), h(y) := ∫_0^y u0(r) dr (so h is Lipschitz), and for t > 0 consider the minimization of y ↦ t L( (x-y)/t ) + h(y). Then: (i) for each t > 0 a minimizer exists for every x, is unique for all but at most countably many x, and, denoting it y(x,t), the map x ↦ y(x,t) is nondecreasing; (ii) the function u(x,t) := (f')^{-1} ( ( x - y(x,t) ) / t ) = L'( (x - y(x,t))/t ), defined for a.e. x and every t > 0, is the unique Kruzhkov entropy solution of u_t + f(u)_x = 0 with u(·,0) = u0; (iii) u satisfies Oleinik's one-sided estimate u(x + z, t) - u(x,t) ≤ z/(θ t) for all z > 0 and t > 0 — so the solution can jump down but never up, and jumps are exactly the points where the minimizer y(·,t) is discontinuous; (iv) u = w_x where w is the Hopf-Lax solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation w_t + f(w_x) = 0 with w(·,0) = h.
f ∈ C^2 with f'' ≥ θ > 0 (uniform convexity); mere convexity gives the formula in a weaker form without the 1/(θt) rate
u0 ∈ L^∞(R) (no continuity or BV assumption is needed)

body:
[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2608.31008, 'Stability of gravitational instantons with a bounded Killing vector field'] Let $(M^4,g)$ be a connected, complete, smooth Ricci-flat
Riemannian manifold. Suppose that, for some
$p\in M$ and all sufficiently large $R$, one has
\[
    \operatorname{Vol}_g B_g(p,R) \leqslant C R^2.
\]
Then every bounded Killing vector field on $(M,g)$ is parallel.
Consequently, if $(M,g)$ is nonflat, it admits no nonzero bounded
Killing vector field.

body: In mathematical logic, model theory is the study of the relationship between formal theories and their models. The aspects investigated include the number and size of models of a theory, the relationship of different models to each other, and their interaction with the formal language itself. In particular, model theorists also investigate the sets that can be defined in a model of a theory, and the relationship of such definable sets to each other. As a separate discipline, model theory goes back to Alfred Tarski, who first used the term "Theory of Models" in publication in 1954. Since the 1970s, the subject has been shaped decisively by Saharon Shelah's stability theory.
title: Model theory

chi_x is a LOWER-bound exponent (a supremum over alpha making Var >= C n^{2 alpha}); chi' is an upper-bound shape exponent (an infimum over kappa sandwiching the ball)
C(x,m) is the cylinder of radius m about the ray through x; Gamma(0,nx) is the geodesic
B(t) is the random ball of radius t and B_nu the limit shape
Chatterjee's exponents are defined in arXiv:1105.4566 and are strictly stronger notions

THE CONCRETE TRAP: Newman-Piza's Theorem 6 concludes xi_x <= (1 + chi')/2 in terms of chi', while their Wehr-Aizenman bound chi_x >= (1 - (d-1) xi_x)/2 is in terms of chi_x. Those are two different exponents in two consecutive displays of the same paper. A derivation that chains them as if they were one object is unsound.
SECOND TRAP: Chatterjee's chi = 2 xi - 1 is a statement about HIS exponents. It does not, on its own, say anything about chi(d), chi_x, chi' or xi_x.
SOURCE: all four definitions read verbatim in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), tex lines 2698-2716 (xi_x, chi', chi_x) and 2946-2959 (Chatterjee's strengthened exponents and their non-existence status).
VERIFICATION STATUS: survey-claim.
title: The fluctuation and wandering exponents of first-passage percolation are DEFINED differently by different theorems and the definitions are not interchangeable: Kesten's chi(d) from Var ~ n^{2 chi}; Newman-Piza's chi_x = sup{alpha : Var T(0,nx) >= C n^{2 alpha} for all n}; the shape-fluctuation exponent chi' = inf{kappa : (t - t^kappa)B_nu subset B(t) subset (t + t^kappa)B_nu for large t, a.s.}; the wandering exponent xi_x = inf{alpha > 0 : liminf_n P(Gamma(0,nx) subset C(x, n^alpha)) > 0}; and Chatterjee's separate, strengthened exponents, which are not known to exist for any weight law. Mixing them silently is how the scaling relation gets misquoted.

body: The determinant is the unique function of the columns of an n x n matrix that is multilinear, alternating (zero when two columns coincide, sign-flipping under column swaps), and equal to 1 on the identity; equivalently det(A) = sum over permutations sigma of sign(sigma) * product_i A[i, sigma(i)]. Key properties: det(AB) = det(A) det(B); A is invertible iff det(A) != 0; the determinant equals the product of eigenvalues (with multiplicity) and is the signed volume scaling factor of the linear map.

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] For every \(m\ge0\), \(F_m\) is an \(m\)-cell.  Two distinct \(m\)-cells
are either disjoint or meet at one common boundary vertex.  Consequently,
every edge of \(F_\infty\) lies in exactly one \(m\)-cell.  If \(m\ge1\),
every \(m\)-cell is the union of \(M\) \((m-1)\)-cells, and the union of
the boundaries of these \(M\) subcells contains \(v_1\) vertices.

[Theorem 3 (Strong Szeg\H{o} expansion) of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\) and \(I_a=[1,a]\). There exists a holomorphic function \(\mathcal C_a:S_\pi\to\mathbb C\) such that, for every compact \(K\subset S_\pi\),
\[
\log\mathbb E\exp(\theta N_a(L))
=
L\Lambda_a(\theta)+\mathcal C_a(\theta)+o(1),
\qquad L\to\infty,
\]
uniformly for \(\theta\in K\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Strong Szeg\H{o} expansion

body:
Let mu be a nonnegative Borel measure on R such that every polynomial is absolutely integrable and integral q(t)^2 dmu(t)>0 for every nonzero real polynomial q. Let p_k be its degree-k monic orthogonal polynomials, with p_0=1. Fix n>=1 and alpha in R, and write r_1<...<r_n for the n distinct real roots of p_n+alpha p_(n-1). Define dmu_j(t)=product_(s=0)^(j-1)(r_(n-s)-t)dmu(t). For 0<=j<=n-1 and 0<=i<=n-j, let q_(j,i) be the unique degree-i monic polynomial orthogonal to every lower-degree polynomial for mu_j; these exist by finite-degree positivity. Also set q_(n,0)=1. Then for 1<=j<=n and 0<=i<=n-j there are coefficients c_0,...,c_i, all strictly positive, such that q_(j,i)=sum_(l=0)^i c_l q_(j-1,l). In particular c_i=1 by monicity. The expansion is into the immediately preceding root-removal family; the measures may be signed. This is Lemma3.8 of Cohn-Kumar.

q_(j,i) defined through degree n-j for j<n; q_(n,0)=1

B(x,r)=x+[-r,r]^d intersect Z^d, r an integer >=1; L=2r+1; n_r=r(2r+1)^(d-1); b_1(y)=omega(y,+e_1)-omega(y,-e_1). For delta>0, I_delta(x,r) counts rows in B with y_1<x_1 and b_1(y)>=delta, plus rows with y_1>x_1 and b_1(y)<=-delta. The plane y_1=x_1 is ignored. A_delta,theta(x,r)={I_delta(x,r)>=2 theta n_r}, theta in (1/2,1]. D(theta||1/2)=theta log(2theta)+(1-theta)log(2(1-theta)), with 0 log 0=0. For integer s>=1 put M_r(s)=2^s s! (2r+1)^s kappa^(-s(2r+1)). Let H be a genuine stopping time for the walk filtration enlarged by its entire fixed environment. Let C be an F_H-measurable integer center, with |C|_infinity<=N and X_H in B(C,r) on H<=N, for deterministic integer N>=0. Set Y equal to the exit time from that box measured after H and Y=0 on H>N. Then E_0[1_{H<=N}1_{A_delta,theta(C,r)}Y^s]<=M_r(s) min(1,(2N+1)^d exp(-2n_r D(theta||1/2))). Under Q=P_0(.|D^ell=infinity), q=P_0(D^ell=infinity)>0, where D^ell is first strict backtracking below the initial ell projection, this nonnegative moment is at most the same bound divided by q. Regeneration times cannot replace H because they depend on the future.

UNAUDITED SOURCE-PROOF CLARIFICATION. Let n>=2 be an integer and m=ceil(n*ln(2)). Let B be uniform on{0,1}^n and U be independently uniform on[n]^m. Let Y in[n]^m be coupled with them so that, almost surely, d_H(B,indicator_Unique(Y))=abs(|{i:B_i=1}|-|Unique(U)|), where the indicator is a length-n binary vector. For0<epsilon<1, the probability that this Hamming distance is at least epsilon*n is at most min(1,2*exp(-max(epsilon*n-2,0)^2/n)). Consequently there is an absolute C>0 such that along parameter choices with n>=C*ln(1/epsilon)^2/epsilon^2, this failure probability is negligible in n. PerturbDifference satisfies the required pathwise support identity. This states the small-tail conclusion supported by the proof of LemmaB.5; its displayed statement instead prints the weaker bound1-negl(n).

[Thm 7 of arXiv:2606.07194, 'Survival Probability of Markov Linear Reccurence Sequence in a Random Environment: Subcrit'] Let $\{Y_n\}$ be a subcritical irreducible aperiodic MRSRE. Assume that~(\ref{BnCond}) holds for some $h>0$, ${\bf E}^{(h)}\kappa_1<+\infty$, and  ${\bf E}\left(\left.Y_1^h\right|Y_0=0\right)<+\infty$. Then $\{Y_n\}$ is geometric ergodic, so
$$
{\bf P}(Y_n=k)\to \pi_k,\ n\to\infty,\ k\ge 1,
$$
where $\{\pi_k\}$ is the unique stationary distribution and the convergence is exponentially fast.

For 0<gamma<2, xi>0, Q=2/gamma+gamma/2, and alpha in [-2,2], set F(alpha)=(2-alpha^2/2)/(xi*(Q-alpha)). Then Q-alpha>0 and gamma/xi-F(alpha)=(alpha-gamma)^2/(2*xi*(Q-alpha)); the unique maximum is gamma/xi at alpha=gamma. In the LQG parametrization xi=gamma/d_gamma, maximizing F returns d_gamma and does not evaluate xi. Gwynne--Pfeffer Theorem 1.5 gives this profile for each fixed alpha and a deterministic or field-independent full-Euclidean-dimension Borel set; the algebra alone does not create one probability-one event for all alpha or an uncountable-union dimension rule. The endpoint gamma=2 is excluded.

[Definition defn:axiomatic_shf of arXiv:2608.11603, 'Continuous-time directed polymers to the Critical SHF via moments'] {}
	A process $\mathcal{Z}^{\theta_{\star}}$ is called a Stochastic Heat Flow with strength $\theta_{\star}$, or $\mathsf{SHF}(\theta_{\star})$, if
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, ref=\thedefinition\textup{(\roman*)}]
    	\item
    	 \textbf{(Continuity)} $\mathcal{Z}^{\theta_{\star}} = \{\mathcal{Z}^{\theta_{\star}}_{s,t}\} \in C(\mathbb{R}_{\leqslant}^{2}, \measspace{\mathbb{R}^2 \times \mathbb{R}^2})$. 
    	\item
    	\textbf{(Chapman--Kolmogorov)} For all $t_{0} < t_{1} < t_{2}$, there exists a sequence $\{u_{\ell}\}$ in $\mathcal{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for which the operator $\psi \mapsto u_{\ell} \ast \psi$ converges strongly to the identity, such that the difference $\mathcal{Z}^{\theta_{\star}}_{t_{0},t_{1}} \bullet_{\ell} \mathcal{Z}^{\theta_{\star}}_{t_{1},t_{2}} - \mathcal{Z}^{\theta_{\star}}_{t_{0},t_{2}}$ is well-defined and converges to $0$ vaguely, in probability as $\ell \to \infty$.
    	\item 
    	\textbf{(Independent increments)} For all $ t_{0}  < \cdots < t_{k}$, the random variables $\mathcal{Z}^{\theta_{\star}}_{t_{0},t_{1}},  \ldots \mathcal{Z}^{\theta_{\star}}_{t_{k-1}, t_{k}}$ are independent.
    	\item
    	\textbf{(Delta-Bose Moments)} For $n = 1,2,3,4$, $s<t$ and $h, h' \in \mathcal{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^2)$, the following holds:
    	\begin{equation*}
    		\mathbf{E} \Big(\Big\langle h, \mathcal{Z}^{\theta_{\star}}_{s,t} h' \Big\rangle \Big)^{n} = \Big\langle h^{\otimes n}, \mathcal{Q}^{[\![n]\!], \theta_{\star}}(t-s) h'^{\otimes n} \Big\rangle \, .
    	\end{equation*} 
    \end{enumerate}
title: Definition defn:axiomatic_shf of arXiv:2608.11603

body: In algebra, the Wedderburn–Artin theorem is a classification theorem for semisimple rings and semisimple algebras. The theorem states that a(n Artinian) semisimple ring R is isomorphic to the product of finitely many ni-by-ni matrix rings over division rings Di, for some integers ni, both of which are uniquely determined up to permutation of the index i. In particular, any simple left or right Artinian ring is isomorphic to an n-by-n matrix ring over a division ring D, where both n and D are uniquely determined.
title: Wedderburn–Artin theorem

[Definition 213 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] The master Riemann--Hilbert problem asks to find an $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{F}(z) = (F_h(z))_{h = 1}^H$ with the following properties for any $h \in [H]$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F_h(z)$ is a meromorphic function of $z \in \amsmathbb{C} \setminus [\alpha_h,\beta_h]$.
\item $F_h(x^{\pm}) = \lim_{\epsilon \rightarrow 0^+} F_h(x \pm \ii \epsilon)$ exist for any $x \in (\alpha_h,\beta_h)$.
\item $F_h(z) = O(\frac{1}{z})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$.
\item $\forall x \in (\alpha_h,\beta_h) \qquad \theta_{h,h}\big(F_h(x^+) + F_h(x^-)\big) + \sum_{g \neq h} 2\theta_{h,g}F_g(x) = D_h(x)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 213 of arXiv:2601.16377

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2609.03195, 'Lecture hall polytopes and\\Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths'] The set of \emph{L-S paths}  with bond $b$ is
\[
\Pi(b) := L(b) \cap \RR^{n+1}_{\ge 0}.
\]
For $\pi = (a_1,\dots,a_{n+1})\in \Pi(b)$ define the \emph{support} $\supp\pi$ as the set of indices $1\leq j\leq n+1$ such that $a_j\neq 0$ and set $\deg(\pi) := a_1 + \cdots + a_{n+1} $, the \emph{degree} of the L-S path $\pi$. Note that if $\pi = m_1v_1 + \cdots + m_{n+1}v_{n+1}$ then $\deg(\pi) = m_{n+1}$; in particular $\deg(\pi)$ is a non-negative integer. We denote by $\Pi(b)_k$ the set of L-S paths of degree $k$.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2609.03195

[Theorem 12 of arXiv:2609.03238, 'Representation Defects and Cassels Pairings for Congruent Number Curves'] Let
\[
n=p_1\cdots p_k
\]
be a product of distinct primes such that
\[
p_i\equiv1\pmod8
\quad(1\le i\le k),
\qquad
\left(\frac{p_i}{p_j}\right)=1
\quad(i\ne j).
\]
Then $M_n=0$, $s_2(n)=2k$, and
\[
\Sel_2'(E_n)
 =\langle\Lambda_1,\ldots,\Lambda_k,
 \Lambda_1',\ldots,\Lambda_k'\rangle,
\]
where $\Lambda_i=(p_i,1,p_i)$ and $\Lambda_i'=(p_i,p_i,1)$.
Let $C_n$ denote the $2k\times2k$ Cassels matrix in this basis, obtained from
\eqref{eq:zh1}--\eqref{eq:zh5} by taking $P=n$, $Q=1$, and $U_P=0$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $\Pf(C_n)=1$ if and only if
\[
\rk E_n(\Q)=0,
\qquad
\Sha(E_n)[2^\infty]\cong(\Z/2\Z)^{2k};
\]
\item one has
\begin{equation}
4^k\mid r_a(n)-h(-n)
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
r_a(n)\equiv h(-n)+4^k\Pf(C_n)\pmod{2\cdot4^k}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

body: [Lemma 6.1 (Ray and localization certificate) of arXiv:2607.11010, 'The storage capacity of the Ising perceptron: verification of the outstand'] Let $P\Subset\operatorname{int}K$ be one certified moment polygon, let $L\subset\mathbb{R}^{2}$ be a closed bounded rectangle, and let $\widehat{b}_{1},\ldots,\widehat{b}_{m}$ lie in $\operatorname{int}L$. For $a\in P$ set $F_{a}(b)=\Phi(b)-b\cdot a$ and $S_{a}=\{b:F_{a}(b)\leq\min_{k}F_{a}(\widehat{b}_{k})\}.$ Suppose each certified subsegment $E\subset\partial L$ and each tangent polygon $P_{j}$ covering $P$ has fixed weights $w_{E,j,k}\geq 0$, $\sum_{k}w_{E,j,k}=1$, for which $\sum_{k}w_{E,j,k}\{\Phi(b)-\Phi(\widehat{b}_{k})-(b-\widehat{b}_{k})\cdot a\}>0\quad(b\in E,\ a\in P_{j}).$ (5) Then the entropy dual $b(a)$ lies in $\operatorname{int}L$ for every $a\in P$. Moreover, with $f=(X,\tanh X)$ define $B_{L}=\mathbb{E}\left[ff^{\top}\max_{b\in L}\operatorname{sech}^{2}(b\cdot f)\right],$ and let $\widehat{B}_{L}\succeq B_{L}$ be any certified positive-definite majorant. Then, for every $v\in\mathbb{R}^{2}$, $v^{\top}\nabla^{2}H(a)v\leq-v^{\top}\widehat{B}_{L}^{-1}v.$ (6) Consequently, fix a unit vector $v$, a radius $R(v)>0$, and the preceding global choice $\dot{\sigma}_{v}=C\cdot v$. Suppose $0=t_{0}<t_{1}<\cdots<t_{r}=R(v)$ and that for every $i$ there are a certified polygon $P_{i}\Subset\operatorname{int}K$ and a closed bounded rectangle $L_{i}$ satisfying the preceding localization hypotheses, with $\{a^{\star}+tv:t\in[t_{i-1},t_{i}]\}\subset P_{i}$. Assume also throughout the prefix that $a_{2}(t)^{2}<q_{0}$ and $s(t)\geq 0$, and that on every segment the certificate bounds the second derivative of the nonentropy part of $\varphi_{v}$ by $v^{\top}\widehat{B}_{L_{i}}^{-1}v$. Then $H+G\leq 0$ on the full ray prefix $0\leq t\leq R(v)$.

[Definition of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let $(X,d,\mu)$ be a metric measure space and $p \in (1,\infty)$. 
		The function  $g \in L^p(X,\mu)$ is a \emph{generalized upper gradient} for
		$f \in L^p(X,mu)$, if there exist sequences, $f_i \xrightarrow{L^p(X,\mu)} f, g_i \xrightarrow{L^p(X,\mu)}g$, such that $g_i$ is an upper
		gradient for $f_i$, for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$. \\
		We say that $g$ is a \emph{minimal generalized upper gradient} for $f$ if $g$ is a generalized upper gradient such that 
		\[
		\norm{f}_{1,p}= \norm{f}_{L^p(\mu)}+\norm{g}_{L^p(\mu)}.
		\]

body: Let X be a Banach space with continuous dual X*. A sequence (x_n) in X converges weakly to x in X, written x_n converges to x weakly, if f(x_n) converges to f(x) for every f in X*. Norm convergence implies weak convergence, but not conversely in infinite dimensions; a weakly convergent sequence is norm-bounded (by the uniform boundedness principle) and its weak limit, if it exists, is unique (by Hahn-Banach). [standard, e.g. Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis]
title: Weak Convergence of a Sequence in a Banach Space

body: The monotone convergence theorem for an INCREASING sequence 0 <= f_1 <= f_2 <= ... needs no integrability hypothesis at all: integral f_n dmu increases to integral (lim f_n) dmu in [0, infinity]. The downward statement is FALSE without an extra hypothesis. On R with Lebesgue measure, f_n = 1_{[n, infinity)} decreases pointwise to 0, yet integral f_n = infinity for every n. The correct downward version requires f_1 in L^1 (equivalently, on a finite measure space with a bounded f_1): if f_n decreases pointwise to f and f_1 is integrable then integral f_n -> integral f, which follows from applying upward monotone convergence to f_1 - f_n. FATOU'S LEMMA, integral liminf f_n <= liminf integral f_n for f_n >= 0, is strict in general and its strictness is exactly the escaping-mass and concentrating-mass phenomena: with f_n = 1_{[n, n+1]} on R, liminf f_n = 0 pointwise so the left side is 0 while the right side is 1; with f_n = n 1_{(0, 1/n)} on [0,1] the left side is 0 and the right side is again 1. Reverse Fatou, limsup integral f_n <= integral limsup f_n, requires an integrable UPPER bound f_n <= g in L^1, and fails without one: for f_n = n 1_{(0, 1/n)} on [0,1] the pointwise limsup is 0 with integral 0, while limsup integral f_n = 1, so the inequality is violated - and no integrable g dominates all the f_n. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorems 2.14 and 2.15]

For logistic Euclidean fixed-step GD on f(v,p)=v[a+b tanh(kp)], b,k>0, |a|<b, and 0<eta<=1/(bk), every finite initialization either converges to the unique hyperbolic saddle (0,atanh(-a/b)/k) or escapes with both coordinates tending to matching-sign infinity. The saddle's global stable set is Lebesgue null; both escaping basins are open and nonempty. Joint normalized limits are (+1,0) and (-1,0). For 0<|a|<b the smaller-absolute-token basin has strictly suboptimal limiting joint normalized margin and positive measure.
One positive-label observation, two fixed scalar tokens a+-b, attention logit gap 2kp, jointly trained shared scalar head v and unfactored scalar query p. Constant eta in displayed interval.
