PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Let an infinite connected locally finite unit-conductance graph C contain a subdivision of a locally finite graph H, replacing each edge e by an internally vertex-disjoint path of length ell_e. If H has a unit flow f from a root to infinity with sum_e ell_e f(e)^2 finite, then C is transient. Lift the constant current along each replacement path; its energy is exactly that sum and its divergence is inherited at branch vertices. Uniformly bounded corridor lengths suffice whenever H is transient. A percolation argument must establish this quantitative energy condition, not only branching topology.

An actual subdivision with disjoint path interiors

[Lemma 24 (The case $n=2$ is the case $n\ge 2$) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero.
    Let $D$ be a derivation of the form $D= \sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}$ where $f_i\in k(X)$ are nonzero rational functions.

    Then, $D$ defines an algebraically integrable foliation on $k(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n,\ldots)$ if and only if 
    for each $1\le i<j\le n$ the derivation $E_{ij}=f_i(x_i)\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}+f_j(x_j)\frac{\partial}{\partial x_j}$ defines an algebraically integrable foliation on $k(x_i,x_j)$.

[Defn de.2 of arXiv:2411.13099, 'Long time behavior of killed Feynman-Kac semigroups with singular Schr{ö}dinger potentials'] Let  $\mathbf F: \mathscr V\to [1,+\infty]$ be a measurable function. 
   We say that  $(Q^{\mathfrak X}_t,t\ge 0)$ is    $\mathbf F$ {\rm compact-ergodic} over $\mathscr V$   if:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[\textbf 1.] There exists a unique q.s.d.  $\rho$ for  $(P^{\mathfrak X}_t,t\ge 0)$ in   $  \mathcal P_{\mathbf F}(\mathscr V)$.  
 \item[\textbf 2.] 
  For all $t>0$, $Q^{\mathfrak X}_t:b\mathcal B_{\mathbf F}(\mathscr V)\to b\mathcal B_{\mathbf F}(\mathscr V)$ is compact and there exists $\lambda\ge  \inf_{\mathscr V} \mathbf V$   such that $\mathsf r_{sp}(Q^{\mathfrak X}_t|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf F}(\mathscr V)} ) =e^{-\lambda t}, \ \forall t>0$. 
  Furthermore,  $\rho    Q^{\mathfrak X}_t =e^{-\lambda t}\rho$, for all $t\ge 0$, and $\rho (O)>0$ for all nonempty open subsets $O$ of $ \mathscr V$. In addition,  there is a unique   function $\varphi \in \mathcal C_{b\mathbf F}( \mathscr V)$   such that  $\rho   (\varphi )=1$ and $
      Q^{\mathfrak X}_t \varphi= e^{-\lambda  t} \varphi  \text{ on } \mathscr V, \forall t\ge0$.  
 Moreover, $\varphi>0$   everywhere on $\mathscr V$.
\item[\textbf 3.] There exist   $\mathfrak m_1>0$, and   $\mathfrak m_2\ge 1$, s.t.  for all  $t>0$ and all   $\nu\in \mathcal P_{\mathbf F  }( \mathscr V)$:
$$
\sup_{\mathcal A\in\mathcal B(\mathscr V)}\big |  \nu P^{\mathfrak X}_t(\mathcal A)-\rho  (\mathcal A)\big |\le \mathfrak m_2 \, e^{-\mathfrak m_1 t} \frac{\nu(\mathbf F )}{\nu(\varphi)}.
$$
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.07365, 'A pathwise Ito formula \\for weakly differentiable functions'] There exists a constant $C_d$ such that if $f\in W^{1, 1}(\Rr^d)$ and its derivatives are defined at every point by \ref{2eq:values}, and $x, y\in\Rr^d$ be such that $|f(y)|, |f(x)| <+\infty.$ If $x, y\in Q$ then
\[
|f(y)- f(x) |\leq C_d\left(\int_Q \frac {|\nabla f(z)|} {|x- z|^{d-1}} dz\,+\, \int_Q \frac {|\nabla f(z)|} {|y- z|^{d-1}} dz\right).
\]
Similarly for $f\in W^{2, 1}(\Rr^d)$, and $x, y\in Q$ with $|f(y)|, |f(x)|, |\nabla f(x)| <+\infty$ 
\[
|f(y)- f(x) - \nabla f(x) (y-x)|\leq C_d\left(\int_Q \frac {|\nabla^2 f(z)|} {|x- z|^{d-2}} dz\,+\, \int_Q \frac {|\nabla^2 f(z)|} {|y- z|^{d-2}} dz\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop eq:lesmom of arXiv:2603.21634, 'Individual-based stochastic model with unbounded growth, birth and death rates: a tightnes'] Let $p \geq 1$, and under the \hyperlink{ren}{renormalized setting}, assume in addition that
\begin{align}
    \underset{K \in \mathbb{N}^{*}}{\mathrm{sup}} \hspace{0.1 cm} \mathbb{E}\left(\left(E_{0}^{K} +N_{0}^{K} + \Omega^{K}_{0}\right)^{p}\right) < + \infty.
    
    \end{align}
Then, for all $T \geq 0$, we have
\[ \sup_{K \in \mathbb{N}^{*}} \mathbb{E}\left( \sup_{t \in [0,T]}\left(E_{t}^{K} +N_{t}^{K} + \Omega^{K}_{t}\right)^{p} \right) < + \infty. \]
This immediately implies that for every $\varphi \in \mathfrak{B}_{1+\mathrm{Id}+\omega}(\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+})$, we have
\[ \sup_{K \in \mathbb{N}^{*}} \mathbb{E}\left(\underset{t \in [0,T]}{\mathrm{sup}} \left|\langle \mu^{K}_{t}, \varphi \rangle\right|^{p} \right) < + \infty. \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let d>=1, sigma>0, and let f be a measurable deterministic classifier or a measurable input-dependent distribution on a finite label set Y of size K>=2. Its internal randomness is averaged together with independent Gaussian noise epsilon~N(0,sigma^2 I_d). Define g(z) as a class maximizing P(f(z+epsilon)=c), using any fixed rule to resolve ties. Fix x in R^d and cA in Y. Suppose 0<pB<pA<1 and P(f(x+epsilon)=cA)>=pA, while max_(c!=cA) P(f(x+epsilon)=c)<=pB. With Phi the standard normal CDF, set R=(sigma/2)*(Phi^(-1)(pA)-Phi^(-1)(pB)). Then simultaneously for all delta with ||delta||_2<R, cA is the unique most probable class at x+delta and g(x+delta)=cA. In the binary case, taking pB=1-pA for pA>1/2 gives R=sigma*Phi^(-1)(pA). The inequalities are bounds on smoothed probabilities; the certificate does not require them to be exact or the base classifier to be continuous.
Finite label set and measurable classifier or Markov classification kernel
Gaussian noise variance sigma^2 I with sigma>0, independent of classifier randomness
Bounds at one fixed x: top-class probability at least pA and every competitor at most pB
Interior nontrivial case 0<pB<pA<1; strict open perturbation ball
No assumption on input distribution or base network architecture

body: In calculus and real analysis, absolute continuity is a regularity property of functions that is stronger than uniform continuity, and hence continuity. The notion of absolute continuity allows one to obtain generalizations of the relationship between the two central operations of calculus—differentiation and integration. This relationship is commonly characterized in the framework of Riemann integration, but with absolute continuity it may be formulated in terms of Lebesgue integration. For real-valued functions on the real line, two interrelated notions appear: absolute continuity of functions and absolute continuity of measures. These two notions are generalized in different directions. The usual derivative of a function is related to the Radon–Nikodym derivative, or density, of a measure. We have the following chains of inclusions for functions over an interval:Lipschitz continuous ⊆ absolutely continuous ⊆ uniformly continuous ⊆ continuous
title: Absolute continuity

body: [Lemma lem-resample-infty-2 of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] For $(\phi, \eta) \sim M_W$, let $\tau$ be the time $\eta$ separates $i$ from $\infty$, and let $U$ be the unbounded connected component of $\mathbb{H} \backslash \eta((0,\tau])$. Conditioned on $\eta$ and $\phi|_{\mathbb{H} \backslash U}$, we have $\phi|_U \stackrel d= h_0 + \mathfrak h_0$ where $h_0$ is a GFF on $U$ with zero boundary conditions on $\partial U \cap \mathbb{H}$ and free boundary conditions elsewhere, and $\mathfrak h_0$ is the harmonic extension of $\phi|_{\mathbb{H} \backslash U}$ to $U$ having zero normal derivative on $\partial U \cap \mathbb{H}$.
title: Lemma lem-resample-infty-2 of arXiv:2411.19810

    \le C|\eta-\eta'|.
\]

body:
Let alpha be irrational and let R_alpha(x) = x + alpha modulo 1 on the circle. Then R_alpha is UNIQUELY ERGODIC: Lebesgue measure is its only invariant Borel probability measure. Equivalently (Weyl), for every continuous f the Birkhoff averages (1/N) sum_{n=0}^{N-1} f(x + n alpha) converge to the integral of f UNIFORMLY in x, and for every arc I the orbit spends asymptotically |I| of its time in I, for EVERY starting point with no exceptional set. For rational alpha the rotation is periodic and has many invariant measures, so irrationality is exactly what is used.
alpha irrational.
The conclusion for every point (not merely almost every point) is the force of unique ergodicity;
Birkhoff's theorem alone would give an almost-everywhere statement.
Uniform convergence is asserted for CONTINUOUS f - for an indicator it follows by approximating the arc from inside and outside, since the boundary has measure zero.

body:
PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. Consider the exact critical tanh two-input Gram chain: initialize a deterministic positive semidefinite Gram with marginal variances q0,r0 in (0,1]; conditional on the completed past F_j, draw n iid centered Gaussian pairs (Ai,Bi) with covariance the current Gram, and set Qnew=mean tanh(Ai)^2, Rnew=mean tanh(Bi)^2, Cnew=mean tanh(Ai)tanh(Bi). Write D_j=1-C_j/sqrt(Q_j R_j), F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2, delta_j=1-E[tanh(Ai)tanh(Bi)|F_j]/sqrt(F(Q_j)F(R_j)), and eta_(j+1)=D_(j+1)-E[D_(j+1)|F_j]. Let K,Lambda be uniform constants with E[eta^2|F_j]<=K delta_j^2/n and E[eta^4|F_j]<=16Lambda^4 delta_j^4/n^2, as supplied by unaudited C010/C015. For positive F_j-measurable a_j<=1+8(Q_j^2+R_j^2), put P0=1, P_(j+1)=P_j a_j. For deterministic B>=0 let tau=inf{j>=0:delta_j/P_(j+1)>B}. For n>=27648 and every finite L>=1, ||P_L sum_(j=0)^(L-1)1_{j<tau} eta_(j+1)/P_(j+1)||_2 <= exp(96(q0+r0))*(4K^2+48Lambda^4)^(1/4)*B*sqrt(L/n). Norms are probability Lp norms. The terminal product may depend on the same innovations. The proof uses unaudited C005 fourth product moments and elementary conditional fourth-power expansion plus Holder. This is a stopped centered-noise component; removal of stopping, predictable forcing, and the full Tensor Programs rate remain open. The general martingale inequality itself is not claimed new.
Exact critical tanh chain with fresh Gaussian rows; deterministic positive initial variances <=1; n>=27648
Positive predictable multipliers bounded by 1+8(Q_j^2+R_j^2); stopping test uses delta_j/P_(j+1)
C005 product moments and C010/C015 noise moment estimates remain unaudited dependencies

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:3a411f05eda0fdfbb5633adc08a89c030fb69044d7101fe7b146a82db2463e36","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/3a/3a411f05eda0fdfbb5633adc08a89c030fb69044d7101fe7b146a82db2463e36.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f338fe623316750b2295d81431a8653a4c68a3e22e65b92e506a2df860ed067c","bundle_entry_key":"tanh_stopped_angular_martingale","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c016-stopped-angular-martingale","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Quantitative Tensor Programs and martingale propagation","draft":"w712/bundle_012.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:critical-tanh-stopped-angular-martingale-dependent-terminal-product","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C016 v1: stopped angular martingale with a dependent terminal multiplier

Kind: moved. Target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unverified.
The general martingale estimate is elementary; no novelty is claimed for
that inequality. The application handles a specific dependence obstruction
in the two-input critical tanh architecture. Stopping removal is not proved.

## Statement

Consider the exact fresh-row critical tanh Gram chain of C015, starting
from deterministic marginal variances q0,r0 in (0,1]. Let F_j be its
completed layer-j past. Let delta_j be the population angular gap at that
current state, and let

    eta_(j+1)=D_(j+1)-E[D_(j+1)|F_j].

C010 v1 and C015 v1 give universal finite K,Lambda such that

    E[eta_(j+1)|F_j]=0,
    E[eta_(j+1)^2|F_j]<=K delta_j^2/n,
    E[eta_(j+1)^4|F_j]<=16Lambda^4 delta_j^4/n^2.     (1)

These two dependencies are unaudited. C005 v1, also unaudited, is the
occupation/stability-product input below. All new conclusions inherit
these explicitly stated dependencies.

Let a_j be finite, positive, F_j-measurable multipliers with

    a_j<=1+8(Q_j^2+R_j^2),
    P_0=1, P_(j+1)=P_j a_j.

The multipliers may depend on all previous innovations. Fix deterministic
B>=0 and define the F_j-stopping time

    tau_B=inf{j>=0: delta_j/P_(j+1)>B},

with inf empty=infinity. The quantity tested at j is F_j-measurable:
P_(j+1) uses a_j but no layer-(j+1) noise. Define

    M_L=sum_(j=0)^(L-1) 1_{j<tau_B} eta_(j+1)/P_(j+1),
    Z_L=P_L M_L.

For n>=27648 and every finite integer L>=1,

    ||Z_L||_2
      <=exp[96(q0+r0)] (4K^2+48Lambda^4)^(1/4)
                                      B sqrt(L/n).  (2)

The assertion includes arbitrary dependence between P_L and M_L.
For L=0, Z_0=0. No bound on the probability of tau_B<=L is asserted.

## 1. Elementary fourth moment under deterministic conditional envelopes

Let xi_(j+1) be martingale differences and assume
E[xi_(j+1)^2|F_j]<=v_j, E[xi_(j+1)^4|F_j]<=w_j,
where v_j,w_j are deterministic nonnegative finite numbers.
Put S_0=0 and S_l=sum_(j<l)xi_(j+1). We prove

    E S_L^4 <=4(sum_(j<L)v_j)^2+3sum_(j<L)w_j.       (3)

All finite sums have finite fourth moments by the triangle inequality.
The martingale-difference property gives, by expanding the square,

    E S_j^2=sum_(i<j) E xi_(i+1)^2<=sum_(i<j)v_i.

Conditionally on F_j, expand the fourth power of S_j+xi_(j+1).
The term linear in xi vanishes. Conditional Cauchy-Schwarz gives
|E[xi_(j+1)^3|F_j]|<=sqrt(v_j w_j). Thus

    E[S_(j+1)^4|F_j]
      <=S_j^4+6v_j S_j^2+4|S_j|sqrt(v_j w_j)+w_j
      <=S_j^4+8v_j S_j^2+3w_j,

using 4xy<=2x^2+2y^2 with x=sqrt(v_j)|S_j|, y=sqrt(w_j).
This also holds when either envelope is zero. Take expectations and sum:

    E S_L^4 <=8sum_(j<L) v_j sum_(i<j)v_i+3sum_(j<L)w_j
       =4[(sum_(j<L)v_j)^2-sum_(j<L)v_j^2]+3sum_(j<L)w_j
       <=4(sum_(j<L)v_j)^2+3sum_(j<L)w_j.

This proves (3). No independence between different increments is assumed.
The negative term was dropped, not declared equal to zero.

## 2. Predictable stopping supplies the envelopes

For xi_(j+1)=1_{j<tau_B}eta_(j+1)/P_(j+1), the weight is
F_j-measurable. Since j<tau_B implies delta_j/P_(j+1)<=B,
(1) gives

    E[xi_(j+1)|F_j]=0,
    E[xi_(j+1)^2|F_j]<=K B^2/n=:v,
    E[xi_(j+1)^4|F_j]<=16Lambda^4 B^4/n^2=:w.

These bounds also prove integrability of the weighted increments; no
uncontrolled inverse moment of P_(j+1) has been hidden. In the zero-gap
case (1) forces eta_(j+1)=0 conditionally, so B=0 is harmless.
Apply (3) to the L increments to get

    E M_L^4 <=4K^2 B^4 L^2/n^2+48Lambda^4 B^4 L/n^2
             <=(4K^2+48Lambda^4) B^4 L^2/n^2,       (4)

where the last inequality uses L>=1. This is a deterministic-time terminal
estimate; no unproved maximal-martingale inequality is needed.

## 3. The terminal product stays dependent

Pointwise, positivity and the bound on a_j give

    0<P_L<=product_(j<L)[1+8(Q_j^2+R_j^2)].

C005 v1, final stability-product assertion at r=4, requires
n>=6912*4=27648 and gives

    E P_L^4 <=exp[384(q0+r0)],
    ||P_L||_4<=exp[96(q0+r0)].                       (5)

The variances Q_j and R_j may be dependent; C005 already uses Holder
across the two marginal chains. We do not replace the fourth moment in
(5) by the smaller number exp[96(q0+r0)]; the latter bounds its fourth root.

Holder applied to the two possibly dependent factors now yields

    ||P_L M_L||_2<=||P_L||_4 ||M_L||_4.

Combine (4)-(5) to prove (2). A terminal product never leaves a conditional
expectation by an independence assertion.

## 4. Application and the exact unpaid step

The positive secant slopes of the normalized tanh covariance map in the
angular variable are admissible multipliers a_j: the upper bound follows
from C004 and positivity from C012. At equal comparison arguments take
the derivative. The resulting P is the homogeneous product in the
angular error's variation-of-constants formula, with population radial
and finite-width bias terms kept as forcing terms. Claims C004 and C012
are contextual inputs for this particular choice; the theorem above
assumes the multiplier bounds explicitly and does not re-prove them.

Taking B=b D0 with fixed b>0 and deterministic initial gap D0 therefore
gives a stopped stochastic-convolution term of order D0 sqrt(L/n).
It does not show that tau_B is late. The missing implication is a
uniform-in-depth bound on delta_j/P_(j+1) relative to D0, or a replacement
localized estimate plus a tail bound strong enough for unstopping.
C014 controls radial mixed moments, but those estimates alone do not
bound this inverse-product-normalized angular quantity or its maximum.
One cannot remove the indicator in M_L without that further argument.

The estimate treats the centered noise component only. Predictable bias,
radial forcing, removal of stopping, and the final readout coupling still
need a joint proof before the full two-input rate can be asserted.

## 5. Load-bearing hypotheses and boundaries

Predictability is essential to the generic noise-envelope argument. Fix
any n>=27648, independent symmetric signs eps_i, eta_i=eps_i/sqrt(n),
delta=1 and terminal multiplier P=1. All conditional noise bounds in (1)
hold with K=Lambda=1. Use nonnegative weights
w_(i-1)=1_{eps_i=1}, not measurable with respect to the previous past.
Although |w|delta<=1, the weighted sum has expectation L/(2sqrt(n)),
and therefore its L2 norm is at least that number. At L=64 it exceeds
52^(1/4)sqrt(L/n), since 32^4>52*8^4. Thus bounded future-dependent
weights cannot replace predictable ones in the generic argument.
This is a counterexample for the abstract noise-envelope inference, not
a claim that these Rademacher innovations are an exact tanh Gram chain.

Terminal dependence is allowed and handled by Holder, not excluded by
hypothesis. Positive multipliers make the normalization and stopping
test defined. The width threshold comes solely from the cited product
moment bound and also implies n>=64 for C010/C015. Zero initial angular
gap in the identical-input case gives zero innovations exactly.

Author check: the finite algebra and dependence handling re-derive.
This is not an independent review, a Lean certificate, or a proof of the
full TARGET. Source locators: C005 v1 final stability-product display;
C010 v1 equation (1); C015 v1 equations (2) and (12).","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:36fafb1fe5b5b0174563524fa7eb99587a35ee6d3602d1e54ff0da8c6df94fdb","revision_digest":"sha256:d98ce27b23ea2784744b82161eacec003e52e6a2e02befd6eccd955a783b20d6","source_id":"own-work:T250-w712-C016-v1","source_revision":"C016-v1-2026-10-21","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 20 (SDE for the second Malliavin derivative) of arXiv:2605.03057, 'Uniform-in-time quantitative fluctuations of large scale interacting particle systems'] Assume that Assumptions \ref{ass:smooth},
and \ref{ass:second-malliavin-uniform} hold. Fix
$ 0 \le r \le s \le t $, $ u \in [s,t] $,
$ i,j,k \in \left\{ 1,\dots,N \right\} $, and
$ \alpha,\beta \in \left\{ 1,\dots,m \right\} $.
Then, the process $\left(
D_r^{k,\beta} D_s^{j,\alpha} X_u^{i,N}
\right)_{u \in [s,t]}$ solves the SDE
\begin{align}

D_r^{k,\beta} D_s^{j,\alpha} X_u^{i,N}
&=
\mathcal I_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\int_s^u
\left(
\partial_x b\left( X_\rho^{i,N},\mu_\rho^N \right)
D_r^{k,\beta} D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{i,N}
+
G_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}(\rho)
+
R_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}(\rho)
\right)
d\rho
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\int_s^u
\left(
\partial_x \sigma\left( X_\rho^{i,N},\mu_\rho^N \right)
D_r^{k,\beta} D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{i,N}
+
H_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}(\rho)
+
S_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}(\rho)
\right)
dB_\rho^i ,
\end{align}
where $\mathcal I_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}$ denotes the initial
condition given by
\begin{align*}
\mathcal I_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}
&=
\mathbf{1}_{\left\{ i=j \right\}}
\partial_x \sigma\left( X_s^{i,N},\mu_s^N \right)
D_r^{k,\beta} X_s^{i,N}
e_\alpha
+
\mathbf{1}_{\left\{ r=s \right\}}
\mathbf{1}_{\left\{ i=k \right\}}
\partial_x \sigma\left( X_s^{i,N},\mu_s^N \right)
D_s^{j,\alpha} X_s^{i,N}e_\beta
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\mathbf{1}_{\left\{ i=j \right\}} \frac1N \sum_{\ell=1}^N
\partial_\mu \sigma\left( X_s^{i,N},\mu_s^N \right)\left( X_s^{\ell,N} \right)
D_r^{k,\beta} X_s^{\ell,N} e_\alpha
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\mathbf{1}_{\left\{ r=s \right\}}
\mathbf{1}_{\left\{ i=k \right\}}
\frac1N \sum_{\ell=1}^N
\partial_\mu \sigma\left( X_s^{i,N},\mu_s^N \right)\left( X_s^{\ell,N} \right)
D_s^{j,\alpha} X_s^{\ell,N} e_\beta ,
\end{align*}
with $ e_\alpha $ denoting the $ \alpha $-th vector of the canonical basis of $ \R^m $,
\begin{align}

G_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}(\rho)
&=
\frac1N \sum_{\ell=1}^N
\partial_\mu b\left( X_\rho^{i,N},\mu_\rho^N \right)\left( X_\rho^{\ell,N} \right)
D_r^{k,\beta} D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{\ell,N},
\end{align}
and $H_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}(\rho) $ is defined by the same formula, with
$ b $ replaced by $ \sigma $, while
\begin{align}

R_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}(\rho)
&=
\partial_{xx}^2 b\left( X_\rho^{i,N},\mu_\rho^N \right)
\left[
D_r^{k,\beta} X_\rho^{i,N}, D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{i,N}
\right]
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\frac1N \sum_{\ell=1}^N
\partial_\mu\left[ \partial_x b \right]
\left( X_\rho^{i,N},\mu_\rho^N \right)\left( X_\rho^{\ell,N} \right)
\left[
D_r^{k,\beta} X_\rho^{\ell,N}, D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{i,N}
\right]
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\frac1N \sum_{\ell=1}^N
\partial_x\left[
\partial_\mu b\left( \cdot,\mu_\rho^N \right)\left( X_\rho^{\ell,N} \right)
\right]\left( X_\rho^{i,N} \right)
\left[
D_r^{k,\beta} X_\rho^{i,N}, D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{\ell,N}
\right]
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\frac1N \sum_{\ell=1}^N
\partial_v\left[
\partial_\mu b\left( X_\rho^{i,N},\mu_\rho^N \right)
\right]\left( X_\rho^{\ell,N} \right)
\left[
D_r^{k,\beta} X_\rho^{\ell,N}, D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{\ell,N}
\right]
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\frac1{N^2}\sum_{\ell=1}^N \sum_{q=1}^N
\partial_{\mu\mu}^2 b\left( X_\rho^{i,N},\mu_\rho^N \right)
\left( X_\rho^{\ell,N}, X_\rho^{q,N} \right)
\left[
D_r^{k,\beta} X_\rho^{q,N}, D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{\ell,N}
\right],
\end{align}
and $ S_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}(\rho) $ is defined by the same formula, with
$ b $ replaced by $ \sigma $. Finally, there exists a constant $ C > 0 $, independent of
$ r,s,t,\rho,N,i,j,k,\alpha,\beta $, such that, for every $ \rho \in [s,t] $,
\begin{align}

\norm{R_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}(\rho)}
+
\norm{S_{r,s}^{i,j,k,\alpha,\beta}(\rho)}
&\le
C \Bigg(
\norm{D_r^{k,\beta} X_\rho^{i,N}}
\norm{D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{i,N}}
+
\norm{D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{i,N}}
\frac1N \sum_{\ell=1}^N
\norm{D_r^{k,\beta} X_\rho^{\ell,N}}
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\norm{D_r^{k,\beta} X_\rho^{i,N}}
\frac1N \sum_{\ell=1}^N
\norm{D_s^{j,\alpha} X_\rho^{\ell,N}}
+
\frac1N \sum_{\ell=1}^N
\norm{D_r^{k,\beta} X_\rho^{\ell,N}}

body: [Lemma lem:crossing_distances_of_small_annuli_are_uniformly_small of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] Let $F \subseteq \BD$ be a compact set and fix $x,y \in F$. Then,  there exist a constant $c_2 >0$ (depending only on $x,y$,  and $F$) and,  for each $c>0$,  constants $R_0 = R_0(x,y,F,c)>1$ and $c_1 = c_1(x,y,F,c)>1$,  such that the following is true for all $c>0$ and all $R \geq R_0$. Let $\SCL$ (resp.\ $\SCL'$) denote the loop in $\Gamma$ surrounding $x$ (resp.\ $y$) and suppose that we are working on the event that $\SCL \neq \SCL'$. Let $P$ be a $D_\Gamma$-geodesic connecting $\SCL$ to $\SCL'$ viewed as a path from $\SCL$ to $\SCL'$,  and let $\widetilde{P}$ denote the time-reversal of $P$. Off an event with probability at most $c_1 e^{-c_2 c R}$,  we have that for all $z \in F$,  if the paths $P$ and $\widetilde{P}$ intersect $\overline{B_{2^{-R}}(z)}$ before intersecting each other, {and if we let $t$ (resp.\ $\widetilde{t}$) be the first time that $P$ (resp.\ $\widetilde{P}$) intersects $\overline{B_{2^{-R}}(z)}$, } then we have that $t \leq 1 - \widetilde{t}$ and that $\len(P|_{[t , 1-\widetilde{t}]} ; D_\Gamma)$,  i.e.\ the $D_\Gamma$-length of the part of $P$ which is left after removing $P|_{[0,t]}$ and the time-reversal of $\widetilde{P}|_{[0,\widetilde{t}]}$,  is strictly less than $c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:crossing_distances_of_small_annuli_are_uniformly_small of arXiv:2609.04140

body: Publication record. A. E. Holroyd, L. Levine, K. Mészáros, Y. Peres, J. Propp and D. B. Wilson (Chip-firing and rotor-routing on directed graphs, 2008, Question 6.2) asked whether the limiting shape of the sandpile aggregate S_{n,H} on a background of height H is a regular (4H+12)-gon. Y. Shmalo, Corner angles of sandpile aggregates on a background of holes (October 2026) shows that for H >= -1 no limit of the rescaled S_{n,H} is a regular (4H+12)-gon: a corner of opening alpha has alpha > pi/2 and sin(alpha) <= 1/(H+3), and a convex polygonal limit has m >= 2 pi / arcsin(1/(H+3)) vertices with 4 | m (Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2). Existence and polygonality of the limit are not shown. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/sandpile-holes-corner-angles (commit db3b70c1c0ca). Not refereed; an outside audit is owed.
title: Holroyd-Levine-Meszaros-Peres-Propp-Wilson Question 6.2 answered negatively for H >= -1: limiting shapes of sandpile aggregates S_{n,H} are not regular (4H+12)-gons (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/sandpile-holes-corner-angles)

[Proposition Prop:WM of arXiv:2609.02213, 'Invariant subspaces for free linearizations of Lipschitz maps'] Let $M$ be an infinite metric space, let $f:M\to M$ be Lipschitz, and let $e\in M$.
		\begin{enumerate}[$(i)$]
			\item If $f$ is weakly mixing, then $T_{f,e}$ is weakly mixing.
			\item If $f$ is mixing, then $T_{f,e}$ is mixing.
			\item If $f$ is weakly mixing and chaotic, then $T_{f,e}$ is weakly mixing and chaotic.
		\end{enumerate}

	\((T_t)_{t\ge0}\) and \((S_t)_{t\ge0}\) on \( \mathcal L^2((0,1);\mathbb R^2)\).
	Consequently, for every initial datum in \(\mathcal L^2((0,1);\mathbb R^2)\), equation \eqref{eq3.2} $\left( \eqref{eq3.3}\right)$  admits a unique mild solution given by $ \bm\rho(t)=T_t\bm\rho_0 $ $ \left( \bm \rho(t)=S_t\bm \rho_0 \right) $.
	Moreover, these solutions are smooth in space and time for every \(t>0\).
	If \( \bm\rho_0\in\mathscr S \) $ \left( \bm \rho_0\in\mathscr S^\dagger \right) $, then $ T_t\bm\rho_0 $ $ \left( S_t\bm \rho_0 \right)  $ will be
	$\mathcal C^\infty$ in space and time for all $t\ge0$.

For every0<l<=L and0<rho_max<358811/13673160 there is delta(l,L,rho_max)>0 such that ordinary separately bias-corrected Adam at beta1=.9,beta2=.999,epsilon outside sqrt,standard zero moments,lambda1,lambda2 in[l,L],eta>0 and0<epsilon/eta<=rho_max*min(lambda1,lambda2) has limsup_t |eta C_active-38|>=delta for almost every full-dimensional initialization. Hence p>1 fails eventual o(1/eta) tracking generically at small eta for every fixed positive eigenvalue pair; at p=1 generic nontracking holds whenever BOTH eigenvalues exceed13673160/358811. Conclusions hold simultaneously along any specified countable eta sequence under any absolutely continuous joint initialization law, without coordinate independence. All dependencies and this exact version require independent reviewer audit; constants are existential.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:84c9b60155af6907a3fecadf669c0ae2002cb0a5ecf3bfea857c31c9207a7993","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/84/84c9b60155af6907a3fecadf669c0ae2002cb0a5ecf3bfea857c31c9207a7993.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:c8400b3426940629e0987d3e44cc0c32080290cb1e304fd09f0c004c16b18142","bundle_entry_key":"small-floor-nontracking","bundle_id":"population.adam-singular-compactification-fullrank-small-floor-nontracking-009","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"adaptive optimization","draft":"w706/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.adam:adam-fullrank-small-floor-uniform-active-threshold-nontracking-p-greater-than-one","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"T421-W706-021 v5; target1; kind narrowed; proof (unaudited).

STATEMENT
Fix 0<l<=L<infinity and 0<rho_max<rho_star=358811/13673160.
There exists delta(l,L,rho_max)>0 such that for every
lambda1,lambda2 in[l,L], eta>0 and
 0<epsilon/eta<=rho_max*min(lambda1,lambda2), ordinary
time0 separately bias-corrected Adam with b=9/10,d=999/1000, epsilon
outside sqrt and standard m0=v0=0, on H=diag(lambda1,lambda2), satisfies

 limsup_t |eta*C_active,t-38| >= delta(l,L,rho_max)        (1)

for Lebesgue-almost every initial position in R^2. Distinct eigenvalues
are allowed; no independence of the initialization coordinates is assumed.
The constant is existential, not a computer-evaluated bound.

For epsilon=eta^p and ANY fixed p>1 and fixed positive eigenvalues,
epsilon/eta eventually satisfies this condition. For any specified
countable eta_n->0 and any absolutely continuous initialization law,
(1) therefore holds simultaneously almost surely for all sufficiently
large n. This refutes eventual o(1/eta) active-threshold tracking on this
whole positive-definite two-coordinate small-floor range. It does not
identify the attracting dynamics, a limiting average, or a limit for
the curvature itself.

P=1 CONSEQUENCE
When epsilon=eta, rho_i=1/lambda_i. If BOTH eigenvalues are strictly
larger than lambda_star=13673160/358811, choose
 max_i(1/lambda_i)<rho_max<rho_star.
The theorem applies and gives generic full-dimensional nontracking.
Thus it covers the entire open p=1 range in which both scalar cycles
are hyperbolic with two unstable directions. The neutral endpoint and
mixed stable/unstable cycle ranges are not asserted. The p>1 consequence
above is unchanged and holds for every fixed positive eigenvalue pair.

AUDIT / DEPENDENCIES
This is an UNAUDITED candidate. It depends on015v3's corrected scalar
countable cycle basin and uniform capture, and019v1/020v1's extraction of
strictness from Fong--Yang's primary H.5 proof. The new work is a compact
closed-relation lift through the singular epsilon/eta=0 limit, relation
chain compression, and the origin margin. Each is supplied below. The
source H.5 inequalities have not been formally verified here. A reviewer
failure of one of these steps invalidates the global claim; origin
algebra alone does not prove it. No source-priority claim is made.

1. UNIFORM COMPACT LIFT
Put c=1/19,nu=1/1000,gamma=9/19,r=epsilon/eta. In coordinate i set

 y=x/(c eta), mu=m/(c eta lambda), V=v/(c eta lambda)^2,
 e=r/(c lambda), z=y_previous, s=sqrt(V)+e.

Use the compact parameter domain lambda_i in[l,L],0<=r<=rho_max*L,
with r<=rho_max*lambda_i for both coordinates. Then
0<=rho_i=r/lambda_i<=rho_max and 0<=e_i<=19*rho_max<1/2. Parameter r=0
will be used only as a compactification, not as an actual Adam run.
For actual r>0 define q=z/s. The raw variance history gives
V>=nu*z^2, and therefore |q|<=1/sqrt(nu)<32.

The absorbing argument of023 Section1 works without a subcritical
assumption and uniformly in r: in X=x/eta coordinates increments are
bounded by80, the corrected first-moment lag bound is720, every X enters
[-801,801], and raw moments have limsup bounds801 and801^2. Let
R=19*802. Every lifted actual tail lies in the fixed compact domain

 |y|,|z|<=R, 0<=V<=R^2, |q|<=32,
 V>=nu*z^2, q*(sqrt(V)+e)=z.                              (2)

Add a discrete branch label ell in{low,high}; low requires s>=1 and
high requires s<=1. At s=1 these are TWO distinct lifted states. This
keeps the potential continuous on the lifted domain instead of asserting
the false continuity recorded in018. Define the continuous functions

 Gamma(V,e)=8*gamma/3*min(sqrt(V),1-e)^3,
 phi_low=-c/2*(y-z)^2-Gamma,
 phi_high=(y^2-b*z^2)/(1+b)-(y+q-z)^2/2-Gamma.             (3)

Continuity is on the compact labeled domain (2); both formulas are
polynomials in y,z,q plus a continuous Gamma. The label copies need
not agree at s=1. Positions and q bounds make phi uniformly bounded.

2. A CLOSED COMPACT EDGE RELATION
For each coordinate an edge from a lifted state to a primed state has
an auxiliary number u satisfying

 V'=dV+nu*y^2, z'=y,
 u*s'=s, u>=0, d*u^2<=1,
 y'=y+b*u*(y-z)-(1+b)*q'.                               (4)

Both endpoints satisfy(2), so q'*s'=y. On a high-labeled source also
require s'<=31/5. For regular s,s'>0, these are exactly source equations
105/118 and F1/F2/F3, with p=1/s,w=1/s',u=w/p. The F3 bound is stronger
than w>c since31/5<19. It follows for every bounded full physical orbit
by unrolling its history, as019 Section1 shows:

 s' <=(1+b)*sqrt(d/(d-b^2))+e <3*(1+b)+1/2=31/5

when p>=1. The disappearing initial-momentum term is taken to zero
along a bounded full history, not estimated using 1/e uniformly in time.

Let
 W_i=(q_i')^2-2*y_i*q_i',
 Psi_i=phi_i'-phi_i-W_i,
 D=sum_i lambda_i*y_i*q_i'.
Require Psi_i>=0 for each i, and the active-band condition

 |sum_i lambda_i*W_i| <= c*delta*D.                       (5)

D>=0 follows from q_i'*s_i'=y_i and s_i'>=0. These constraints define
a closed relation R_(lambda,r,delta) on the product compact lift.
The existential u variables range in a compact interval, so projection
preserves closedness. The family is jointly closed in lambda in[l,L]^2,
r in[0,rho_max*L] with r<=rho_max*lambda_i, and bounded delta>=0. The source potential inequality
is included as Psi_i>=0; its applicability to actual limiting edges
is proved next, and its equality cases on all allowed regular edges
are checked in Section4.

The work expression has no singular denominator. In ordinary states
q_i'=w_i,next*y_i, so W_i=y_i^2*w_i,next*(w_i,next-2), and

 eta*C_active=(1/c)*sum_i lambda_i*(q_i')^2 / D.

Thus(5) is exactly the multiplied width-delta threshold inequality,
extended as0<=0 if the full gradient vanishes.

3. FIXED-POSITIVE-r CORRECTED OMEGA SETS ARE CONTAINED AND CHAIN TRANSITIVE
Here r>0 is fixed FIRST. On the physical absorbing box, the corrected
maps converge uniformly to uncorrected maps because denominators have
the fixed positive floor r/lambda_i. No uniform clock bound as r->0
is needed. We take an omega limit for each fixed r, and only THEN
allow a sequence of r values to approach zero.

Lift the actual tail using its current and previous positions, raw V,
q=z/(sqrt(V)+e), and the actual branch label (low at equality).
Every limit of adjacent lifted pairs satisfies(4): the source two-step
recursion is the uniform fixed-r limit after the clocks vanish. Extract
a bounded full physical orbit through such a pair from shifted original
histories. Its F3 bound is uniform as in Section2. The actual labels may
limit to either copy at s=1, but the closed-branch source inequalities
still give Psi_i>=0: the finite-curvature boundary checks in020 Section2
apply to each of the four branch closures. All other identities are
continuous. If the corrected active curvature eventually lies in the
width-delta band, (5) holds on every adjacent-pair limit as well.

Let K be the nonempty compact omega-limit of this lifted sequence.
Every adjacent-pair limit lies in R intersect(K x K). Every point of K
has both an incoming and outgoing edge there (extract preceding/following
states); by compact diagonal extraction it lies on a full path in K.
The distance of adjacent late pairs to this compact restricted relation
tends to zero, since any counterexample subsequence has a limit there.

K is internally chain transitive for this RESTRICTED CLOSED RELATION.
An epsilon-chain consists of true edges(a_j,b_j) in the relation, first
source a_0=x, jumps d(b_j,a_(j+1))<epsilon and final jump d(b_last,y)<epsilon.
For x,y in K choose late visits near x with their following states
converging to some v in R(x) intersect K. Use (x,v) as first edge. Follow
the actual late segment until a later visit near y, replacing each
adjacent pair by a nearby true restricted edge. All gaps are small and
all edges have endpoints in K. The last target jumps to y. This proves
internal chain transitivity without assuming a discontinuous label lift
preserves a single-valued continuous map.

4. ZERO-MARGIN FULL PATHS, INCLUDING THE SINGULAR ORIGIN
At regular scalar states s>0, the next s' is also positive: if e=0,V>0,
then V'>=dV>0. Source H.5's six-case algebra and the strict boundary
checks of019/020 apply. They use only(2),(4),F3 and e>=0; for finite
p,w the inequalities extend to e=0. In particular the smallest cubic
contribution was already bounded by its e=0 value in source Eq126.
The speed endpoint u=d^(-1/2) is treated by the y=0 case; if y!=0 it
is strict. Zero margin can therefore occur only at a scalar cycle,
at a regular origin (e>0), or on the pure-variance axis y=z=q=0
with p,w<=1. All the rational strictness gaps are those checked in
logs/stationary_margin_exact.json. At p or w equal1, use the labeled
closed-branch expressions checked in020, not continuity between copies.

The new singular case is s=0. It forces e=V=z=0, but y may initially
be nonzero (a spike following an origin). First take y=0. Then V'=0,
s'=0 and the high label is forced at both endpoints. Put h=q'. Equation
(4) gives y'=-(1+b)*h. Equations(3) yield exactly

 phi=-q^2/2,
 phi'=(1+b-b^2/2)*h^2,
 W=h^2,
 Psi=(b-b^2/2)*h^2+q^2/2=99*h^2/200+q^2/2.              (6)

Thus a zero-margin origin edge has q=h=0 and y'=0. This calculation
uses no floating-point estimate; check_origin_margin.py verifies it.

A scalar state with V=0,y!=0 cannot occur on a full zero-margin path.
Its predecessor has V_previous=0 and y_previous=0 by the nonnegative
variance recursion. That predecessor is an origin edge of(6), and zero
margin would prohibit the nonzero next position. Likewise a positive
pure-variance axis state leaves the zero-margin set in finite time:
V decreases geometrically until w crosses1, when the Gamma decrease or
the above-one case is strict. At e=0 it also crosses1 in finite time.

Consequently the only FULL scalar paths with Psi=0 at every edge are
the origin and exact two-cycle. In the lift the cycle phases are

 y=+/-a, z=-y, V=a^2, q=-2*y, ell=high,
 a=1/2-e,

and the origin has y=z=V=q=0,ell=high. The two-coordinate full
zero-margin paths are their nine product states. These statements apply
to every edge allowed by the broad relation, not only actual Adam paths.

5. EXACT-BAND FULL PATHS HAVE FINITELY MANY ACYCLIC CRITICAL ENDS
Now set delta=0. On every allowed product edge, (5) gives sum lambda_i W_i=0,
and therefore for the CONTINUOUS lifted function H=sum_i lambda_i*phi_i,

 H'-H=sum_i lambda_i*Psi_i>=0.                            (7)

Take any full path in a compact restricted relation with incoming and
outgoing edges at every point. Boundedness of H gives limits at both
time ends and Psi_i->0 there. Shift along any convergent subsequence
at either end and extract a full limiting path. Continuity of H and
closedness of the relation force Psi_i=0 on all its edges. Section4
therefore puts both end-limit sets among the nine critical product states.

At a critical product state its exact-band outgoing edge is unique.
A regular cycling coordinate has its usual next cycle phase and work0.
Each origin coordinate could algebraically have a singular h=q' at r=0,
but its work is h^2. The total exact work constraint forces every such
h to vanish. Thus critical product edges are precisely the fixed-origin
and the four period-two groups. Compactness/closedness then prevents a
tail approaching this finite set from jumping between different groups.
The full path approaches one critical orbit at each end.

H has one value at both phases of each critical orbit. At the scalar
cycle it is c*a^2-(8*gamma/3)*a^3, and at the origin it is0. There are
only finitely many product values. If a full path is not itself a
critical orbit, some Psi_i is positive at some edge by Section4, so(7)
implies STRICT increase between its two critical end values. Hence the
possible connecting paths are acyclic in a finite ordering.

6. CONTINUOUS SUPERLEVEL SETS GIVE A RELATIVE ATTRACTOR
Let K be compact, every point admitting incoming/outgoing restricted
edges, and internally chain transitive for the exact-band relation.
Choose h_max, the largest H value among critical periodic orbits in K.
At least one exists by Section5. Choose h<h_max above every smaller
critical value (if there is no smaller value, any h<h_max works).
The closed set
 U={z in K:H(z)>=h}
is positively invariant by(7). Let A be its maximal invariant subset,
 A=intersection_(n>=0) R^n(U).
The sets R^n(U) are nested nonempty compact sets. A is fully invariant;
compact diagonal extraction supplies a full path in U through each of
its points (also Akin2307.03815v1 Corollary2.6).

Every full path in A has both critical ends in U. The only critical
orbits in U have value h_max, so a noncritical such path would violate
the strict end ordering in Section5. Therefore A is exactly the finite
union of critical orbits of value h_max. In particular A subset int_K(U).
Nested compactness implies that for some finite N,
 R^N(U) subset int_K(U): otherwise select a point of each nested image
outside int(U) and obtain a point of A there, contradiction.

If K is not A, it has a point x outside U. Indeed if U=K, full invariance
would give A=K. Construct a one-step trapping neighborhood W containing U
and excluding x as follows. Put W0=U. Work backwards from N-1 to1,

# Relative attractor construction for exact-band rigidity
Supplement to T421-W706-021 v5 Section6. Kind:special; target1.
Status: proof (unaudited). This verifies an abstract implication, conditional
on the full-path classification and strict end ordering of021 Section5.
It is not an independent proof of those source-dependent inputs.

HYPOTHESES. K is a nonempty compact metric space, R a closed subset of K times K,
and every point has at least one incoming and outgoing R-edge in K.
A continuous H:K->R is nondecreasing on edges. There are finitely many
critical periodic orbits. Every full doubly infinite path approaches one
such orbit at each time end. If a full path is not itself critical, its
forward critical end has STRICTLY larger H value than its backward end.
Each critical state has a unique outgoing edge, its ordinary successor.
The R-chain convention is true edges followed by small jumps, including
a final small jump to the desired endpoint, as in021 Section3.

CONCLUSION. If K is internally chain transitive, it is one critical orbit.

1. Closed relations and nested images.
For compact C subset K, R(C) is compact as the projection of the compact
set R intersect (C times K). Moreover for nested nonempty compact C_n,
 R(intersection_n C_n)=intersection_n R(C_n).
The forward inclusion is immediate. For the reverse, fix y in every
R(C_n). Its possible predecessors in C_n form nested nonempty compact
sets. Their intersection supplies a predecessor in intersection C_n.
No lower semicontinuity or continuous selection is used.

Choose h_max, the largest critical H value in K, and h<h_max above all
smaller critical values. At least one critical orbit exists by taking a
full path through any point; compactness supplies the stated end orbits
in K. Set U={H>=h}, with interiors always relative to K. It is nonempty,
compact and positively invariant. C_n=R^n(U), n>=0, are nested nonempty
compact sets: R(U) subset U by monotonicity, and every point has an outgoing
edge. Their intersection A satisfies R(A)=A by the preceding identity.
In particular each point of A has incoming and outgoing edges in A, and
one can recursively choose a full path in A through it. Positive-time
choices remain in A; predecessor choices use R(A)=A.

Every such full path has both end orbits in U, necessarily at level
h_max. Strict end ordering excludes every noncritical full path. Thus
A consists exactly of the union of critical orbits at level h_max.
Conversely each such orbit is contained in every R^n(U), because it has
arbitrarily long predecessors in that orbit. Therefore A subset int_K U,
since its H value is strictly greater than h.

2. Finite entry into the interior and one-step trapping.
Some N>=1 satisfies C_N subset int_K U. Otherwise the nested nonempty
compact sets C_n intersect (K minus int_K U) have a common point, which
would belong to A outside int_K U. If K!=A then some x in K lies outside
U: if U=K, seriality in both directions gives R(K)=K and A=K. Since U
is compact and x is outside, its distance from x is positive.

We use the following upper-neighborhood fact: if C is compact and
R(C) subset O for an open O, then a sufficiently small closed metric
neighborhood N_eta(C) in K satisfies R(N_eta(C)) subset O. Otherwise
choose eta_n->0 and edges with source tending to C and target outside O.
A convergent subsequence and closedness give an edge from C to K minus O,
contradiction. Closed metric neighborhoods are compact here.

If N=1 use W=U. If N>1, work backward j=N-1,...,1. Given an open
neighborhood O of C_(j+1), the upper-neighborhood fact permits a compact
neighborhood W_j of C_j with R(W_j) subset O and excluding x. Start
with O=int_K U and subsequently use O=int_K W_(j+1). Each C_j is a
subset of U, so x can always be excluded. Taking W_0=U gives
 R(W_(N-1)) subset int_K U,
 R(W_j) subset int_K W_(j+1), 1<=j<N-1,
 R(U)=C_1 subset int_K W_1.
Thus W=union_(j=0)^(N-1) W_j is compact, contains A, excludes x, and
 R(W) subset int_K W.
U itself need not be a neighborhood of all of U; only its interior
containing C_N and A is used. This avoids a hidden openness assumption.

3. Chains cannot escape.
R(W) and K minus int_K W are disjoint compact sets and both are
nonempty when needed; their distance gamma is positive. A relation
chain whose first source is in A remains in W when every jump is less
than gamma: an edge with source in W has target in R(W), and any such
jump lands in int_K W. The same gap prevents its final jump from reaching
x outside W. This contradicts internal chain transitivity. Hence K=A.
On A, true edges follow the unique critical successors. The finite set
of distinct critical orbits has positive separation; chains with smaller
jumps cannot switch orbits. Internal chain transitivity leaves one orbit.

APPLICATION / LIMITS. The closed compact relation, monotone H and unique
critical edges in021 meet the structural hypotheses only subject to their
own proofs. The hardest input still to audit is Section5: all full path
end limits are the nine critical states, with strict ordering for a
noncritical path. This note closes neither that input nor the entire
frontier target. The finite three-state check exercises a strictly
specified discrete analogue; it is not a certificate for the continuum.

edge. This note does not present that calculation as new or rerun it.

 V'=d*V+(1-d)*y^2, z'=y, q'*s'=y,

from positive variances; u>0 follows from u*s'=s; and b>0 is a hypothesis.

constant positive pure variance is a bounded full path. If boundedness
or full negative-time history is removed, the forward orbit above is
not excluded. The lemma does not exclude limit states reached by
one-sided paths unless a full bounded limiting history has been obtained.

Supplement to T421-W706-021 v5; kind special; target1.

HYPOTHESES, NOT CONCLUSIONS OF COMPACTNESS
Use the compact labelled lifted relation R of021, or any compact closed
relation with the following properties. Parameters are constant along
paths and range in a compact set with0<=e_i<=e_max<1/2 and positive

bounded. All scalar edges obey069's equations with b=.9,d=.999.

Let s_i=sqrt(V_i)+e_i and similarly s_i_prime, with physical curvature
variables p_i=1/s_i,w_i=1/s_i_prime whenever these speeds are positive.
Fix sigma>0. Let C_sigma be the closed subset of R on which at least one
coordinate has s_i,s_i_prime>=sigma and either s_i=1 or s_i_prime=1.
All labels are retained as distinct copies, as in070/074.

1. NO BOUNDED FULL ZERO-DISSIPATION PATH MEETS C_sigma.

If both speeds are1,070 makes its Psi strictly positive. Otherwise074
makes it strictly positive except for the explicit low-source target-
threshold pure-variance equality. That exception has y=z=q=0 and
V=(1-e)^2/d>0 at its source. The relation q*s=z implies q=0 since
s>0. Lemma069 excludes this state on any bounded full physical path.
All cases contradict zero dissipation. This argument uses no assertion
that individual work terms W_i vanish, and uses no023 audit.

The regularity trim is essential to this statement's scope. No claim is
made here for s_i=0 or s_i_prime=0; those singular edges still require
the main021 origin analysis. Nor does this classify full zero-Psi paths
that stay in the interiors of the labelled branches.

2. UNIFORM FINITE-WINDOW PAYMENT.
Put D(edge)=sum_i lambda_i*Psi_i(edge)>=0, continuous on compact R.
There are an integer N>=1 and epsilon>0 such that every finite R path
(z_n) for -N<=n<=N+1 whose central edge lies in C_sigma satisfies
 sum_{n=-N}^N D(z_n,z_(n+1))>=epsilon.                    (1)
If there is no such finite path, the assertion is vacuous.

Otherwise, if no N,epsilon exist, for each integer j>=1 select an
R path on[-j,j+1] with central edge in C_sigma and total D<1/j.
Compactness of the state and auxiliary edge spaces and a countable
diagonal subsequence yield a full limit R path on all integers. Every

Psi_i on that limit edge is zero. Closedness keeps its central edge
in C_sigma. This contradicts Section1, proving(1). This is a finite-sum
positivity argument followed by a diagonal limit, not a product of
conditional probabilities or an independence assertion.

 Psi=99*(q')^2/200+q^2/2.

# Corrected lifted edge limits and omega-set chains
Kind: special; target:1. Status: proof (unaudited).
Supporting argument for056 Section3, with a direct F3 derivation.
It does not independently audit the source potential inequalities or021.

1. The exact corrected recurrence and its limiting edge.
Fix eta>0, positive lambda_i and r=epsilon/eta>0. In one coordinate
use056's normalization c=1/19,b=9/10,d=999/1000,nu=1-d,
 y_t=x_t/(c eta), mu_t=m_t/(c eta lambda),
 V_t=v_t/(c eta lambda)^2, e=r/(c lambda)>0,
 z_t=y_(t-1), s_t=sqrt(V_t)+e, q_t=z_t/s_t.
Assume the actual tail and raw moments lie in a fixed bounded box;
this note does not re-prove the absorbing box. For t>=1 put
 kappa_t=(1-b^t)*(sqrt(V_t/(1-d^t))+e).
The position update at the PREVIOUS step gives exactly
 mu_t=-c*kappa_t*(y_t-z_t).
The raw recurrences mu_(t+1)=b*mu_t+(1-b)*y_t and
 V_(t+1)=d*V_t+nu*y_t^2 therefore imply
 y_(t+1)=y_t+b*(kappa_t/kappa_(t+1))*(y_t-z_t)
              -(1+b)*y_t/kappa_(t+1).                 (1)
Here (1-b)/c=1+b exactly; the clocks in kappa_(t+1) have index t+1.
On the bounded box kappa_t-s_t tends uniformly to zero at fixed e>0.
Indeed the sqrt clock factor tends to1, and its uncorrected argument
is uniformly bounded. For all sufficiently large t, kappa_t>=e/2.
All divisions in (1) thus pass to adjacent-pair limits. Every limiting
edge satisfies
 V'=dV+nu*y^2, z'=y, q'*s'=y, u=s/s',
 y'=y+b*u*(y-z)-(1+b)*q'.                             (2)
Also V>=nu*z^2, qs=z, u>=0 and d*u^2<=1, since
 s'>=sqrt(d)*sqrt(V)+e>=sqrt(d)*s.
Labels are part of a finite discrete coordinate: low at s>=1, high at
s<=1. At s=1 the two copies remain distinct. Label limits satisfy
these closed constraints; continuity of a single-valued label map is
neither asserted nor needed.

2. F3 from the bounded full gradient history.
Through any adjacent-pair limit, diagonal extraction of shifted raw
(y,mu,V) histories supplies a bounded doubly infinite uncorrected path.
Its moment recurrences unroll to the absolutely convergent formulas
 mu_t=(1-b)*sum_(j>=0) b^j*y_(t-1-j),
 V_t=nu*sum_(j>=0) d^j*y_(t-1-j)^2.                   (3)
Boundedness makes the discarded remainders b^n*mu_(t-n) and
d^n*V_(t-n) tend to zero. The past-step position equation is
 y_t=y_(t-1)-mu_t/(c*s_t).
Write B=1+b, s=s_t, V=V_t. In this linear functional of the past
positions the coefficient for j=0 is 1-B/s and for j>=1 is
 -B*b^j/s. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz, with positive weights d^j and
b^2<d, gives
 nu*y_t^2 <= V*[1-2B/s+B^2*d/(s^2*(d-b^2))].          (4)
The bracket is the sum of squared functional coefficients divided
by d^j; in particular it is nonnegative. This is a deterministic
Hilbert-space inequality, not a concentration or independence argument.
The geometric series used is sum_(j>=1)(b^2/d)^j=b^2/(d-b^2).
Adding dV to (4), using V=(s-e)^2<=s^2 and positivity of the
resulting coefficient, yields
 V_(t+1) <= (1+d)*s^2-2B*s+B^2*d/(d-b^2).
For a high source 0<s<=1 and 1+d<2B, so its first two terms have
nonpositive sum. Consequently
 s'<=B*sqrt(d/(d-b^2))+e <3B+1/2=31/5                 (5)
whenever e<1/2. The square-root comparison uses d/(d-b^2)<9.
All constants in (5) are independent of the positive lower bound on e.
At e=0 singular source states are not derived by dividing by s here:
when parameters later tend to that boundary, the closed bound s'<=31/5
is inherited from these fixed-positive-e limiting edges instead.

3. Passing the active band without dividing at zero gradient.
With the post-variance-update convention in056, define
 qbar_i=y_i/(sqrt(V_i'/(1-d^(t+1)))+e_i),
 Dbar=sum_i lambda_i*y_i*qbar_i.
When the active quotient is defined its width-delta inequality is
 |sum_i lambda_i*(qbar_i^2-2*y_i*qbar_i)|<=c*delta*Dbar.
At fixed positive e_i, qbar_i-q_i' tends uniformly to zero on the
bounded box. Thus adjacent-pair limits obey the same multiplied band
with q_i'. This passage remains valid when the limiting gradient is
zero: no division by a limiting D is made. The statement here uses
exactly this timing convention; a different preconditioner timing
requires its own identification before applying this formula.

4. A compact-sequence lemma: restricted edge limits are chain transitive.
Let a_n be ANY sequence in a compact metric space, K its nonempty omega
set and G the set of all limits of pairs (a_n,a_(n+1)) as n->infinity.
Then G is compact and contained in K times K. Every point of K has an
incoming and an outgoing G-edge, by extraction of its predecessor or
successor along a subsequence. Also dist((a_n,a_(n+1)),G)->0; otherwise
a counterexample subsequence has a convergent pair limit belonging to G.

Fix x,y in K and epsilon>0. Choose h>0 with 2h<epsilon. Along a
subsequence a_n->x also extract a_(n+1)->v, giving the TRUE edge (x,v).
Choose n sufficiently late that dist(a_(n+1),v)<h and every later pair
is within h of G in the max product metric. Choose a later m>=n+2
with dist(a_m,y)<h. For j=n+1,...,m-1 replace the pair
(a_j,a_(j+1)) by an edge (A_j,B_j) of G within h.
Begin with (x,v). Its jump to A_(n+1) is <2h. Consecutive replacement
edges have jumps dist(B_j,A_(j+1))<2h, as does the last target's jump
to y. Thus this is an epsilon-chain with first source EXACTLY x,
all true edges and endpoints in K, and an allowed final jump to y.
There is no accumulated error and no uniform bound on m-n is required.
Therefore K is internally chain transitive for G and for every closed
relation restricted to K that contains G. This does not require
continuity of the label lift or of an underlying map.

5. Application boundary: what is CLEAN and what remains separate.
CLEAN for the compact-sequence lemma and the corrected algebra/F3
calculations above: their hypotheses, indices, inequality directions
and constants re-derive. For the actual lifted sequence, Sections1-3
place G in the physical and band constraints of056, assuming its
bounded box and its stated active-curvature timing convention.
The FIRST additional assertion not re-derived in this note is
 Psi_i=phi_i'-phi_i-W_i>=0 for every limiting labeled branch edge.

[Lemma lem:local-max of arXiv:2608.23135, 'Graph distance and effective resistance of the random walk trace in four and five dimensio'] There exist constants $C_1,C_2<\infty$, depending only on $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$, such that
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{P}\left(
\exists 1\le j\le M:
\max_{u_{j-1}\le r\le s\le u_j}X[r,s]> C_1\mathbb{E}[\Delta_n]
\right)
\le C_2(\log n)^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, outside an event of probability $O((\log n)^{-1})$,
\begin{equation}

\max_{u_{j-3}\le r\le s\le u_j}X[r,s]
\le C'_1\mathbb{E}[\Delta_n]
\qquad\text{for all }3\le j\le M.
\end{equation}
Moreover, if we fix $l,q>0$,  
then for every $p>0$ there is
$K=K(p,l,q,\varepsilon,\delta)$ such that
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{P}\left(
\exists r\le M:
\max_{u_r- l a_n^{(q)} \le s\le t\le u_r+{ la_n^{(q)}}}
X[s,t]
> K\mathbb{E}[X_{l a_n^{(q)}}]
\right)
\le (\log n)^{-p}.
\end{equation}
title: Lemma lem:local-max of arXiv:2608.23135

body: [Proposition prop:bounded_hausdorff of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Fix $\kappa \in (0,4)$ and $a,b \in \mathbf{R}$ with $a+b > -2\lambda$.  Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $\mathbf{H}$ with boundary conditions given by $-a$ on $\mathbf{R}_-$ and $b$ on $\mathbf{R}_+$.  For each $\theta \in \mathbf{R}$ we let $\eta_\theta$ be the flow line of $h$ from~$0$ to~$\infty$ with angle $\theta$.  Then~$\eta_\theta$ converges to~$\mathbf{R}_+$ in probability in the bounded Hausdorff metric as $\theta \downarrow -(\lambda+b)/\chi$. Furthermore, for any $\delta_0, p \in (0,1)$ and $R > 0$, there exists $\theta_0 > -(\lambda + b)/\chi$ (depending only on $\kappa$, $R$, $\delta_0$, $p$, $a$, and $b$) such that for any $\theta \in (-(\lambda+b)/\chi, \theta_0)$ the following holds with probability at least $1-p$: for each $x \in [0,R]$, there exists $y \in \eta_\theta \cap [0,R]$ such that $\n{x-y} \leq \delta_0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 47 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \((U,h)\) be a smooth Riemannian manifold, and let
\(H_i,H:U\to\R^k\) be smooth maps with
\(H_i\to H\) in \(C^\infty_{\rm loc}\).  Suppose that \(0\) is a regular
value of \(H\), and set \(S=H^{-1}(0)\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item If \(K\Subset\operatorname{int}K^+\Subset S\) are compact
domains, then, for all large \(i\), \(H_i^{-1}(0)\) contains a small
normal graph \(K_i\) over \(K\), and \(K_i\to K\) smoothly.
\item If \(S\) is compact and is the entire zero set of \(H\) in a
precompact tubular neighbourhood \(U_0\Subset U\), then, for all large
\(i\), \(H_i^{-1}(0)\cap U_0\) contains a compact boundaryless normal
graph \(S_i\) over \(S\).  Moreover, \(S_i\to S\) smoothly and
\(S_i\cong S\).
\end{enumerate}
If Riemannian metrics \(h_i\) on \(U\) converge smoothly to \(h\), the
induced metrics and volume forms on these graphs converge smoothly. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop Sgn of arXiv:2609.00672, 'Deciding superellipticity and computing the Weierstrass normal form'] Let $g\ge 2$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\mathcal S_{g,n}=\emptyset$ for $n>2g+2$.
\item For $g+2<n\le 2g+2$, the locus $\mathcal S_{g,n}$ is empty unless $n\in\{2g+1,2g+2\}$, and then it consists of the single point $y^n=x^2-1$, which lies in the hyperelliptic locus.

\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 12 of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Follow the same setup and notation as \Cref{lem:subgaussian-kahane-khintchine} with $H \coloneqq H^1(\mathcal{I};\mathbb{K})$ and $\mathbb{K} = \R$ or $\C$. 
There exist $c,C>0$ such that for all $m\in\N$ and $u\geq0$, we have
\begin{align}
        \P\Big(
        \max_{0\le k\le m}\|S_k\|_\infty>u
        \Big)
        \le
        Ce^{-cu^2/\sigma_m^2}\,.
\end{align}
where we use the convention that $1/\sigma_m^2 \coloneqq 0$ when $\sigma_m = 0$.
Moreover, for all $\lambda,K>0$, there exists $C_\lambda<\infty$ (also depending on $K$) such
that whenever $\sigma_m \in [0,K]$, we have
\begin{align}
        \E\big[\exp( \lambda \max_{0\leq k\leq m} \|S_k\|_\infty)\big]-1
        \leq
        C_\lambda\sigma_m .
\end{align}

Method: Asymptotic total length of finite SIRSN samples structural attempt Result: A local truncation argument gives the lower bound liminf E length/k>=ell. Tile the bulk of the large square by unit cells. For fixed R and M, retain in each cell only the length, truncated at M, of routes between sampled endpoints within distance R of that cell. Its local binomial point configuration converges in total variation to the corresponding rate1 Poisson configuration. The retained length is bounded by M, so its expectation converges. Summing disjoint unit-cell contributions and then taking k to infinity gives the Poisson local truncated expectation as a lower bound. Let M and then R increase: monotone convergence recovers the full sampled-network intensity ell. Check: Only a bounded endpoint region is used before taking k to infinity; its binomial count tends to a Poisson count and conditional positions have the same uniform law. Truncation avoids any unproved uniform-integrability step. Boundary cells are an asymptotically negligible fraction for fixed R. Obstruction: This proves no upper bound on total length. Rare paths can leave the sampling square by a large distance, and their exterior contribution is absent from the local lower-bound argument. Controlling those excursions remains necessary for equality.

[Corollary 7 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\equiv c>0$ and $V\in C_b(\R)$. Then
\[
\alpha d\,\cH\!\left(\frac{c}{\alpha d}\right)-\sup_\R V
\le\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)\le
\alpha d\,\cH\!\left(\frac{c}{\alpha d}\right)-\inf_\R V.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)}{|\log\alpha|}\longrightarrow\frac{c}{R_+}
\qquad(\alpha\downarrow0).
\]
Under the edge hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:heteroHamiltonian},
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)
=\frac{c}{R_+}\left[\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}
+p\log\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}-p\log R_+-\log(R_+A)-1\right]+O(1).
\]
If, in addition, $V\equiv a_0$, then
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)=\alpha d\,\cH\!\left(\frac{c}{\alpha d}\right)-a_0
=\sup_{s\in\R}\{cs-\alpha d(M(s)-1)\}-a_0.
\]
If $s_\alpha>0$ is the optimizer, then $\alpha dM'(s_\alpha)=c$ and
\[
(\Lambda_D^\R)'(\alpha)=-d(M(s_\alpha)-1)<0,\qquad
(\Lambda_D^\R)''(\alpha)=\frac{c^2}{\alpha^3dM''(s_\alpha)}>0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)=-a_0+\frac{c^2}{2\alpha dD_2(J)}
-\frac{D_4(J)c^4}{24\alpha^3d^3D_2(J)^4}+O(\alpha^{-5})
\qquad(\alpha\to+\infty),
\]
and, under the edge hypothesis,
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)=\frac{c}{R_+}\left[\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}
+p\log\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}-p\log R_+-\log(R_+A)-1+o(1)\right]-a_0
\]
as $\alpha\downarrow0$. Finally, for
$\cA_{\sigma,m,\R}u=\sigma^{-m}(J_\sigma*u-u)+cu'+a_0u$,
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,\R})=\sigma^{-m}\cH(c\sigma^{m-1})-a_0.
\]

body:
Let n>=2, K>0, and let x=(x_1,...,x_n) and y=(y_1,...,y_n) be real random vectors whose 2n coordinates are mutually independent, each with a Lebesgue density bounded almost everywhere by K. Let Z be a deterministic real n by n matrix, u,v deterministic real n-vectors, and w a deterministic real scalar. Write sigma_1(Z)>=...>=sigma_n(Z)>=0 for its singular values, and assume r=rank(Z)>=2. Then Q=x^T Z y+x^T u+v^T y+w has a Lebesgue density satisfying ||p_Q||_infinity <= 2(C_RV K)^2 sqrt(2e*pi) min_{2<=j<=r} [j^(-1/2) (product_{i=1}^j sigma_i(Z))^(-1/j)], where C_RV is the universal constant in the Rudelson-Vershynin bounded-density projection theorem. Equivalently one may minimize over 2<=j<=n, interpreting terms with zero singular-value product as infinity. This is the k=1 corollary of Banks, Garza-Vargas, Kulkarni and Srivastava, arXiv:2005.08930. No bounded-density bound is available in general at rank one: if U,V are independent uniform(0,1), UV has density -log(t) on 0<t<1, which is unbounded near zero. Independence only between the two vectors is insufficient even at rank two: x=(U,U), y=(V,V), Z=diag(1,-1) gives Q=0 almost surely. A quadratic-form application must independently verify the coordinate independence and rank hypotheses.
n>=2 and K>0
All 2n coordinates of x and y are mutually independent and each has a Lebesgue density bounded a.e. by K

[Proposition prop:c2fail of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] For $\varepsilon>0$ define directions in $\mathbb{R}^4$
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_0&=-\varepsilon(e_1+e_2), & d_1&=e_1,\ d_2=e_2,\\
d_3&=-\varepsilon(e_3+e_4), & d_4&=e_3,\ d_5=e_4,\\
d_6&=-\varepsilon(e_1+e_3), & d_7&=-\varepsilon(e_2+e_4),
\end{aligned}
\]
with masses $s_0=s_3=s_6=s_7=\frac1{4(1+2\varepsilon)}$ and
$s_1=s_2=s_4=s_5=\frac{\varepsilon}{2(1+2\varepsilon)}$, realized as a
whitened system through Lemma~(lem:realize of the paper). Exactly the four points
$d_0,d_3,d_6,d_7$ are strictly $4$-generated, and the four side points
$d_1,d_2,d_4,d_5$ are not generated by the other rays at all. The exact
Mahalanobis norms are
\[
\lVert v\rVert^2=\frac{2\varepsilon(3\varepsilon+2)}{\varepsilon+1}
\ \text{(generated points)},\qquad
\lVert v\rVert^2=\frac{\varepsilon^2+4\varepsilon+2}{\varepsilon(\varepsilon+1)}
\ \text{(side points)} .
\]
For $0<\varepsilon<\frac{\sqrt{33}-3}{12}\approx0.2287$, all generated
points have $t=1/\lVert v\rVert^2>1$ and all side points have $t<1$: no point is
simultaneously cheap and generated. At $\varepsilon=\frac1{100}$ the values
are exactly $t=\frac{5050}{203}$ and $t=\frac{101}{20401}$.

body: In mathematics, the pigeonhole principle states that if n items are put into m containers, with n > m, then at least one container must contain more than one item. For example, of three gloves, at least two must be right-handed or at least two must be left-handed, because there are three objects but only two categories of handedness to put them into. This seemingly obvious statement, a type of counting argument, can be used to demonstrate possibly unexpected results. For example, given that the population of London is more than one unit greater than the maximum number of hairs that can be on a human head, the principle requires that there must be at least two people in London who have the same number of hairs on their heads.
title: Pigeonhole principle

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:cd7babe876c3357d888afeb8ef19c6394e317abef58a458426469b0be2afe042","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/cd/cd7babe876c3357d888afeb8ef19c6394e317abef58a458426469b0be2afe042.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:5d544a0cbc0f2ffed98a3664ea50e70ceeb525f95c42c1200e5418673643b262","bundle_entry_key":"instance_uniform_weighted_sampler_barrier","bundle_id":"population.t410-oracle-sampling-barriers-protected-blocks-003","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"computational complexity; conditional sampling; relative entropy; autoregressive scoring","draft":"w739/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:instance_uniform_weighted_sampler_barrier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Instance-uniform sampling is incompatible with Target 2 circuit hardness

Claim C005 v1. Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: route-failure. Target: 2.
No novelty priority is claimed. This is an elementary necessary restriction
on an oracle construction, not a separation or an impossibility of C003 A.

## Exact hypothesis

Fix an oracle O. Suppose there is one randomized oracle algorithm U which,
given an explicit description of any deterministic oracle circuit C on m bits,
with output in {0,1,4} and positive total weight, samples a distribution within
total variation 1/10 of the law assigning probability C(z)/sum C to z.
Its time and randomness are bounded by one polynomial in the description
length and m. The quantifier includes circuits containing a fixed input x as
constants. Ordinary polynomial-size circuits may use O gates, in the usual
bit-query model. This is an INSTANCE-UNIFORM sampler interface.

Then NP^O is contained in RP^O, and consequently NP^O is contained in P^O/poly.
It is therefore incompatible with the circuit-hardness requirement of Target 2.

## Verifier reduction

Let A be any NP^O language, with a polynomial-time oracle verifier V(x,w)
and exactly p(|x|) witness bits after padding. Given x, construct in polynomial
time a circuit C_x with m=1+p(|x|) input bits. It assigns weight 1 to 0^m,
weight 4 to 1w when V(x,w) accepts, and zero to all other strings. The circuit
is polynomial-size: unroll the bounded verifier, with oracle gates for its
queries, and hardwire x. Its normalizer is 1+4 Z_x, where Z_x counts witnesses.
No normalizer computation is used by the reduction.

Run U on C_x. Accept only if the sampled word is 1w and V(x,w) actually
accepts. On a no input this never accepts. On a yes input the target event has
mass 4Z_x/(1+4Z_x)>=4/5. Total variation at most 1/10 leaves acceptance
probability at least 7/10. This proves A is in RP^O. The running time is
polynomial in |x| because U has one polynomial bound uniform over descriptions.

## Relativized randomized-to-advice step

For each input length n, repeat the preceding test independently k=n+2 times
and accept if any run accepts. A yes input is rejected with probability at
most (3/10)^k; a no input is never accepted. The union bound over all 2^n
inputs of length n gives probability of any mistake at most

    2^n (3/10)^(n+2) = (9/100)(3/5)^n < 1.

Thus there is one fixed polynomial-length collection of k random tapes that
works simultaneously for EVERY length-n input. Hardwire those tapes as advice
and unroll the oracle computation into a polynomial-size oracle circuit.
Only the independent repetitions on a single input were multiplied; inputs
need no independence. This proves A is in P^O/poly. The tape collection may
depend on n and O, exactly as the circuit model permits.

## Why this does not contradict C003

C003 A has quantifier form: for every fixed uniform weighted family W, there
exists a uniform polynomial-time sampler S_W. It supplies neither a computable
compiler W to S_W nor a polynomial bound uniform over weight descriptions.
In the reduction above x varies with the INSTANCE, not just with the length.
Replacing the family-specific samplers by a single sampler accepting C_x would
be an extra assumption, which is precisely what the theorem rules out.

C004 encoded a unary input into a polynomially related output length and so
did not require this additional uniformity. Encoding every binary x into its
own length requires exponentially many lengths; it does not yield a polynomial
time reduction and cannot silently convert C003 A into this stronger property.

Therefore an oracle construction for C003 must achieve family-specific
sampling without a polynomial-time instance-uniform weight-circuit interface.
It must also preserve hardness after all sampling/inversion interfaces are
available. Neither this proof nor C004 proves such a construction exists.
The joint oracle consistency problem for binary NP circuit hardness is OPEN.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:a709e45865929b025dd7f8ab22e9a633f013cb492fed61e532bf39a91f8c0201","revision_digest":"sha256:d9fe42072d4cba052697690bd26cd19d3d236739c096685e652aa411c85317b6","source_id":"own-work:T410-w739-C005-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T21:39:37.775816+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}
title: Instance-uniform weighted sampling forces NP into RP and P/poly (unaudited)

[Lemma 2 (Linearized forward equation) of arXiv:2604.00937, 'Infinite Horizon Optimal Control of Forward-Backward Stochastic Volterra Equations with De'] The process $\dot{X}$ satisfies
\begin{align*}
\dot{X}(t) &= \int_0^t \left[ \frac{\partial b}{\partial x}(t,s)\dot{X}(s) + \frac{\partial b}{\partial x_1}(t,s)\dot{X}_1(s) + \frac{\partial b}{\partial u}(t,s)\beta(s) \right] ds \\
&\quad + \int_0^t \left[ \frac{\partial \sigma}{\partial x}(t,s)\dot{X}(s) + \frac{\partial \sigma}{\partial x_1}(t,s)\dot{X}_1(s) + \frac{\partial \sigma}{\partial u}(t,s)\beta(s) \right] dB(s) \\
&\quad + \int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{R}_0} \left[ \frac{\partial \theta}{\partial x}(t,s,e)\dot{X}(s) + \frac{\partial \theta}{\partial x_1}(t,s,e)\dot{X}_1(s) + \frac{\partial \theta}{\partial u}(t,s,e)\beta(s) \right] \tilde{N}(ds,de),
\end{align*}
where $\dot{X}_1(t) = \dot{X}(t-\delta)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Linearized forward equation

body:
Own-work draft, C006 version 2, proof (unaudited); priority not established. Fix L>=3, d>=1, H=L-1, equal hidden widths m, a C2 activation with |sigma|, |sigma prime|, |sigma double prime|<=1, and data ||x||<=1, |y|<=1. Let h1_i=sigma(w_i dot x), hl_j=sigma(m^(-1)sum_i B^l_ji h(l-1)_i) for 2<=l<=H, and f=m^(-1)sum_j a_j hH_j, with half-squared population loss. Initialize two independent runs with w_i iid in [-1,1]^d, a_i iid in [-1,1] and entries of every B^l iid in [-1,1]; arrays are mutually independent and each array law is common across runs. Train all parameters by simultaneous fresh-sample SGD or finite minibatch averages, using multipliers m for a,w and m^2 for every middle matrix, with deterministic nonnegative steps summing to T<infinity. Set S2=sum eta_k^2, A=2exp(T), define M_l=1+2A^2 T product_{s=l+1}^H M_s backwards for l=H,...,2, W=sqrt(d)+2A^2 T product_{s=2}^H M_s, R=max(1,A,W,M_2,...,M_H), and r=6sqrt(d)m^(-1/(d+2))+6m^(-1/3)+6(L-2)m^(-1/2). A compatible tuple of hidden-layer permutations, selected only from the initial boundary arrays, has expected population loss-chord barrier <=8R^L exp(64L^2 R^(2L)T)[r+4L R^L sqrt(S2)]. Thus eta_max<=m^(-2/(d+2)) yields O_{L,d,T}(m^(-1/(d+2))) for every fixed depth. The boundary matchings and identity internal permutations suffice: each middle cut error adds linearly at initialization, and deterministic transpose cut estimates handle trained dependence. No bound uniform in growing depth, ReLU theorem, fixed-step independent-data limit, low-risk endpoint guarantee or independent audit is established.
All stated bounded smooth fixed-depth, fixed-horizon and independent iid initialization hypotheses
Fresh iid SGD data; deterministic steps; small-step condition required for width vanishing
title: General fixed-depth mean-field SGD permutation connectivity via cut norms (unaudited campaign draft)

body: [Theorem 4.3 of arXiv:1908.07093, 'Uniform Reliability of Self-Join-Free Conjunctive Queries'] Consider the query Q1, and let ϕ be a function mapping the relation symbols R, S, and T to rational values such that 0 < ϕ(R), ϕ(T) < 1 and 0 < ϕ(S) ≤1. Then WUR(Q1, ϕ) is #P-hard. We will prove Theorem 4.3 in Sections 5–7. Note that this result does not cover the case where relations have deterministic facts, except that we do not need to assume that ϕ(S) < 1: we will come back to this issue in Section 8.
title: Theorem 4.3 of arXiv:1908.07093: Uniform Reliability of Self-Join-Free Conjunctive Queries

body: [Theorem complete feedback optimal strategy of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] Suppose a deck of $n$ cards is given a shelf shuffle with a single shelf, and the player is given complete feedback. The player should guess card $1$ in position $1$, and the card immediately following the previously shown card in all other positions. Once one of card $n-1$ or $n$ is first shown, the player should guess the remaining cards in descending order, and is guaranteed to get these correct. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem complete feedback optimal strategy of arXiv:2507.10294

body: Let (X, Sigma_X, mu) and (Y, Sigma_Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces and let f be measurable on the product sigma-algebra of X times Y, with values in R or C. If the double integral of |f| over X times Y with respect to mu times nu is finite (f is integrable), then for a.e. x the slice y -> f(x,y) is integrable, for a.e. y the slice x -> f(x,y) is integrable, and integral_X integral_Y f dnu dmu = integral_Y integral_X f dmu dnu = integral over X times Y of f d(mu times nu). Tonelli's theorem gives the same conclusion for f merely nonnegative and measurable, integrals allowed to be +infinity.

The source has d unknown A/S context pairs, one arbitrary r-support A and one all-K S each, and N-2d known S contexts; it selects contexts uniformly then truths uniformly. Independently receive uniform ell-subsets of truths in BOTH variable contexts,ANY0<=ell<=r, and n actual iid untagged facts. Every realized generator must be source Mis_infinity<=c at exact score bins in ALL data-compatible worlds,0<=c<1/(2NrK),rational c. For each FIXED alphabet bound K0, C026 true-posterior native branch frontier and an attaining randomized robust policy are polynomial-time computable in growing d,n,N and rational budget bit size, for every verifier fraction in the coprime small-budget paired actual-iid model. Low whole contexts separate; whole choices are posterior prefixes per h; sorted-coefficient marked multiset DP solves allocation. No uniform polynomial-in-K, efficient global expectation or classical ERM/PAC claim. The C026 conditional Bayes minimum beta is min_branches,partitions(sum f*p/m-c*max f/m), where unresolved h=min union chooses paired residual (2(K-h),F,(2-h/r-h/K)/N), or F units(2,1,1/(NK)) at h=r, OR BOTH posterior-weighted whole contexts(K,F*pi,1/N),(K,F*(1-pi),1/N). Resolved A union j<r contributes(K-j,F,(r-j)/(Nr)),otherwise none. pi is the true original-data posterior defined by L(u,j)=(K/r)^u*binom(K-j,r-j)/binom(K-ell,r-ell). All lower-posterior whole contexts can be isolated. For any number of whole choices among pairs with the same h, keep the largest max(pi,1-pi) values. Enumerate those per-h prefix lengths. Remaining native types are at most2K-1. Sort selected high false counts, and candidate cell signatures by coefficient [lambda*m(s)-p(s)+e*c]/[m(s)+K*q],lambda=1/(NK),where q high whole objects and donor mark e are included. An ordered unbounded resource DP allocates contiguous high-count blocks with exactly one mark. Rearrangement and exchange arguments prove equality. This gives a polynomial-time estimator for every fixed K0 with growing VC d; polynomial degree depends on K0. Learning-policy symmetrization attains C026 global minimax E beta, without averaging generator laws. The global oracle penalty formula is unchanged. Dependence on the earlier unaudited characterization is explicit.
