body: In calculus and real analysis, the mean value theorem is a theorem about differentiable functions, roughly stating that the average rate of change of such a function over an interval is equal to the instantaneous rate of change at some point in the interval. For example, if a car smoothly travels a certain distance over a given finite time interval, then at some moment during the trip, its instantaneous speed equals its average speed for the whole trip.
title: Mean value theorem

body:
[Lem 189 (error between $Q$ and $\tilde{Q}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $Q^{\sigma,\tau}=E^{\sigma,\tau}+\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\tau}$ as given by \eqref{e:qv.covar} and \eqref{e:tQ.notIs}. Then
	\[\Big|
	\Delta E^{\sigma,\tau}(q_d)\Big| 
	\le O(1)\bigg\{
	\eta^2
	+
	\sum_{\rho\in\{\sigma,\tau\}}
	\bigg[
	\eta\bigg(
	\min\Big\{
	\Delta Q^\rho(q_d),
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^\rho(q_d)\Big\}
	\bigg)^{1/2}
	+ \Big( \Delta \bar{D}^\rho(q_d)\Big)^2
	\bigg]
	\bigg\}\]
for all $\sigma,\tau\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$.
The same bound holds with $Q^\frozen$, $\tilde{Q}^\frozen$, $E^\frozen$
in place of $Q$, $\tilde{Q}$, $E$.

\begin{proof} Recall that $\vZ\equiv \vY-\vD$, so we can rewrite \eqref{e:qv.covar} as
	\[
	\Delta Q^{\sigma,\tau}(q_d)
	= \bE \bigg[
		\Big( \Delta Y^\sigma(q_d)
			-\Delta D^\sigma(q_d)
			\Big)
		\Big(
		\Delta Y^\tau(q_d)
		-\Delta D^\tau(q_d)
		\Big)
		\,\bigg|\, \cG(q_d)
		\bigg]\,.
	\]
For simplicity of exposition, let us consider the case $\sigma=\tau=\RomI$.
Similarly to the argument for
Lemma~\ref{l:D.barD.discrep},
let $B=B(q_d,a(q_d))$ denote the bucket at time $q_d$ that contains $a(q_d)$. Lemma~\ref{l:X.Y.discrep} then tells us that $\Delta Y^\RomI(q_d)$ is within $2\eta$ of $\Delta X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))$, where
$a(q_{d+1})$ is a uniformly random sample from
$B$. Thus define $\bar{Q}^{\RomI}$ to be the process with increments
	\beq
	\Delta\bar{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d)
	= \frac{1}{|B|}
	\sum_{a\in B}
	\Big(
	\Delta X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a)-\Delta D^\RomI(q_d)
	\Big)^2
\,.
	\eeq
 It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:X.Y.discrep} that
	\[
	\Delta Q^{\RomI}(q_d)
	=\frac{1}{|B|}
	\sum_{a\in B}
	\bigg\{
	O(\eta)
	+\Delta X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a) 
	- \Delta D^{\RomI}(q_d)
	\bigg\}^2\,,\]
which allows us to bound
	\begin{align}\nonumber
	&\Big|\Delta Q^{\RomI}(q_d)
	-\Delta\bar{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d)\Big| 
	\le O(\eta^2)
	+ O(\eta)
	\frac{1}{|B|}
	\sum_{a\in B}
	\bigg|
	\Delta X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a) 
	- \Delta D^{\RomI}(q_d)\bigg|
	\\ \nonumber
	&\qquad\le O(\eta^2)
	+ O(\eta) 
	\bigg[\frac{1}{|B|}
	\sum_{a\in B}
	\Big(
	\Delta X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a) 
	- \Delta D^{\RomI}(q_d) \Big)^2\bigg]^{1/2}\\
	&\qquad\le
	O(1)\bigg\{ \eta^2+\eta 
		\Big( \Delta\bar{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d) \Big)^{1/2}\bigg\}\,.
	
	\end{align}
This shows that increments of
$Q^{\RomI}$ and $\bar{Q}^{\RomI}$ are close. We can further bound
	\begin{align}\nonumber
	&\Big|
	\Delta\bar{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d)
	-\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d)\Big| 
	=\bigg| \frac{1}{|B|}
	\sum_{a\in B}
	\bigg\{
	\Delta X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a)-\Delta D^{\RomI}(q_d)
	\bigg\}^2
	- \frac{1}{|B|}\Big(\Delta X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a)\Big)^2\bigg|
	\\ \nonumber
	&\qquad=\bigg|
	\Big(\Delta D^{\RomI}(q_d)\Big)^2
	- 2
	\Big( \Delta D^{\RomI}(q_d)\Big)
	\frac{1}{|B|}
	\sum_{a\in B}
	\Delta X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a)
	\Big)
	\bigg|\\ \nonumber
	&\qquad=\bigg|
	\Big(\Delta D^{\RomI}(q_d)\Big)^2
	-2\Big(\Delta D^{\RomI}(q_d)\Big)
	\Big(\Delta \bar{D}^{\RomI}(q_d)\Big)
	\bigg|\\
	&\qquad\le O(1)  
	\bigg\{
	\Delta \bar{D}^{\RomI}(q_d)^2
	+ \eta\Big|\Delta \bar{D}^{\RomI}(q_d)\Big| + \eta^2\bigg\}
	\le O(1)
	\max\bigg\{\Delta \bar{D}^{\RomI}(q_d)^2,\eta^2\bigg\}
	
	\,,\end{align}
having used the definition of $\bar{D}$ from \eqref{e:barD}, together with Lemma~\ref{l:D.barD.discrep}. Combining the bounds gives
	\[
	\Big|
	\Delta E^{\RomI}(q_d)\Big| 
	\le  O(1)
	\bigg\{ \eta^2 
	+\eta\Big( \Delta\tilde{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d) \Big)^{1/2}
	+\Big(\Delta \bar{D}^{\RomI}(q_d)\Big)^2
	\bigg\}\,.
	\]
Next note that \eqref{e:barQ.to.tildeQ} implies
	\[\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d)
	\le O(1)\max\bigg\{ 
	\Delta \bar{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d),
	\Delta \bar{D}^{\RomI}(q_d)^2,
	\eta^2
	\bigg\}\,.\]
Meanwhile \eqref{e:Q.to.barQ} implies that either 
$\Delta\bar{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d) \le O(\eta^2)$, in which case
$\Delta Q^{\RomI}(q_d) \le O(\eta^2)$ also,
or $\Delta\bar{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d)$ is much larger than $\eta^2$, in which case it is of the same order as
 $\Delta Q^{\RomI}(q_d)$. It follows that
	\[\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\RomI}(q_d)
	\le O(1)\max\bigg\{ 
	\Delta Q^{\RomI}(q_d),
	\Delta \bar{D}^{\RomI}(q_d)^2,
	\eta^2
	\bigg\}\ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: error between $Q$ and $\tilde{Q}$

[Lemma lem:pdf_std_norm_asymp of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $f(\bm{v})\coloneqq (2\pi)^{-d/2}e^{-\bm{v}^\intercal\bm{v} /2}$, $\bm{v} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, denote the density of the multivariate standard normal random vector $\bm{Z}$.\\
\normalfont{(a)} Let $t\mapsto \bm{\theta}(t)\in\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfy $\bm{\theta}(t) \to \bm{0}$ as $t \to \infty$. Then, $f(\bm{\theta}(t)+\bm{v}) \sim f(\bm{v})$ for any $\bm{v} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ as $t \to \infty$.\\
\normalfont{(b)} Let $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ and $(\bm{M}(s,t))_{s\in I}$ be $d \times d$ matrices such that $\bm{M}(s,t)\to\bm{I}_d$ uniformly in $s\in I$ as $t \to \infty$. Then, for any $\bm{v} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, it holds that $f(\bm{M}(s,t)\bm{v}) \sim f(\bm{v})$ uniformly in $s\in I$ as $t \to \infty$.

body: In mathematics, specifically in homology theory and algebraic topology, cohomology is a way of attaching algebraic invariants to a topological space or other mathematical object that encode its properties in a way that is often computable. Cohomology is often related to questions of whether some local property of the space is obstructed when passing to a global property. For example, the Möbius strip is not the product space of a line segment with a circle (i.e., a cylinder), but locally on any segment of the circle it resembles an ordinary rectangle (product of two line segments) without the global twist. The obstruction to making the product structure global is encoded in the first cohomology of the underlying circle, which classifies the two inequivalent ways a line can twist around a circle (an even number of twists or an odd number of twists). The fact that there are only two inequivalent ways of twisting a line around a circle is encoded in the relevant cohomology group $H^{1}(S^{1},\{+1,-1\})$ which can be computed as isomorphic to the group $\{+1,-1\}$ where $+1$ corresponds to an even number of twists, and $-1$ to an odd number.

[Theorem 135 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Consider a discrete ensemble satisfying Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta}, \ref{Assumptions_basic}, \ref{Assumptions_offcrit}, and \ref{Assumptions_analyticity} and such that the equations \eqref{eq_equations_eqs} deterministically fix the segment filling fractions and each segment contains a single band.

For any $\varepsilon>0$ and compact sets $\amsmathbb{K}_h\subset \amsmathbb C\setminus \amsmathbb{A}_h^{\mathfrak{m}}$ indexed by $h\in[H]$, there exists a sequence of positive constants $(C_n)_{n \geq 1}$ depending only on $\eps$, the compacts and the constants in the assumptions, and there exists for each $h \in [H]$ two holomorphic functions $\widetilde{W}_{1;h}^{[1]}(z)$ and $\widetilde{W}_{2;h}^{[2]}(z)$ of $z \in \amsmathbb{C} \setminus (\alpha_h,\beta_h)$ which are $O\big(\frac{1}{z^2}\big)$ as $z \rightarrow +\infty$, such that for any $n \in \amsmathbb{Z}_{> 0}$, $h_1,\ldots,h_n \in [H]$ and any $z_i\in \amsmathbb{K}_{h_i}$ for $i \in [n]$, we have
\begin{align}
 \big|W_{1;h_1}(z_1) - \widetilde{W}_{1;h_1}^{[1]}(z_1) - \N^{-1} \widetilde{W}_{1;h_1}^{[2]}(z_1)\big| & \leq C_1\,\N^{-\frac{3}{2} + \varepsilon}, \\
\big|W_{2;h_1,h_2}(z_1,z_2) - \mathcal{F}_{h_1,h_2}(z_1,z_2)\big| & \leq
C_2\,\N^{-\frac{1}{2} + \varepsilon}, \\
\forall n \geq 3,\qquad \big|W_{n;h_1,\ldots,h_n}(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\big| & \leq
C_n\,\N^{-\frac{1}{2} + \varepsilon},
\end{align}
where $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{F}}(z_1,z_2)$ is as in Section~\ref{TheopUpsec2}. The functions $\widetilde{W}_{1;h}^{[p]}(z)$  for $p \in \{1,2\}$ depend smoothly on parameters, in the following way.

Let $p \in \amsmathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. Suppose that we allow segment filling fractions and endpoints $(\hat{\boldsymbol{a}},\hat{\boldsymbol{b}},\hat{\boldsymbol{n}})$ to vary in some open of $\amsmathbb{R}^3$. Suppose that the weights $(w_h(x))_{h = 1}^{H}$, the parameters $\rho_{h,j}$, the regular part of the potentials $(U_h(x))_{h = 1}^{H}$ are $p$ times continuously differentiable with respect to $(\hat{\boldsymbol{a}},\hat{\boldsymbol{b}},\hat{\boldsymbol{n}})$ while the integers $(\iota_h^{\pm})_{h = 1}^{H}$ remain constant, and that Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta}, \ref{Assumptions_basic}, \ref{Assumptions_offcrit}, \ref{Assumptions_analyticity} hold for uniform constants and the assumption of one band per segment remain satisfied. Then $\widetilde{W}_{1;h}^{[p]}(z)$ for $p \in \{1,2\}$ are $p$ times continuously differentiable with respect to $(\hat{\boldsymbol{a}},\hat{\boldsymbol{b}},\hat{\boldsymbol{n}})$ for $z$ away from the segments, and all the partial derivatives up to order $p$ are uniformly bounded for $z$ away from the segments, with constants determined by the constants in the assumptions. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $n,d,k\in \mathbb{N}$ and let
$(\mu_r, f_{1,r},\ldots,f_{k,r})$ be a sequence such that each $\mu_r$ is an
isotropic log-concave measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
\[
f_{j,r}\in \mathcal{P}_d(\mathbb{R}^n),
\quad
\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\},\ \forall r\in\mathbb{N},
\]
and
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}f_{j,r}\,d\mu_r =0,\quad
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}f_{j,r}^2\,d\mu_r =1,
\quad
\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\},\ \forall r\in\mathbb{N}.
\]
Then there exist an isotropic log-concave measure $\mu$, polynomials
$f_1,\ldots,f_k\in\mathcal P_d(\mathbb R^n)$, and a subsequence
$\{r_\ell\}_{\ell\in \mathbb{N}}$ such that
$\mu_{r_\ell}\Rightarrow\mu$
weakly, and, for every $j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$, the coefficients of
$f_{j,r_\ell}$ converge to the coefficients of $f_j$. Moreover,
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}f_j\,d\mu =0,\quad
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}f_j^2\,d\mu =1,
\quad
\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
\]

Build a second copy W' of W such that (W, W') is exchangeable and E[W'|W] is a linear contraction of W; the linear relation gives normal approximation, Poisson approximation and concentration bounds. Ross, Remark 3.3: if X_0, X_1, ... is a stationary Markov chain reversible with respect to the underlying measure, then W = W(X_0), W' = W(X_1) is an exchangeable pair, while the linearity condition must be verified separately. Ross, Definition 3.2: the ordered pair (W, W') is an exchangeable pair if (W, W') =d (W', W); if for some 0 < a ≤ 1 it satisfies E[W'|W] = (1 − a)W, then (W, W') is an a-Stein pair. Theorem 3.7: if (W, W') is an a-Stein pair with E[W²] = 1 and Z is standard normal, then d_W(W, Z) ≤ √(Var(E[(W' − W)²|W]))/(√(2π) a) + E|W' − W|³/(3a). Theorem 4.20: if W is a non-negative integer valued random variable, (W, W') is an exchangeable pair, F is a σ-field with σ(W) ⊆ F and Z ~ Po(λ), then for all c ∈ R, d_TV(W, Z) ≤ min{1, λ^{−1/2}} (E|λ − c P(W' = W + 1 | F)| + E|W − c P(W' = W − 1 | F)|). Theorem 7.2: if (W, W') is an a-Stein pair with Var(W) = σ² < ∞, E[e^{θW}|W' − W|] < ∞ for all θ ∈ R, and for some σ-algebra F ⊇ σ(W) there are non-negative constants B and C with E[(W' − W)²|F]/(2a) ≤ BW + C, then for all t > 0, P(W ≥ t) ≤ exp(−t²/(2C + 2Bt)) and P(W ≤ −t) ≤ exp(−t²/(2C)).

[Theorem thm:upper_lower_general of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\bm{X}$ belong to the domain of non-normal attraction of an $\alpha$-stable process $\bm{Z}$.\\
{\normalfont(a)} Let $\alpha\in(0,2)\setminus\{1\}$ and Assumptions~(\nameref{asm:C}) and (\nameref{asm:S}) hold for some $p\in(0,\infty)\setminus\{ \alpha-1\}$, $\delta>0$ and $G_2\in\mbox{SV}_0$. Then, 
\[
\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t,\bm{Z})
=\mathcal{O} ( G_2(t)^q)
\qquad\text{as }t \downarrow 0,
\]
for any $q\in(0,1]\cap(0,\alpha)\setminus\{\alpha/(p+1),\alpha/(\alpha\delta+1)\}$ with $\mathds{E}[|\bm{X}_1|^q]<\infty$.\\
{\normalfont(b)} Let $\alpha \in (0,2]$ and define $a(t) \coloneqq G(2t)/G(t)$ for $t>0$. Then for any $q\in(0,1]\cap(0,\alpha)$,  
\begin{align*}
\max\big\{\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{Z}_1)
,\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^{2t}_1,\bm{Z}_1)\big\}
\geqslant |1-a(t)^q|\mathds{E}\big[|\bm{Z}_1|^q\big]/3,
\quad \text{for all sufficiently small }t >0.
\end{align*} 
Moreover, $|1-a(t)^q|$ cannot be upper bounded by a non-decreasing function $\phi$ with $\int_0^1\phi(t)t^{-1}\mathrm{d} t<\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:upper_lower_general of arXiv:2411.03609

body:
Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); T385-w737-C14 v1; no independent PASS, Lean certificate, or novelty claim. Let X_n be deterministic real n by n matrices with ||X_n||<=L, w_1,...,w_n independent N(0,I_n), z_j=ReLU(X_n w_j)-E ReLU(X_n w_j), and Sigma_n=E z_j z_j^T with ||Sigma_n||<=K. Let A_n and T_n be deterministic conditional on X_n, A_n real symmetric with A_n>=eta I_n for fixed eta>0, and ||T_n||<=K_T. Put Q_n=[A_n+(1/n)sum_j z_j z_j^T]^-1 and P_n(t)=[A_n+Sigma_n/(1+t)]^-1. The recorded unaudited derivation asserts a unique nonnegative t_n=Tr(Sigma_n P_n(t_n))/n and Tr[T_n(Q_n-P_n(t_n))]/n ->0 in probability. Random inputs independent of the Gaussian feature columns are admitted on typical events with tight input and covariance norms. This is a fixed-ridge normalized-trace statement for each prescribed bounded deterministic test sequence, not a uniform statement over feature-dependent tests. The proof uses leave-one-out concentration, a deterministic scalar mesh to handle the random self-consistent parameter, exact resolvent identities, and scalar fixed-point stability. In the square Gaussian all-weights raw-ReLU NTK, earlier unaudited derivative/covariance reductions yield the corresponding covariance-aware MP-input integral equation at each fixed positive ridge. Independent review of all dependencies is pending. No bounded spectral-edge law, anisotropic edge estimate, absence of bounded outliers, or promotion of the conditional upper-edge estimate is asserted.
Square X_n, deterministic conditional input, ||X_n||<=L
n independent standard Gaussian feature-weight vectors, independent of any random input
z_j conditionally mean-centered raw ReLU columns, covariance norm at most K
A_n symmetric, deterministic conditional on input, uniformly A_n>=eta I for fixed eta>0
T_n deterministic conditional on input with uniformly bounded operator norm
Normalized trace limit as n tends to infinity; positive ridge fixed
Status proof (unaudited), dependent C06/C08/C13 also await independent review

Let G be an algebraic group over a number field k. The Brauer-Manin obstruction to weak approximation on the classifying stack BG is the only obstruction: the topological closure of the image of BG(k) in BG(A_k) is precisely the Brauer-Manin set BG(A_k)^{Br}.

body:
[Lemma KacRice of arXiv:2604.20660, 'The Legendre structure of the TAP complexity\\ for the Ising spin glass'] Let $\zeta$ be a probability measure on $[0,1]$ with a $2$-atom prefix
		$\{0,q\}$ for some $q\in(0,1)$, and let $\varepsilon\in(0,q/2)$.
		Let $\mathcal N_\varepsilon(f,\zeta,q)$ be the number of critical points $\mathbf{m}$ of
		$F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}$ such that
		\[
		\mathbf{m}\in \mathrm{SUSY}_1(\zeta,\varepsilon)
		\qquad\text{and}\qquad
		\frac1N F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})\in(f-\varepsilon,f+\varepsilon).
		\]
		For $\mathbf{m}\in(-1,1)^N$, write $q_\mathbf{m}:=\frac1N\|\mathbf{m}\|^2$.
		
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\item \textup{(Mixed case.)}
			Assume that for every $\mathbf{m}\in(-1,1)^N$ with
			$q_\mathbf{m}\in(q-\varepsilon,q+\varepsilon)$, the Gaussian vector
			\[
			\bigl(\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m}),\,F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})\bigr)
			\]
			is non-degenerate.  In particular, this holds for a genuine mixed
			$p$-spin Hamiltonian, i.e.\ when
			\[
			\xi(t)=\sum_{p\ge 2}\beta_p^2 t^p
			\]
			has at least two non-zero coefficients.
			Then
			\begin{multline}
				\mathbb{E}[\mathcal N_\varepsilon(f,\zeta,q)]
				=N\int_{[-1,1]^N}\int_{(f-\varepsilon,f+\varepsilon)}
				\mathbb{E}\!\left[
				|\det(\nabla^2 F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m}))|
				\,\middle|\,
				\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=0,\,
				F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=Nf'
				\right]
				\\
				\times
				\varphi_{(\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m}),\,F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m}))}(0,Nf')\,
				\mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{SUSY}_1(\zeta,\varepsilon)}(\mathbf{m})\,
				\mathrm{d}\mathbf{m}\,\mathrm{d} f'.
			\end{multline}
			
			\item \textup{(Pure case.)}
			Assume that $\xi(t)=\beta_p^2 t^p$ is pure $p$-spin for some $p\ge2$.
			Recalling the notation~(equation eq:def-Rex-KR of the paper),
			\begin{multline}
				\mathbb{E}[\mathcal N_\varepsilon(f,\zeta,q)]
				=
				\int_{[-1,1]^N}
				\mathbb{E}\!\left[
				|\det(\nabla^2 F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m}))|
				\,\middle|\,
				\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=0
				\right]
				\varphi_{\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})}(0)
				\\
				\times
				\mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{SUSY}_1(\zeta,\varepsilon)}(\mathbf{m})\,
				\mathbf{1}_{(f-\varepsilon,f+\varepsilon)}
				\!\left(\frac1N\mathcal R^{\rm ex}_\zeta(\mathbf{m})\right)
				\mathrm{d}\mathbf{m}.
			\end{multline}
		\end{enumerate}

[Prop 36 (Smallest singular value) of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $(B(t))_{t\geq 0}$ be a $(\rho,\zeta)$-Brownian motion. 
    Let $A$ be an $N\times N$ matrix, deterministic or random and independent of $(B(t))_{t\geq 0}$.
    Then the following hold for $0<t\le T<\infty$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] If $|\zeta|<\rho$, then for all $\alpha>0$, \eqref{bd:smallest} holds for all $N\ge (4/\alpha)^{3/2}+ t^{-1/2}$, with $C=2$, $c=1-\alpha$ and the implicit constant depending only on $\alpha,\rho,\zeta,T$. 
        \item[(b)] (Degenerate case). If $|\zeta|=\rho$, then \eqref{bd:smallest} holds for universal constants $C,c\in (0,\infty)$ and all $N\ge t^{-c/C}$, with the implicit constant in \eqref{bd:smallest} depending only on $\rho$ and $T$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $\theta\in (0,1)$. There exist $\delta\in (0,1)$ and $L\in (0,\infty)$ such that for every partition $\Pcal=\{S=U_0<U_1<\ldots<U_N=T\}$ (with $N\in\Nsf$, $N\geq 2$) satisfying \ref{ass:sewing-p} the estimate
	\[
		|Z_{s,t}|\leq L\omega_{s,t}^\frac{3}{p}
	\]
holds for every $(s,t)\in \Delta\llbracket 0,N \rrbracket$ satisfying $\omega_{s,t}<\delta$. Both constants $\delta$ and $L$ depend only on $\theta$, $m$, $\|f\|_2$, $\mathrm{supp}(f)$, $p$, $\omega(S,T)$, and $\|X\|$.

[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2609.02779, '2609.02779'] There exists $C_r>0$ such that
\[
  \|u_\lambda-u_0\|_\infty
  \ge C_r\lambda^{1/(2r-1)}
\]
for all sufficiently small $\lambda>0$. If $r=1$, then
\[
  \|u_\lambda-u_0\|_\infty\asymp\lambda.
\]
If $r\ge2$, the estimate
$\|u_\lambda-u_0\|_\infty=O(\lambda)$ fails. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 9 of arXiv:2609.02779

body: In mathematics, Abelian and Tauberian theorems are theorems giving conditions for two methods of summing divergent series to give the same result, named after Niels Henrik Abel and Alfred Tauber. The original examples are Abel's theorem showing that if a series converges to some limit then its Abel sum is the same limit, and Tauber's theorem showing that if the Abel sum of a series exists and the coefficients are sufficiently small then the series converges to the Abel sum. More general Abelian and Tauberian theorems give similar results for more general summation methods.

body:
Load-bearing distinction: for $f\in L^1$ the transform is an honest absolutely convergent integral, bounded, continuous, defined at every $\xi$; for $f\in L^2\setminus L^1$ it is defined only as the $L^2$-limit $\hat f=\lim_{R\to\infty}\widehat{f\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\le R\}}}$ (the unique continuous extension from the dense subspace $L^1\cap L^2$), hence is an equivalence class defined only almost everywhere. Example: $f(x)=\sin(\pi x)/(\pi x)\in L^2\setminus L^1$, whose Plancherel transform is $\mathbf 1_{[-1/2,1/2]}$ a.e.; the truncated integrals converge to $1$ for $|\xi|<1/2$, to $0$ for $|\xi|>1/2$ and to $1/2$ at $\xi=\pm1/2$, but no value at $\pm1/2$ is meaningful for the $L^2$ transform. Consequences an auditor should check: (i) claims like '$\hat f(\xi_0)=0$' or '$\hat f$ is continuous' are meaningless for $L^2$ data without naming a representative (the usual legitimate versions are 'a.e.' statements or support statements up to null sets); (ii) $\|\hat f\|_\infty\le\|f\|_1$ is unavailable; (iii) that $\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{-R}^Rf(x)e^{-2\pi ix\xi}dx$ exists for a.e. $\xi$ when $f\in L^2(\mathbb R)$ is a deep result (the Fourier-integral form of Carleson's theorem), not a corollary of Plancherel, which only gives $L^2$ convergence and hence a.e. convergence along some subsequence of radii. On $L^1\cap L^2$ the two definitions agree a.e., which is what makes the extension consistent.

body:
Let $x_1,\dots,x_N$ be random points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose joint law is invariant under reflection of any subset of them through the origin, and which are almost surely in general position. Then the probability that all of them lie in a single open halfspace whose boundary contains the origin, equivalently the probability that the origin is not in their convex hull, equals $2^{-N+1}\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}\binom{N-1}{k}$. In particular this probability is $1$ whenever $N \le d$. Note that symmetry alone does not suffice: general position is needed, since for instance two points i.i.d. uniform on $\{\pm e_1\} \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ are symmetric (their joint law is invariant under reflection of any subset of them through the origin) but not in general position, and they lie in a common open halfspace whose boundary contains the origin with probability $1/2$ (exactly when the two points coincide; $e_1$ and $-e_1$ lie in no such halfspace, and the origin is in their convex hull), whereas the formula gives $2^{-1}\left(\binom{1}{0}+\binom{1}{1}\right)=1$.
the joint law of the points is invariant under reflection of any subset through the origin
the points are almost surely in general position (every d or fewer are linearly independent)
independence of the points is not required

[Theorem thm:popularity of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $h\geq2$.  There are explicit positive rational constants
$\kappa_2,\ldots,\kappa_h$ such that, as $q\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 F_{h,M_h-M_{h-r}}(q)=\kappa_rq^3+O_h(q^2)
 \qquad(2\leq r\leq h),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 F_{h,M_h}(q)=\binom q4-
 \left(\sum_{r=2}^h\kappa_r\right)q^3+O_h(q^2).
\end{equation}
For every
\[
 n\in\mathcal R(h,4)\setminus
 \left(\{M_h\}\cup\{M_h-M_{h-r}:2\leq r\leq h\}\right)
\]
there is an explicit positive rational constant $\lambda_{h,n}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 F_{h,n}(q)=\lambda_{h,n}q^2+O_h(q).
\end{equation}
Thus exactly $h$ cardinalities are popular: the maximum has frequency of
order $q^4$, the other $h-1$ displayed values have frequency of order
$q^3$, and every remaining attainable value has frequency of order $q^2$.

[Corollary co:subsequential_limit_cond_laws of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Let $X,Y$ be Polish spaces. Let $
u$ be a probability measure on $X$, and $\mu_n[dy \mid x]$ a sequence of probability kernels from $X$ to $Y$. Suppose that the sequence of measures $(
u\otimes\mu_n)$ on $X 	imes Y$ is tight, and that the sequence $(\mu_n)$ is equicontinuous as functions from $X$ to the space of probability measures on $Y$ equipped with the Prokhorov metric. Then there exists a subsequence $(n_k)$ such that $\mu_{n_k}[\cdot \mid x]$ converges weakly for $
u$-almost every every $x \in X$.

[Definition D_Kr_tree of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] We call a graph $T$ a {\it $K_r$-tree}
(or a {\it clique tree})
of {\it order} $\vartheta$ if it is 
the union of $\vartheta$
many copies $H_1,\ldots,H_\vartheta$ of $K_r$, 
and that, 
for every $1<i\leqslant \vartheta$, $H_i$ shares exactly 
one edge with $H_1 \cup\cdots \cup H_{i-1}$.
We call an edge $e\in E(G)$ an {\it internal edge} 
of $T$ if it is contained in at least two of the copies of $K_r$.

Let $Y = X + \sigma Z$ be an $m \times n$ matrix, $m \le n$, $\beta = m/n \in (0, 1]$, where $Z$ has i.i.d. entries of mean zero and variance one and $X$ has fixed rank $r$ (not growing with $m$). Let $y_{\mathrm{med}}$ be the median of the singular values of $Y$ and let $\mu_\beta$ be the median of the Marchenko-Pastur law with ratio $\beta$ and variance one (support $[(1 - \sqrt\beta)^2, (1 + \sqrt\beta)^2]$). Then $$\hat\sigma := \frac{y_{\mathrm{med}}}{\sqrt{n\, \mu_\beta}} \to \sigma$$ almost surely as $m, n \to \infty$ with $m/n \to \beta$. (Gavish and Donoho, 2014.) The estimate is unaffected in the limit by the low-rank signal because $X$ displaces at most $r$ of the $m$ singular values, which does not move the sample median.

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent mathematical, priority and target-scope audit pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K,F=K-r,kappa=F/K. There are d unknown A/S pairs, one A with an arbitrary r-truth support and one all-true S per pair, and N-2d known S contexts. The source chooses a context uniformly then a true atom uniformly. Independently a verifier gives a uniform r-subset T_x of truths in EVERY variable context, including S, without orientation labels. Observe n iid actual facts without tags. Each realized learned law must have source Mis_infinity<=c in EVERY compatible world, at exact generator-score bins, with 0<=c<1/(2NrK). Let U count pairs with no observed fact outside either certificate. EVERY feasible law has false mass at least (kappa*U/N-c)_+/2 in EACH compatible world, and an efficient observed-data residual-pooling rule attains equality in all worlds simultaneously. The exact global expected robust minimax frontier is Gamma(c)=kappa*d/(2N)*(1-kappa/N)^n -c/2*sum_{j=1}^d(-1)^(j+1)*binom(d,j)*(1-j*kappa/N)^n. The supplied-partition oracle has zero false mass; Gamma is the exact learning penalty in this full-verifier experiment. No coprimality or r>=K/2 restriction is needed. The pointwise lower removes globally false atoms without increasing calibration or any loss, uses bin-mass quantization to force invariant bins, and charges a certified-truth baseline excess rho/(2Nr) when actual bin risk rho exceeds one half. The class has VC dimension d. This is an expected compatible-world robust game with full certificates in BOTH contexts, not a classical labeled-data ERM/PAC result or a general partial-verifier frontier.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:f430bebcb8cc10d3867c88702e15cc125066a3735b9727a34e37b09b46500ab7","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/f4/f430bebcb8cc10d3867c88702e15cc125066a3735b9727a34e37b09b46500ab7.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:bfb40a85e981a6703e4456e0e3fa9b45c2c93b227fb79e44e72bd633065bfbc2","bundle_entry_key":"full-verifier-global-small-budget-frontier","bundle_id":"population.t379-full-verifier-arbitrary-vc-global-frontier-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"calibrated generation; partition learning; global minimax and occupancy","draft":"w709/bundle_014.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:kalai-vempala-full-verifier-arbitrary-vc-global-small-budget-frontier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Full verification: arbitrary-VC global frontier for all truth fractions

T379-C022 v3, proof (unaudited); exact checks PASS. Target 1, secondary target 2.
This removes r>=K/2 from the v1 derivation in
full_verifier_dense_global_frontier.md. The new ingredient is a certified-
truth baseline margin; no coprimality assumption is required.

## Statement

Integers d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K; F=K-r,kappa=F/K,lambda=1/(NK).
There are d A/S context pairs, each with one A having an arbitrary
r-truth support and one S having all K truths, and N-2d known S contexts.
The factual law chooses a context uniformly, then a true atom uniformly.
An independent verifier gives a uniform r-subset T_x of truths in EACH
variable context, including S, without orientation labels. Observe n
actual iid facts without tags. Thus A truths equal T_A, while S has
F truths outside T_S. A pair is resolved exactly when a sampled fact
lies outside one of its certificates. Let U be the unresolved pair count.

For every 0<=c<1/(2NrK), require each realized learned generator to have
source Mis_infinity<=c in EVERY data-compatible world, with source
coarsening uniform inside exact generator-score bins. Then:

 (i) EVERY feasible g has actual false mass >=(kappa U/N-c)_+/2
     in EACH compatible world.
 (ii) An efficient observable-data policy attains equality simultaneously.
 (iii) The exact global expected robust minimax false mass is

 Gamma(c)=kappa*d/(2N)*(1-kappa/N)^n
  -c/2*sum_{j=1}^d(-1)^(j+1)*binom(d,j)*(1-j*kappa/N)^n.       (1)

The same-data known-partition oracle is zero. Hence (1) is the exact
experiment-specific partition-learning penalty in this full-verifier
regime. No standard labeled-data ERM/PAC result is asserted.

## Hardest step

Invariant score bins can have actual false fraction above one half if
r<K/2. The v1 dense-support bound therefore FAILS in that range.
The proof below handles such bins by an explicit positive baseline
margin, not by assuming the false-fraction bound holds.

## Remove globally false atoms

Use the constructive reduction proved in the v1 file: from each score
cell remove atoms Z false in every compatible world, preserving the
cell's total generator mass uniformly on its remaining atoms. Remove
pure-Z cells and transfer their generator mass to a remaining cell.
This weakly lowers false risk in every world and does not increase
cell-level TV to any source; new equal-score mergers contract TV further.
The proof is elementary: (f-z)/(m-z)<=f/m for mixed cells, and deleting
pure-Z mass delta reduces its L1 term by delta while transfer increases
another term by at most delta. Thus it suffices to lower-bound g' zero
on Z. This is a law transformation, not a mixture of generators.

## Common coarsened source and the zero-score cell

Source bin masses are multiples of 1/(NrK). If two compatible coarsened
source laws differ, their TV is at least 1/(NrK). Robust feasibility
instead bounds this by 2c<1/(NrK). Thus source bin masses are common
across worlds. The zero-score bin has g' mass zero, so its source mass
is <=c. Any nonzero source mass would be >=1/(NrK)>c. Therefore its
source mass is zero in every world; it contains only globally false
atoms. Ignore it below. Other bins exclude Z.

Average source laws fairly over all compatible unresolved orientations,
regardless of their true sampling posterior. Call the result mu.
On an unresolved pair mu has density

 sigma=(1/(Nr)+1/(NK))/2 on certified atoms T,
 lambda/2 on the outside-T atoms M.

Every resolved or fixed atom outside Z is universally true and has
source density >=lambda. Invariance implies p0=mu_Pi is the common
coarsened source of g', and TV(p0,g')<=c.

## Baseline margin and actual bin risks

Fix ANY actual compatible world. In a nonzero bin B let
c_B,d_B count outside-T atoms respectively false and true in that world,
t_B count unresolved certified atoms, and s_B count remaining safe atoms.
Write m_B=c_B+d_B+t_B+s_B and rho_B=c_B/m_B. Then

 p0(B)>=lambda*m_B/2+t_B/(2Nr)+lambda*s_B/2,

since sigma-lambda/2=1/(2Nr). Therefore the baseline false mass in B is

 rho_B*p0(B)>=lambda*c_B/2
                 +rho_B*(t_B/(2Nr)+lambda*s_B/2).          (2)

Summing first terms gives B0=lambda F U/2=kappa U/(2N).
All remaining terms are nonnegative.

For each unresolved pair, let u_L,u_R count its certified atoms in B
and v_L,v_R its outside atoms. Independent orientation invariance gives

 F*(u_L-u_R)=r*(v_L-v_R).                               (3)

If t_B=0, then all u's vanish, hence v_L=v_R for every pair. Exactly
half the M-atoms in B are false in the actual world, and safe atoms
only lower the fraction. Consequently rho_B>1/2 implies t_B>=1.
This implication holds for every r and needs no coprimality.

Let alpha=max_B rho_B over nonzero bins. If alpha<=1/2, bounded-risk
TV transport gives H(g')>=H(p0)-c/2>=B0-c/2. If alpha>1/2, select a
maximizing bin. It has t_B>=1, so (2) gives the GLOBAL baseline excess
H(p0)-B0>=alpha/(2Nr). Bounded-risk TV transport gives instead

 H(g')>=H(p0)-alpha*c
       >=B0+alpha*(1/(2Nr)-c)
       >=B0
       >=B0-c/2,

because c<1/(2NrK)<1/(2Nr). Thus high-risk bins are too expensive in
baseline false mass to improve on pooling at this small budget.
Adding nonnegativity when U=0 proves (i), including original laws g
whose risk is >=that of g'. This is a POINTWISE argument in each world.
It does not infer a global lower bound by averaging conditional maxima.

## Attainment, occupancy and global equality

If U>0, pool all 2FU outside-T atoms of unresolved pairs. Their common
source mass is M=kappa U/N and their actual false fraction is 1/2 in
every world. Give them total mass (M-c)_+, transfer min(c,M) to fixed S,
retain the invariant paired certified-truth source scores, and give
resolved truth/false atoms their true source probabilities/zero.
These source group masses are invariant, and equal-score mergers
preserve calibration <=c. False mass is exactly (M-c)_+/2. For U=0,
all truths are identified and the actual source law has zero false mass.
The construction needs only observed T, outside hits and known parameters.

In each fixed actual world and certificate realization, the d disjoint
S-outside-T distinguishing event sets each have source mass kappa/N.
Thus E[U]=d*(1-kappa/N)^n and inclusion-exclusion gives
P(U>0)=sum_{j=1}^d(-1)^(j+1)binom(d,j)(1-j*kappa/N)^n.
Do not assume independence of the unresolved indicators.
Since c<kappa/N, the conditional value is
kappa U/(2N)-c/2*1_{U>0}; averaging pointwise lower and matching upper
in each world yields (1). The oracle knows each A orientation and
T_A then reveals its entire support; it can emit its true source and
has both source calibration and false mass zero.

## Scope and provenance

The paired orientation class has VC dimension d. Computation of the
observable policy is polynomial in the explicit alphabet size and n.
This is an expected compatible-world robust game, not labeled-sample
ERM, a high-probability PAC frontier, a fractional-verifier theorem, or
a result for larger c. The full verifier supplies all A truths AND r
truths from S. It leaves orientation uncertain, rather than merely
providing a labeled partition. All independent audits and priority/scope
assessments remain pending.

inequalities across ALL truth fractions, including 572 genuine high-risk
bins with certified-truth baseline margins; 9850 sparse multi-pair
actual-world cell checks; 391 exhaustive sparse invariant partitions and
782 pointwise exact TV-ball optima; 3528 all-world attainer/calibration
checks and 588 exact occupancy/global expectations. The earlier dense
suite checked 2717 known-false-removal risk/TV comparisons, 8022 exhaustive
invariant partitions, 17282 pointwise TV-ball optima, and 2016 all-world
attainers. All use integers and Fraction, no numerical estimates.
Finite checks support the analytic proof, not an independent audit.

The dense lemma that every actual bin risk is <=1/2 fails for sparse r:
a real K=3,r=1 invariant whole-context bin has risk 2/3. The general
proof uses the certified-truth baseline margin instead of that lemma.

Assumption2.4 and Theorem4.2 (printedpp4,7), require global Regular Facts
for all unobserved statements and give a posterior-probability innovation
bound. The full structured experiment retains known-S unseen truths and
potentially different unresolved orientation posteriors; no direct
application of their globally regular theorem is asserted. This comparison
does not certify novelty or exclude useful restrictions of that theorem.

[Lemma lem:c4-basic of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $G=(I,J,M)$ be $C_4$-free.

\begin{enumerate}
\item If $i\in I$ and $j,j'\in N_G(i)$ are distinct, then
\[
(N_G(j)\setminus\{i\})\cap (N_G(j')\setminus\{i\})=\emptyset.
\]

\item If $j_\star\in J$, $I_\star=N_G(j_\star)$, and
\[
j\ne j_\star,
\qquad
N_G(j)\cap I_\star\ne\emptyset,
\]
then $j$ is adjacent to a unique vertex of $I_\star$.

\item If $J'\subseteq J$, then $G[J']$ is $C_4$-free.

\end{enumerate}

[Definition of arXiv:2412.03366, 'Regularity of Weighted Tensorized Fractional Brownian Fields and associated function space'] Let $\psi$ denote a Lemari\'e-Meyer  wavelet  and $\varphi$ the associated scaling function. The hyperbolic wavelet basis is defined as the system $$\{\psi_{j_1,j_2,k_1,k_2} :  \, (j_1, j_2) \in (\mathbb{N}\cup \{-1\})^2, \, (k_1, k_2) \in \mathbb{Z}^2\}$$
where
\begin{itemize}
\item if $j_1,j_2\geq 0$,
$$
\psi_{j_1,j_2,k_1,k_2}(x_1,x_2)= \psi(2^{j_1}x_1-k_1)\psi(2^{j_2}x_2-k_2)\; ,
$$
\item if $j_1=-1$ and $j_2\geq 0$
$$
\psi_{-1,j_2,k_1,k_2}(x_1,x_2)= \varphi(x_1-k_1)\psi(2^{j_2}x_2-k_2)\; ,
$$
\item if $j_1\ge 0$ and $j_2=-1$
$$
\psi_{j_1,-1,k_1,k_2}(x_1,x_2)= \psi(2^{j_1}x_1-k_1)\varphi(x_2-k_2)\;,
$$
\item if $j_1=j_2=-1$
$$
\psi_{-1,-1,k_1,k_2}(x_1,x_2)= \varphi(x_1-k_1)\varphi(x_2-k_2)\;.
$$
\end{itemize}
For any $f\in\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^2)$, one then defines its hyperbolic wavelet coefficients by
\begin{eqnarray*}
c_{j_1,j_2,k_1,k_2}&=&2^{j_1+j_2}<f,\psi_{j_1,j_2,k_1,k_2}>\mbox{ if }j_1,j_2\geq 0\;,\\
c_{j_1,-1,k_1,k_2}&=&2^{j_1}<f,\psi_{j_1,j_2,k_1,k_2}>\mbox{ if }j_1\geq 0\mbox{ and }j_2=-1\;,\\
c_{-1,j_2,k_1,k_2}&=&2^{j_2}<f,\psi_{j_1,j_2,k_1,k_2}>\mbox{ if }j_1=-1\mbox{ and }j_2\geq 0\;,\\
c_{-1,-1,k_1,k_2}&=&<f,\psi_{j_1,j_2,k_1,k_2}>\mbox{ if }j_1=j_2=-1\;.
\end{eqnarray*}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2412.03366, 'Regularity of Weighted Tensorized Fractional Brownian Fields'

[Corollary of arXiv:2411.06827, 'The Exponential Lie Series and a Chen--Strichartz Formula for L{\'e}vy Processes'] The following elements form a family of algebraic generators of the algebra $({\mathbb R} {\langle}\overline{\mathbb A}{\rangle},\mathrm{conc})$
$$
	\overline a^0 := \sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}\sum_{[a_1, \ldots, a_n]=a} \overline a_1 \cdots \overline a_n,
$$
for $a\in {\mathbb A}$. Thus, denoting $\overline{\mathbb A}^0$ the set of such elements, the two algebras $({\mathbb R} {\langle}\overline{\mathbb A}{\rangle},\mathrm{conc})$ and $({\mathbb R} {\langle}\overline{\mathbb A}^0{\rangle},\mathrm{conc})$ are equal. 
Furthermore, the elements of $\overline{\mathbb A}^0$ are primitive for the coproduct $\delta$. Thus, on  $({\mathbb R} {\langle}\overline{\mathbb A}^0{\rangle},\mathrm{conc})$ the expression of the coproduct is given by the unshuffling of words:
$$
	\delta(\overline a_1^0\cdots \overline a_n^0)
	=\sum\limits_{{\{i_1,\ldots,i_k\}\cup \{j_1,\ldots,j_{n-k}\}=\{1,\ldots,n\}}}
	\overline a_{i_1}^0 \cdots \overline a_{i_k}^0 \otimes \overline a_{j_1}^0\cdots \overline a_{j_{n-k}}^0,
$$
for $\overline a_i^0$ in $\overline{\mathbb A}^0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition 17 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Let $\Sigma \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and $\llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket$ be a nonempty integer interval in $\mathbb{Z}$. Consider the set $Y$ of functions $f: \Sigma \times \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ such that $f(i, j+1) - f(i,j) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ when $i \in \Sigma$ and $j \in\llbracket T_0, T_1 -1 \rrbracket$ and let $\mathcal{D}$ denote the discrete $\sigma$-algebra on $Y$. We call a function $f: \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ such that $f( j+1) - f(j) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ when $j \in\llbracket T_0, T_1 -1 \rrbracket$  an {\em increasing path} and elements in $Y$ {\em collections of increasing paths}. A {\em $\Sigma$-indexed geometric line ensemble $\mathfrak{L}$ on $\llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket$}  is a random variable defined on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{B}, \mathbb{P})$, taking values in $Y$ such that $\mathfrak{L}$ is a $(\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{D})$-measurable function. Unless otherwise specified, we will assume that $T_0 \leq T_1$ are both integers, although the above definition makes sense if $T_0 = -\infty$, or $T_1 = \infty$, or both.

[Lemma lem:ito-expansion-Lp of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Let \(p>2\), and recall that 
\[
    L_p(t)
    :=
    \frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J
    \phi_{a,p}(Y_t^j,\hat Z_t^j),
    \qquad
    \phi_{a,p}(y,z)
    :=
    a|y|^p+|z|^p+\frac m\gamma |y|^{p-2}\langle y,z\rangle \,,
\] and $\Delta_\alpha(t):=m_X(\mu_{X_t^J})-\mathcal M_\alpha(t)$. Hence, $ X_t^j-\mathcal M_\alpha(t)=Y_t^j+\Delta_\alpha(t)\,,$
and
\[
    \mathrm d\hat Z_t^j
    =
    (-K_Z\hat Z_t^j-K_YY_t^j)\mathrm d t+\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}},
\]
where
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}
    :=
    \frac{\sigma}{m}
    \left[
        \left(1-\frac1J\right)
        S(Y_t^j+\Delta_\alpha(t))\,\mathrm d W_t^j
        -
        \frac1J\sum_{k\ne j}
        S(Y_t^k+\Delta_\alpha(t))\,\mathrm d W_t^k
    \right].
\end{equation}
The stochastic differential of \(L_p(t)\) is
\begin{align}
    \mathrm d L_p(t)
    &=
    \frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J
    \Bigg\{
    \left[
        \left(\frac{ap}{\gamma}-\frac m\gamma K_Y\right)|Y_t^j|^p
        -
        pK_Z|\hat Z_t^j|^p
    \right]\mathrm d t
    \notag\\
    &\quad
    +
    \left[
        \left(
            ap-\frac m\gamma K_Z+\frac{m(p-1)}{\gamma^2}
        \right)
        |Y_t^j|^{p-2}\langle Y_t^j,\hat Z_t^j\rangle
        -
        pK_Y|\hat Z_t^j|^{p-2}\langle \hat Z_t^j,Y_t^j\rangle
    \right]\mathrm d t
    \notag\\
    &\quad
    +
    \left[
        \frac m\gamma |Y_t^j|^{p-2}|\hat Z_t^j|^2
        +
        \frac{m(p-2)}{\gamma}
        |Y_t^j|^{p-4}\langle Y_t^j,\hat Z_t^j\rangle^2
    \right]\mathrm d t
    \notag\\
    &\quad
    +
    \mathcal T_{\mathrm{noise}}^j(t)\,\mathrm d t
    +
    \mathrm d M_{p,t}^j
    \Bigg\},
    
\end{align}
where
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d M_{p,t}^j
    :=
    p|\hat Z_t^j|^{p-2}
    \left\langle \hat Z_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle
    +
    \frac m\gamma |Y_t^j|^{p-2}
    \left\langle Y_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle .
\end{equation}
We denote $ M_{p,t}:=\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J M_{p,t}^j$ as the local martingale part of \(L_p(t)\). The noise trace satisfies
\begin{align}
    \mathcal T_{\mathrm{noise}}^j(t)
    &=
    \frac12
    \operatorname{Tr}
    \left(
        \nabla^2(|\hat Z_t^j|^p)\,
        \mathrm d\langle M^{j,\mathrm{center}}\rangle_t
    \right)
    \notag\\
    &=
        \frac{p\sigma^2}{2m^2}\left(1-\frac1J\right)^2 |\hat Z_t^j|^{p-4}
        \left[
            (p-2)\left|S(X_t^j-\mathcal M_\alpha)^\top\hat Z_t^j\right|^2
            +|\hat Z_t^j|^2\norm{S(X_t^j-\mathcal M_\alpha)}_F^2
        \right] \notag \\
        &\quad
        +\frac{p\sigma^2}{2m^2J^2}\sum_{k\ne j}|\hat Z_t^j|^{p-4}
        \left[
            (p-2)\left|S(X_t^k-\mathcal M_\alpha)^\top\hat Z_t^j\right|^2
            +|\hat Z_t^j|^2\norm{S(X_t^k-\mathcal M_\alpha)}_F^2
        \right]\\
        & \leqslant
    \frac{p\sigma^2\chi_S}{2m^2}
    |\hat Z_t^j|^{p-2}
    \left(
        |Y_t^j+\Delta_\alpha(t)|^2
        +
        \frac1J\sum_{k=1}^J |Y_t^k+\Delta_\alpha(t)|^2
    \right).
    
\end{align}

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2605.03057, 'Uniform-in-time quantitative fluctuations of large scale interacting particle systems'] Assume that Assumptions \ref{ass:smooth},
\ref{ass:second-malliavin-uniform}, \ref{ass:flow-smothness} and \ref{ass:coeff-level-new} hold,  and let
$\varphi\in C_b^2\left(\R^d\right)$.
For $ t \ge 0 $, define
\begin{align*}
\Delta_{N,t}
&=
\iint_{A_t\times A_t}
\sqrt{
\E\left(
\left(
D^2F_t^N\left(\varphi\right)\otimes_1
D^2F_t^N\left(\varphi\right)
\right)\left(x,y\right)^2
\right)
}
\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad
\sqrt{
\E\left(
DF_t^N\left(\varphi\right)\left(x\right)^2
DF_t^N\left(\varphi\right)\left(y\right)^2
\right)
}
\lambda_t\left(dx\right)\lambda_t\left(dy\right),
\end{align*}
where
$A_t=\left[0,t\right]\times\left\{1,\dots,N\right\}\times\left\{1,\dots,m\right\}$,
and
\begin{equation*}
\lambda_t\left(ds,dj,d\alpha\right)=ds\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{\alpha=1}^m
\delta_{\left(j,\alpha\right)}.
\end{equation*}
Then, there exists a constant $ C > 0 $, independent of $ t $ and $ N $, such that
\begin{equation}

\sup_{t \ge 0} \Delta_{N,t}\le \frac{C}{N}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let R be a principal ideal domain (for instance Z or a field's polynomial ring k[x]) and A an m x n matrix over R. Then there are invertible matrices P (m x m) and Q (n x n) over R such that P A Q = D is diagonal in the sense that its only nonzero entries are d_1, ..., d_r in positions (1,1), ..., (r,r), with each d_i dividing d_{i+1}. The integer r is the rank of A, and the d_i (the invariant factors) are unique up to multiplication by units: d_1 ... d_k equals the greatest common divisor of all k x k minors of A (the k-th determinantal divisor), which invertible transformations do not change. Consequences: the structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID (every such module is R^{n-r} direct sum of R/(d_i)), in particular the classification of finitely generated abelian groups and the rational canonical form of a matrix over a field.

[Conjecture conj:barcode_kernel_intro of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] Around any macroscopic point $(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})$ in the waterfall region $\mathcal{W}$, the
	random configuration of square lozenges
	on a horizontal slice
	converges to a
	determinantal \textbf{barcode process} on $\mathbb{Z}$ with the symmetric correlation kernel
	$\mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}(s,t)$.\footnote{In particular, 
	we conjecture that the limit (equation eq:K_barcode_intro of the paper) exists for all integers $s\ge t$.}
	The barcode process depends only on the parameters $q$ and $\kappa$,
	but not on the geometry of the hexagon or the macroscopic location $(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})$
	inside $\mathcal{W}$, as long as the waterfall phase is present, i.e., $\mathsf{N}<\mathsf{T}$.
	
	The limiting kernel is $2\times 2$ block Toeplitz, that is,
	\begin{equation*}
		\begin{pmatrix}
			\mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}(s,t)& \mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}(s,t+1)\\
			\mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}(s+1,t) & \mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}(s+1,t+1)
		\end{pmatrix}
		=
			\begin{pmatrix}
				\mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}_{00}(s-t) & \mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}_{01}(s-t)\\
				\mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}_{10}(s-t) & \mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}_{11}(s-t)
			\end{pmatrix},
			\qquad s,t\in 2\mathbb{Z},
	\end{equation*}
	and satisfies
	$\mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}(0,0)=1-\mathcal{K}^{\mathrm{barcode}}(1,1)$ 
	(the plot of this function
	in $q$ and $\kappa$ is given in (fig:density_rho_even_3d of the paper)).
	Consequently, the barcode process has global density $1/2$
	for every choice of $q$ and $\kappa$, and it is invariant
	under even but not odd shifts. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

[Definition def:sparsestack of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Fix integers $n,\zeta,b \in \mathbb{N}$, and set
\[
    k:=\zeta b.
\]
Partition the column set $[k]$ into $\zeta$ consecutive blocks of size $b$. 
Independently choose a uniformly distributed random position in each block and populate these positions with independent $\pm 1$ entries.

More formally, the SparseStack matrix is a random $n\times k$ matrix
$S=(s_{ij})$
constructed as follows: for every row index $i \in [n]$ and every block index $t \in [\zeta]$, choose
$p_{i,t} \in [b],$
$\varrho_{i,t} \in \{-1,1\},$
independently and uniformly at random, and place the value $\varrho_{i,t}/\sqrt{\zeta}$ in the matrix coordinate of $S$
\[
    (i,(t-1)b+p_{i,t}).
\]
After the construction is complete, set all unassigned entries of $S$ to zero.
title: SparseStack

[Lem slconv of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Suppose we have a sequence of $\Phi$-horizontal $C^0$-foliations $\mathcal{G}_k$, $k \geq 0$, on $\mathbb{T}^2$, converging to a $\Phi$-horizontal foliation $\mathcal{G}$ in the $C^0_\mathrm{Fol}$ topology. Furthermore, assume that each $\mathcal{G}_k$ is Reebless with slope $s_k \in \mathbb{R}$, and that $(s_k)_k$ converges to some slope $s_\infty \in \mathbb{R}$.
    Then $\mathcal{G}$ is admissible, and either
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\mathcal{G}$ is of $\aleph$ type, or
        \item $\mathcal{G}$ has no Reeb annuli and has slope $s = s_\infty$.
    \end{itemize}

    Moreover, in the second case, if $(s_k)_k$ is strictly increasing (resp.~decreasing), then $\fs(\mathcal{G}) \in \{s^\natural, s^\flat\}$ (resp.~$\fs(\mathcal{G}) \in \{s^\natural, s^\sharp\}$).

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2607.06242, 'Exponential mixing and Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for Markov cocycles'] Assume that for $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$ the noisy system has a unique stationary measure $\mu^{\varepsilon}_{\s}$ and satisfies the trajectory Freidlin--Wentzell uniform LDP. Suppose further that for $m$-a.e. $\sigma\in\Sigma$, the quasipotential $E_{\Ac(\sigma)}$ has compact level sets, and that the tracking property, the nontrivial escaping energy property, and weak exponential tightness hold. Then for $m$-a.e. $\sigma\in\Sigma$, the upper large deviation bound
    \[
            \limsup_{\eps\to0}\eps\ln\mu^\eps_\sigma(F)
            \leq -\inf_{u\in F}E_{\Ac(\sigma)}(u)
    \]
    holds for every closed set $F\subset H$.  If the deterministic pullback attractor is a random point, then the matching lower bound
    \[
            \liminf_{\eps\to0}\eps\ln\mu^\eps_\sigma(G)
            \geq -\inf_{u\in G}E_{\Ac(\sigma)}(u)
    \]
    holds for every open set $G\subset H$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 64 of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] Recall that $\rho=k/N$, $\alpha=1-2\rho$, as well as $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(N,k)=N^{-3/2}\beta^{3/2}$ for $\beta=\beta(\alpha)$ from \eqref{def:betaASEP}. For all $i\in \lbr M \rbr$, $z\in \R$, $t \geq 0$, and periodic initial data $ h^{\per,\varepsilon}_0$, we define the \textbf{rescaled patched ASEP height function} as 
\begin{align*}
\hfix^{\textup{patch},\delta,\varepsilon}( \hfix^{\per,\varepsilon}_0;z,t) := \sigma(\alpha)^{-1}\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{3}}&\Big(2\mu(\alpha)\varepsilon^{-1}t +\mu^{\prime}(\alpha)\beta(\alpha)z\varepsilon^{-\frac{2}{3}} \\
&- h^{\textup{patch},\delta}( h^{\per,\varepsilon}_0,0;2\alpha t \varepsilon^{-1} + \beta(\alpha)z\varepsilon^{-\frac{2}{3}},2(1-q)^{-1}\varepsilon^{-1}t) \Big) 
\end{align*} whenever the argument for $h^{\textup{patch},\delta}$ is an integer, and linear interpolation otherwise. Here, we obtain $\hfix^{\per,\varepsilon}_0$ from $h^{\per,\varepsilon}_0$ as in \eqref{def:RescaledPeriodicASEPheight}.

[Definition def:resampling_target of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Let $\Gamma$ be a ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} in $D$.  Let $W\subseteq D$ open and $r > 0$. Suppose that we are given the following random variables.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $M^*<\infty$.
\item  A set $\{(\ell_i^1,\ell^2_i)\}_{i=1,\ldots,M^*}$ of pairs of arcs in $\Gamma$ with $\ell_i^1,\ell^2_i \subseteq W$ and such that none of them overlap with each other.
\item A set of $M^*$ points $\underline{y}$ such that
\begin{itemize}
 \item $y_i\in  \ell_i^1\cap \ell^2_i$ and $B(y_i,4r)\subset W$ for $i=1,\ldots,M^*$,
 \item the endpoints of $\ell^1_i, \ell^2_i$ lie outside $B(y_i,4r)$,
 \item $B(y_i,4r)\cap B(y_j,4r)=\varnothing$ and $(\ell_i^1 \cup \ell_i^2) \cap B(y_j,4r) = \varnothing$ for all $i\neq j$.
\end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}
We denote these target pivotals by $\mathfrak F_{W,r} = \{(\ell^1_i,\ell^2_i,y_i)\}_{i=1,\ldots,M^*}$.

If $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}$ is a resampling of $\Gamma$, then we say that $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}$ is $\mathfrak F_{W,r}$-successful if the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
 \item The loops and strands of $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}$ are identical when restricted to the set $D \setminus \bigcup_{i=1}^{M^*} B(y_i,4r)$.
 \item Let $\tau_i^j$ (resp.\ $\overline{\tau}_i^j$) be the first (resp.\ last) time that $\ell_i^j$ is in $\overline{B}(y_i,4 r)$, for $i=1,\ldots,M^*$, $j=1,2$. Then in $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}$ the connections between the four strands $\ell_i^1|_{[0,\tau_i^1]}$, $\ell_i^1|_{[\overline{\tau}_i^1,1]}$, $\ell_i^2|_{[0,\tau_i^2]}$, $\ell_i^2|_{[\overline{\tau}_i^2,1]}$ (assuming that they are parameterized on $[0,1]$) are flipped, i.e.\ the strand $\ell^{{\mathrm{res}},1}_i$ (resp.\ $\ell^{{\mathrm{res}},2}_i$) in $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}$ starting with $\ell_i^1|_{[0,\tau_i^1]}$ (resp.\ finishing with $\ell_i^1|_{[\overline{\tau}_i^1,1]}$) is linked to $\ell_i^2|_{[0,\tau_i^2]}$ or $\ell_i^2|_{[\overline{\tau}_i^2,1]}$. Moreover, it holds again that $\ell^{{\mathrm{res}},1}_i \cap \ell^{{\mathrm{res}},2}_i \cap B(y_i,r) \neq \varnothing$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Target pivotals

Let P be a finite set of mutually independent random variables, and let A_1, ..., A_m be bad events each determined by a subset of variables vbl(A_i). If there exist x_i in [0, 1) such that P(A_i) <= x_i \prod_{j: vbl(A_j) \cap vbl(A_i) \neq \emptyset} (1 - x_j), then the randomized algorithm that repeatedly resamples variables of any violated event terminates in expected time at most sum_{i=1}^m x_i / (1 - x_i) steps with a valid assignment avoiding all bad events.
Events are determined by independent underlying variables
Asymmetric LLL conditions hold

Specifically, the theorem states that an appropriately centered and scaled version of the empirical distribution function converges to a Gaussian process.

Own-work draft, claim w733-T363-017 v1, proof (unaudited), no novelty claim. Let x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4), both labels+1. Train both hidden/output weights of f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j dot x), with no biases, by continuous gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss, using ReLU derivative zero at zero. Assume every initial neuron is either strictly dead on both points (output arbitrary) or has positive output in a strict activation sector. Require at least one neuron active only on x1 and one active only on x2; arbitrary additional positive-output both-active neurons are allowed. A global absolutely continuous flow exists, and every such global flow has convergent normalized parameter direction with global normalized margin sqrt17/16. Trajectory uniqueness at grazing contacts is not asserted. Writing a_i=-ell_prime(f_i), T=integral(a1+a2)dt, surviving both-active squared norm is at most C exp[(4/sqrt17)T], while permanent one-point seeds give total squared norm at least K exp[(sqrt17/4)T], K>0. Their normalized contribution therefore vanishes. After the last strict activation exit, one-point predictions are H_i=alpha_i exp[2a I_i]-beta_i exp[-2a I_i], a=sqrt17/4, I_i=integral a_i dt. The uniform clock trap gives I1-I2-log(alpha2/alpha1)/(2a)->0 and hence H1/H2->1. For iid hidden/output N(0,sigma^2) coordinates, any sigma>0, put p=atan(1/4)/pi. The exact probability of this sufficient global family is H_m=((1+p)/2)^m-2(1/4+p)^m+(3p/2)^m. The previous no-both-active family has mass G_m=(1/2)^m-2(1/4+p/2)^m+p^m, so H_m-G_m is the added mixed-positive family mass. This labels56 additional signed permutation orbits at widths2..6 (0,1,5,15,35), leaving2713 of the prior2994 orbits unclassified. These are sufficient-family probabilities, not total global/bad basin probabilities. Fifty-six conditional scale1e-6 simulations support the theorem but do not independently certify it. Live negative-output neurons and patterns missing one-point seeds are outside the statement.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:2435eb502e588caced75f502ddb4e6475ad92deeea6fb3c6d286a7fcb14c3255","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/24/2435eb502e588caced75f502ddb4e6475ad92deeea6fb3c6d286a7fcb14c3255.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:6612e8be5286dcb85c1c995f251a976a35e4a7937f2be28a3fa1e14027739ceb","bundle_entry_key":"mixed-positive-one-point-seeds-global-margin","bundle_id":"population.relu-mixed-positive-one-point-seeds-global-margin","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"neural-network implicit bias","draft":"w733/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.implicit_bias:relu-two-point-mixed-positive-sectors-one-point-seeds-global-margin","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Mixed positive ReLU sectors with two permanent seeds reach global margin

Claim w733-T363-017 v1. Target2; kind narrowed. Proof (unaudited); executed checks complete; independent review pending. No novelty claim.

## Statement
Let x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4), labels+1, and f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j dot x), with no biases and both layers trained by gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss. Initially each neuron is either strictly dead on both inputs (output arbitrary) or has positive output and lies in a strict activation sector. Assume at least one positive-output x1-only neuron (A) and one positive-output x2-only neuron (B). Any number of additional positive-output both-active neurons (C) is allowed, without the collective barrier of claim013.

A global absolutely continuous flow exists under the convention ReLU'(0)=0. Every global absolutely continuous flow under this convention has convergent normalized parameter direction and reaches normalized margin sqrt17/16, the global maximum. Uniqueness of the trajectory at grazing contacts is not asserted. This is a whole activation-pattern family, not a radial subcone.

## 1. Positive outputs, finite sector changes, and existence
Put z_ij=w_j dot x_i and a_i=-ell'(f_i)>0. For live positive-output neurons, vdot=sum_i a_i ReLU(z_i)>=0. For A, z1dot=(17/16)a1*v>0 and z2dot=-(15/16)a1*v<0, while v increases. Thus A stays strictly A forever; the B rule is symmetric. Dead neurons remain constant. These are the no-return equations recorded in claim015.

For C, writing w=(u,y), ydot=v(a1+a2)/4>0. Hence a first C-boundary hit cannot make both preactivations zero, since C initially has y>0. A strict exit therefore enters A or B, after which no further activation change is possible. There are at most m such strict exits, including simultaneous exits counted per neuron.

Existence can be constructed by finite smooth phases. Follow the smooth vector field with the current masks until a first boundary hit. At a hit z2=0,z1>0, choose the A continuation: its normal derivative is -(15/16)a1*v<0, so the smooth A-mask solution is strictly A immediately afterward. Treat all simultaneous hits the same way, with the appropriate index. The symmetric construction applies at the other boundary, including a grazing incoming C trajectory. Each such continuation removes one or more C neurons. No dead or existing one-point neuron hits a boundary. With at most m removals, this constructs an absolutely continuous trajectory satisfying the prescribed vector field almost everywhere.

No finite-time blowup obstructs this construction. If N=sum_j(v_j^2+||w_j||^2), a=||x_i||=sqrt17/4, and A=a1+a2, then

    Ndot=4 sum_j v_j sum_i a_i ReLU(z_ij) <= 2a A N.

All predictions are nonnegative, so a_i<=1 and Ndot<=4aN. Thus bounded-time smooth phases have bounded parameters and can continue up to a boundary or indefinitely.

The conclusion also applies to any other global absolutely continuous continuation, even one that grazes and returns to C. At z2=0,z1>0 the prescribed zero-derivative vector field gives z2dot=-(15/16)a1*v<0. The derivative of an absolutely continuous real function is zero almost everywhere on one of its level sets; consequently such boundary times have measure zero. The same holds at z1=0. Before a strict exit a surviving C neuron therefore obeys the C-mask equations almost everywhere. Each strict exit is irreversible. After the last of the finitely many strict exits, all sector equations have fixed masks almost everywhere. Choose a finite base time b after that last exit and outside the null boundary sets. The proof below applies to every such continuation, not just the constructed one.

## 2. A slower norm exponent for surviving C neurons
Reset clocks at b: I_i(t)=integral_b^t a_i(s)ds, T=I1+I2. Let S_C be the total squared norm of the remaining C neurons. Claim016's cone estimate gives

    S_C <= S_C(b) exp(kappa T), kappa=4/sqrt17.

For completeness, if y>=4|u| then 0<=w dot x_i <= (2/sqrt17)||w||. For x1 its squared certificate is

    (4/17)(u^2+y^2)-(u+y/4)^2
      = (y-4u)(47y+52u)/272 >=0.

The x2 case substitutes -u. Since n_dot=4v sum_i a_i z_i for a C neuron and 2v||w||<=n, n_dot<=kappa A n. Gronwall proves the estimate. C predictions c_i consequently satisfy 0<=c_i<=S_C/sqrt17.

The permanent A/B seeds give N>=K exp(aT), K>0, by the exact one-point formula (q+v)=(q(b)+v(b))exp(aI_i), q=w dot x_i/a. Thus

    S_C/N <= (S_C(b)/K) exp[-T/(4sqrt17)] ->0,

provided T tends to infinity. It does: Ndot<=2a A N implies bounded T would bound N and both predictions, which would keep A bounded away from zero on the infinite physical-time solution. This contradicts bounded T. The exact exponent gap is a-kappa=1/(4sqrt17)>0.

## 3. The imbalance trap (load-bearing new step)
At time b both one-point sectors are nonempty. In sector i use q_j=w_j dot x_i/a>0, s_j=q_j(b)+v_j(b)>0, d_j=q_j(b)-v_j(b). Perpendicular hidden coordinates remain constant, and the exact sector contribution is

    H_i = alpha_i exp(2aI_i) - beta_i exp(-2aI_i),
    alpha_i=(a/4)sum_j s_j^2>0, beta_i=(a/4)sum_j d_j^2>=0.

In fact alpha_i>beta_i because all v_j(b),q_j(b) are positive. The full predictions are f_i=H_i+c_i. Define

    delta=log(alpha2/alpha1)/(2a),
    D=I1-I2-delta.

Fix epsilon>0. On D>=epsilon, the leading one-point terms satisfy

    alpha1 exp(2aI1)-alpha2 exp(2aI2)
       >= gamma_epsilon exp(aT),
    gamma_epsilon=2 sqrt(alpha1*alpha2) sinh(a*epsilon)>0.

Indeed their ratio is exp(2aD), and I1=(T+delta+D)/2. The decaying term in H1 has magnitude at most beta1; the positive decaying term from -H2 can be discarded. Hence uniformly on D>=epsilon,

    f1-f2 >= gamma_epsilon exp(aT)-beta1
                -(2/sqrt17)S_C(b)exp(kappa T) -> +infinity.

The reflected argument gives f2-f1 tending uniformly to infinity on D<=-epsilon. This is where the strict exponent gap kappa<a is essential; a mere o(N) assertion without this uniform estimate would not suffice.

For exponential loss a1/a2=exp[-(f1-f2)]. For logistic loss, because f2>=0,

    a1/a2=(1+exp(f2))/(1+exp(f1)) <=2exp[-(f1-f2)].

Thus, for all sufficiently large T, on D>=epsilon we have a1/a2<=1/3 and

    dD/dT=(a1-a2)/(a1+a2)<=-1/2.

On D<=-epsilon the derivative is at least1/2. The continuous D clock enters [-epsilon,epsilon] in finite additional T and cannot exit after these inward inequalities hold. Since epsilon is arbitrary, D->0. Therefore I1,I2->infinity and H1/H2->1.

## 4. Direction, margin, and global optimality
The hyperbolic sector formula gives N_i/H_i->2/a for each one-point sector: q_j and v_j both have leading term (s_j/2)exp(aI_i), while their difference decays and perpendicular coordinates stay bounded. Since S_C/N->0, dead norms are constant, and H1/H2->1,

    N ~ (2/a)(H1+H2),  c_i/N->0,
    min(f1,f2)/N -> a/4 = sqrt17/16.

The whole normalized direction converges. Within each sector, q_j/sqrt(N) and v_j/sqrt(N) tend to s_j/(2 sqrt(sum_sector s^2)); hidden perpendicular components vanish. Each sector occupies half the limiting squared norm. C and dead parameter components vanish after normalization.

This is the known global margin value for the two-point example. A short norm certificate is: ReLU(w.x1)+ReLU(w.x2) is the maximum of w dotted with 0,x1,x2,x1+x2. The largest norm of these four vectors is a. Therefore for arbitrary signed output weights, f1+f2<=a sum_j |v_j| ||w_j||<=aN/2, and min(f1,f2)/N<=a/4. The limit attains this upper bound.

## 5. Exact Gaussian family mass and width2..6 pattern inventory
Assume every hidden/output coordinate is independently N(0,sigma^2), sigma>0. Let p=atan(1/4)/pi and q=1/4-p/2. Probabilities of A+, B+, C+, and dead neurons with arbitrary output are respectively q,q,p/2,p. Thus the exact probability of the theorem's family (A+ and B+ both present; only these four categories) is

    H_m=((1+p)/2)^m -2(1/4+p)^m +(3p/2)^m.

This holds at every scale, including sigma=1e-6. The previous no-C family of claim009 has mass

    G_m=(1/2)^m -2(1/4+p/2)^m +p^m.

The added mixed family, with at least one C+, has exact mass H_m-G_m. It is zero at width2 and positive for every width>=3. These are sufficient GLOBAL-family masses, not total global or bad basin probabilities.

Resolving dead output signs produces five allowed types A+,B+,C+,D+,D-. With A+ and B+ mandatory the number of permutation orbits at width m is binom(m+2,4). Requiring C+ too adds binom(m+1,4) previously unlabelled orbits: at widths2..6 these are0,1,5,15,35, totaling56. This does not change any label for a negative-output live neuron. The earlier inventory has2994 total orbits,20 known bad-source orbits,135 nonfitting orbits,70 no-C global orbits, and2769 unclassified. Adding these56 disjoint global orbits leaves2713 unclassified. The old inventory is preserved; changes belong in a separate overlay.

## Verification and limits
Geometry/setup source: Vardi, Shamir and Srebro, On Margin Maximization in Linear and ReLU Networks, arXiv:2110.02732v4, Theorem3.2 and AppendixC.3. Earlier diagnostics and claims009/015 are taken as ground where cited, not independently audited here. The work in this round is the mixed-sector suppression and uniform clock trap; no literature novelty is claimed.

The proof still requires independent review, particularly the global continuation at grazing contacts and the uniform imbalance trap. Finite rational checks and floating-point simulations can support its algebra and examples but cannot independently certify the full dynamical theorem. No Lean certificate has been obtained. Full Gaussian basin classification, especially negative-output live neurons and patterns without both permanent seeds, remains open.


## Executed checks for claim017 v1
scripts/mixed_positive_checks.py passed the exact rational coefficient identity for the cone bound,164 cone-point checks including both edges, the exponent-gap coefficient1/68, hyperbolic identities, and an independent multinomial enumeration of Gaussian mass polynomials. An incorrect cone constant is rejected, and doubling the C exponent fails the strict exponent-gap test. The exact enumeration finds56 additional signed permutation orbits and2713 remaining unclassified orbits. All decimal mass evaluations in the log are estimates; the event formulas and rational polynomial coefficients are exact.

The56 newly labelled patterns (widths3..6) each received one conditional isotropic Gaussian initialization at scale1e-6, seed733368. The full original exponential-loss gradient ODE was integrated in log(1+t) to40, rtol1e-9, atol1e-16, maxstep.02, with two auxiliary loss clocks. Maximum final margin error from sqrt17/16 was5.83e-8; maximum clock-imbalance residual was8.51e-8. The norm-suppression inequality held at accepted nodes. These are floating-point probes, not rigorous bounds, continuous event certificates, or frequency estimates. No logistic simulations were run. The script checkpoints each case to logs/mixed_positive_flow.jsonl; summary and exact algebra/mass results are in logs/mixed_positive_flow_summary.json and logs/mixed_positive_exact_checks.json. On the uniform cube {-1, 1}^n let f be real, f^(S) = E[f chi_S] its Walsh coefficients and W_k = sum over |S| = k of f^(S)^2. For rho in [-1, 1], T_rho is the noise operator: T_rho f(x) = E[f(Y)] where the Y_i are independent with P(Y_i = x_i) = (1 + rho)/2, so T_rho chi_S = rho^|S| chi_S. For a rho-correlated pair (X uniform, Y the noisy copy), Stab_rho[f] = E[f(X) f(Y)] = <f, T_rho f> = sum_S rho^|S| f^(S)^2 = sum_k rho^k W_k. So the level weights are W_m = S^(m)(0)/m! for the polynomial S(rho) = Stab_rho[f], with S(1) = ||f||^2, S(0) = (E f)^2 and S(-1) = E[f(X) f(-X)]. On [0, 1], r -> Stab_r[f] is nondecreasing and convex; it is strictly increasing iff f is not constant, and strictly convex iff some level k >= 2 carries weight. For f with values +-1 and Y obtained by flipping each bit independently with probability delta, P(f(X) != f(Y)) = (1 - Stab_{1 - 2 delta}[f])/2 = (1/2) sum_S (1 - (1 - 2 delta)^|S|) f^(S)^2.

Status: proof (unaudited); owner-work claim T410-w739-C006 version 2; independent review pending. Fix h protected inputs, independent fair truth bits b_y, and independent uniform unique-witness locations r_y in a set of size M. Witness queries return 1 exactly at (y,r_y) with b_y=1. For every fixed deterministic adaptive Q-query algorithm, with arbitrary fixed auxiliary answers independent of all protected bits AND witness locations, the probability of guessing all h bits is at most 2^-h(1+1/M)^Q. For T fixed circuit descriptions making at most q witness queries per input the all-correct probability is at most T*2^-h(1+1/M)^(h*q). If the auxiliary oracle is selected, even as a function of the hidden variables, from at most 2^a fixed reference oracles independent of the hidden variables, multiply this bound by 2^a. For independent length-n blocks with h_n=2^floor(n/2) and M_n=2^(n^2), the resulting witness-existence language is in NP^O but not P^O/poly almost surely, for every fixed independent auxiliary oracle. The latter conclusion also holds if, conditional on all other blocks, the full auxiliary oracle ranges over at most 2^a(n) fixed independent references with a(n) polynomial. Polynomial-length individual oracle answers do not imply this total-leakage condition. No required sampling/inversion interfaces or common oracle for T410 Target 2 are constructed; no novelty priority is claimed.
Auxiliary oracle and unprotected answers independent of every protected truth bit AND witness location
Circuit-description and query counts as specified in proof
Leakage extension: at most 2^a fixed reference auxiliary oracles, not merely polynomial-length individual answers
