Put ell=1/(2sqrt(k)), A=1/12, Q=[-ell/2,ell/2]^k, and b(t)=64t^3(1-t)^3 on [0,1], zero outside. For n>=1 put h=ell/n and partition Q into n^k cells with lower corners c_i. For every sigma in {-1,+1}^(n^k), define f_sigma(x)=A h^2 sum_i sigma_i product_j b((x_j-c_ij)/h), T_sigma(x,z)=(x,z+f_sigma(x)), Vn=area(T_sigma(M0)), and t_n=(V0/Vn)^(1/k). Let mu_(sigma,n) be exactly uniform surface probability on t_n T_sigma(M0), isometrically embedded into R^D. There are constants C,W0 depending only on k,D and this fixed base such that, for W>=W0, a common scalar-input ReLU feedforward DAG architecture with at most W charged edge weights and biases has sup_(n,sigma) inf_theta W1((G_theta)#Unif[0,1],mu_(sigma,n))<=C W^(-4/k), with depth O(W). All fixed coefficients are charged; absent edges are absent; skip connections, unrestricted real weights and discontinuous target-to-weight assignments are allowed. The exact squared-gradient graph area density is C2 across every cell face with bounds independent of n; uniformly positive C2 chart densities have uniformly C2 inverse triangular transports. Apply Yarotsky-Zhevnerchuk Theorem 3.3 (arXiv:1906.09477, p.5) at r=2,d=k, then a logarithmic-size tent-map scalar-source conversion and a fixed finite chart mixture with positive-time connectors. The source-conversion coupling uses the exact smooth map Lipschitz constant, not the coding network Lipschitz constant. This is a candidate theorem only for this entire explicit packing family, not all reach-bounded C2 surfaces. No bounded-bit, efficient weight-computation, complete T339 solution or novelty claim is made.

body:
For an integral operator T_k on L^2 with kernel k, the formula tr T_k = integral of k(x,x) dx is not a definition and not automatic. (1) An L^2 kernel is an equivalence class modulo null sets, and on a nonatomic space the diagonal is a null set, so k(x,x) has no meaning at all without choosing a distinguished representative; different representatives give different 'diagonal integrals'. (2) Continuity of the kernel is not enough for trace class. Carleman's example: there are continuous 2pi-periodic functions g whose Fourier coefficients are not absolutely summable. The convolution operator (T f)(x) = (1/(2 pi)) times the integral over the circle of g(x - y) f(y) dy has the continuous kernel k(x,y) = g(x - y)/(2 pi), is normal with eigenvalues the Fourier coefficients of g and eigenfunctions the exponentials, so its singular values are the moduli of those coefficients; hence T is Hilbert-Schmidt but not trace class, while the naive diagonal integral is the finite number g(0). (3) What does hold: if T is trace class on L^2([a,b]) and has a continuous kernel on [a,b] x [a,b], then tr T = integral of k(x,x) dx; and by Mercer's theorem, if k is continuous, symmetric and positive semidefinite on a compact interval (more generally on a compact metric space with a finite Borel measure of full support), then the associated operator is trace class, the eigenfunction series converges absolutely and uniformly, and tr T = integral of k(x,x) dx = sum of the eigenvalues. So the safe routes are positivity plus continuity (Mercer), or an independent proof of trace class plus continuity; 'the kernel is nice' by itself is not a proof.
the operator is trace class, or the kernel is continuous and positive semidefinite (Mercer) on a compact space with a finite Borel measure of full support
the kernel is a continuous representative, so that its diagonal values are defined
an L^2 kernel alone determines only a Hilbert-Schmidt operator, whose diagonal is undefined

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2608.11071, 'Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents'] For each $\kappa,\alpha, n>0$, there exists a non-negative function $\psi\in C^3[-n^{1/4}\kappa,0]$ such that the following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The function $\psi$ solves the ODE (Stein's equation)
    \begin{equation}
        \psi''(z)-\alpha z^3 \psi'(z)=-1,
        
    \end{equation}
    with boundary conditions $\psi'(-n^{1/4}\kappa)=\psi(0)=0$.
     \item We have $\psi'(z)\leq 0$ for all $z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa, 0]$ and $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa, 0]}|\psi'(z)|<C_1$ for some positive constant $C_1$ independent of $n$.
    \item We have $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa, 0]}\psi(z)<C_2$ for some positive constant $C_2$ independent of $n$.
    \item  For all sufficiently large $n$ we have $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa,0]}|\psi'''(z)|=\alpha\kappa^3n^{3/4}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Dfn 4 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] Let $\lambda = [\lambda(0), \lambda(1), \cdots, \lambda(m)]$ be a path of length $m$ in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$. We define the chronological loop-erasure of $\lambda$, denoted by $\text{LE} (\lambda)$, in the following manner. First, set
$$ t_0 \coloneqq \max\{t \ge 0 \, : \, \lambda(t) = \lambda(0)\}.$$
For each $i \geq 1$, define
$$ t_i \coloneqq \max\{t \ge 0 \, : \, \lambda(t) = \lambda(t_{i-1}+1)\}. $$
Let 
$$n = \min\{i \, : \, t_i = m\}.$$
    Then, the chronological loop-erasure of $\lambda$ is given by
    $$\text{LE} (\lambda) \coloneqq [\lambda(t_0), \lambda(t_1), \ldots, \lambda(t_n)].$$

Let X_1, \dots, X_n be independent random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_k] = 0 and \text{Var}(X_k) = \sigma_k^2 < \infty. Let S_k = \sum_{j=1}^k X_j. Then for every \epsilon > 0, \mathbb{P}\left( \max_{1 \le k \le n} |S_k| \ge \epsilon \right) \le \frac{1}{\epsilon^2} \sum_{k=1}^n \sigma_k^2 = \frac{\text{Var}(S_n)}{\epsilon^2}.

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] We have $S_1\sim\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}(n-\sqrt{n})^{1/2}$
    \begin{proof}
        We may compute $S_1$ explicitly. We have, via a combinatorial identity,
        \[S_1=\frac{n-2m-3}{2^{n-2m-4}}\binom{n-2m-4}{\frac{n}{2}-m-2}\]
        By a special case of Stirling's estimate, we have
        \[\binom{n}{n/2}\sim 2^n(\pi n/2)^{-1/2}\] 
        This gives
        \[S_1\sim \frac{(n-2m-3)(2^{n-2m-4})}{(2^{n-2m-4})\sqrt{\pi(\frac{n}{2}-m-2)}}=\frac{(n-2m-3)}{\sqrt{\pi(\frac{n}{2}-m-2)}}\]
        \[=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\left(\frac{n-2m-3}{\sqrt{n-2m-4}}\right)\]
        \[=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\left(\frac{n-\left\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\right\rceil-2}{\sqrt{n-\left\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\right\rceil-3}}\right)\]
        \[\sim\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}(n-\sqrt{n})^{1/2}\]
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a nonnegative random variable X, typically a count of some combinatorial structure written as X = sum_i X_i for indicator random variables X_i, the Paley-Zygmund inequality gives P(X > 0) >= (E[X])^2 / E[X^2]. Expanding E[X^2] = E[X] + sum_{i != j} E[X_i X_j], the method succeeds in proving P(X>0) is bounded away from 0 exactly when the pair-correlation sum sum_{i != j} E[X_i X_j] is of the same order as (E[X])^2, that is, when correlations between the indicators do not overwhelm the square of the mean. This is the standard route to existence results, such as an infinite cluster, a long crossing, or a large clique, once a first-moment computation has already established that E[X] is large or diverging, complementing the first-moment method, which by Markov's inequality only ever gives upper bounds on P(X>0). The method does not give any rate of convergence beyond the crude Paley-Zygmund ratio, gives no lower bound at all if the correlation structure is not controlled, and can produce a vacuous (near-0) bound whenever the variance is dominated by rare, strongly correlated configurations even though the mean itself is large. Typical failure: Computing a large or diverging first moment E[X] and declaring existence of the structure without bounding E[X^2]; if the indicators X_i are strongly positively correlated (a common situation for overlapping structures), the pair-correlation term can dominate (E[X])^2, making the Paley-Zygmund bound vacuous even as E[X] -> infinity, which is exactly the situation where a large first moment gives a false sense of near-certain existence. Canonical reference: Paley and Zygmund, 1932, Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society; Alon and Spencer, The Probabilistic Method, fourth edition, Wiley.

the correlation sum not growing asymptotically faster than (E[X])^2

body:
Let P be a locally finite poset, R a nonzero commutative ring with 1, and Q a subset with the induced order. Restricting an element of the incidence algebra I_R(P) to the comparable pairs of Q is a unital R-algebra homomorphism onto I_R(Q) if and only if Q is order-convex: x <= z <= y with x, y in Q forces z in Q. In that case mu_Q(x, y) = mu_P(x, y) for all x <= y in Q.

Finite-dimensional local corollary of van den Berg-Hetebrij-Rink parameterization theorem. Let F be a C^k map, integer k>=2, on a neighborhood of 0 in R^c x R^s, fixing 0, with DF(0)=diag(I_c,A_s) and spectral radius(A_s)<1. Then, after restricting to a neighborhood, there is a C^k center graph h with h(0)=0,Dh(0)=0 and a local C^k center map R, DR(0)=I_c, such that F(u,h(u))=(R(u),h(R(u))) wherever both sides remain local. The graph is parameterized by its center coordinate u. For k=3 this gives a C3 center graph. This assertion is a graph-existence and reduced-map theorem; it does not by itself assert a phase projection or stable foliation for nearby points.

Model: unit-rate rightward TASEP on Z; extra killing at0 at rate kappa>0.

Writing J_i=E[eta_i*(1-eta_(i+1))], stationarity of eta_i gives J_(i-1)-J_i=kappa*1_(i=0)*E eta_0. There is also an exact obstruction to any independent Bernoulli invariant law whose site densities r_i all lie strictly between0 and1. For adjacent sites, subtract the derivative of r_i*r_(i+1) from the generator derivative of E[eta_i*eta_(i+1)]. At a product law the covariance derivative equals J_i*(r_(i+1)-r_i), with killing terms cancelling. Stationarity therefore forces all adjacent densities equal. The one-site balance at0 then forces kappa*r_0=0, a contradiction.

The internal jump i to i+1 leaves eta_i*eta_(i+1) equal to0 both before and after, whereas it changes the two marginal means by -J_i and +J_i. Incoming and outgoing exterior jumps factor under the product law, giving the displayed covariance derivative. Independent killing at0 contributes the same product term in both expressions and cancels.

Strictly interior densities are essential: degenerate empty or blocked measures are not ruled out by dividing by J_i=r_i*(1-r_(i+1)). The invariant-law classification remains open here. [Lem number-crossings-check of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] Consider an annulus $A(x;r,2r)$. Let $\check{F}_1(\check{M})$ be the event that there are at most $\check{M}$ distinct clusters (open or closed) that cross this annulus. If there exist both an open crossing and a closed crossing of $A(x;r,2r)$, then for any open (resp.\ closed) cluster that crosses this annulus, one can find two (not necessarily disjoint) open (resp.\ closed) crossings of the annulus $\eta_c$ and $\eta_a$ that serve as the clockwise most and counterclockwise most boundaries of this cluster. 
Define the event $\check{F}_2(\check{b})$ as follows. If there are at least 2 crossing clusters of $A(x;r,2r)$, then for every open (resp.\ closed) crossing cluster of $A(x;r,2r)$, let $v$ be the endpoint of $\eta_a$ on the inner boundary of $A(x;r,2r)$. On $\check{F}_2$, we require that there exists an open (resp.\ closed) path from $\eta_a$ to the inner boundary of $A(x;r,2r)$ that stays at distance at least $10\check{b}r$ away from $v$. We also require the same assertion when we swap $\eta_a$ with $\eta_c$. In particular, this implies that for points $v$ that are the endpoints of the interfaces of crossing clusters at the inner boundary of $\check{A}$, no crossing clusters apart from the ones whose interface $v$ is on enter the box $B(v,10\check{b}r)$. 

The following holds for $R$ large enough. For each $\check{p}>0$, there exist $\check{M}$ large enough and $\check{b}>0$ small enough so that $$\mathbf{P}\!\left(\check{F}_1(\check{M})\cap \check{F}_2(\check{b})\right)\geq 1-\check{p}$$ for all annuli $A(x;r,2r)$ of radius $r\geq \frac{R}{\check{b}n}$.

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] \label[lemma]{lem:induction}
Let $P$ be a Markov operator on a Polish metric space $(\Omega,d)$. Let $G\colon \Omega \to \Hm$ be $L$-Lipschitz
and $H \in  \Hm$. Let $\sigma_\infty(x) \coloneqq \diam \supp P(x,\cdot)$.
Then,
\[
P \tr\exp\left( H + G \right)(x) \le  \tr\exp\left(H + PG(x) + 2 L^2 \sigma_{\infty}^2(x) \Id \right).
\]
title: Lemma 15 of arXiv:2605.24445

\(

\lVert f\rVert_{\ell^r(\Gamma_n(\alpha))}

\]

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.01346, '2609.01346'] For every pair of integers satisfying \eqref{eq:nk-range}, there is a compact
embedded rotational torus $\Sigma^n\subset\R^{n+1}$ whose homothetic
dilations form a shrinking solution of the unnormalised $\sigma_k$-curvature
flow \eqref{eq:sigma-k-flow} in the Sobolev almost-everywhere sense defined in
Section~\ref{sec:weak}.  More precisely, $\Sigma$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item The torus is smooth away from two rotational latitudes and satisfies
  $\langle X,\nu\rangle=-\sigma_k(S)$ there.
  \item If $\Omega$ is the bounded domain enclosed by $\Sigma$ and
  $S_{\mathrm w}$ is the weak shape operator of $\partial\Omega=\Sigma$, then
  $\langle X,\nu\rangle=-\sigma_k(S_{\mathrm w})$ almost everywhere with
  respect to the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal H^n$.
  \item Set $X_t=((k+1)(T-t))^{1/(k+1)}X$ and
  $\Sigma_t=X_t(M)$.  If $\nu_t$ and $S_{\mathrm w,t}$ are the outward unit
  normal and weak shape operator of $\Sigma_t$, respectively, then
  $\langle\partial X_t/\partial t,\nu_t\rangle
  =\sigma_k(S_{\mathrm w,t})$ at $\mathcal H^n$-almost every point, for every
  $t<T$.
  \item Its profile curve has H\"older regularity $C^{1,1/k}$ and belongs
  to the Sobolev class $W^{2,p}$ for every $1\leq p<k/(k-1)$.
\end{enumerate}
If $s$ is arclength along the profile curve and $s_0$ is either singular
parameter, then the profile curve is
not $C^2$ at $s_0$, and the magnitude of its meridional principal curvature
is asymptotic to a positive multiple of $|s-s_0|^{-(k-1)/k}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.01346

This is ONLY the chi-square projection-ratio component of C004. It is not
the full ReLU transition, which also contains Q, flips, and arctan terms.

Let k be Bin(n,1/2). On n/3<=k<=2n/3 let S and R be independent
chi-square variables with respectively k and k-1 degrees of freedom and
M=sqrt(S/R). Off this central-k event put M=1. For fixed 0<d<K and bounded
C^5 f with bounded derivatives through order five, uniformly for u in [d,K],

    n E[f(uM)-f(u)] = 2u f'(u)+u^2 f''(u)
        +(1/n)[10u f'(u)+11u^2 f''(u)+4u^3 f'''(u)
                            +(u^4/2)f''''(u)] + O_(f,d,K)(n^(-3/2)). (B)

The exact conditional raw moments, for k large enough, are

    E M     = (k-1)/(k-2),
    E M^2   = k/(k-3),
    E M^3   = (k^2-1)/[(k-2)(k-4)],
    E M^4   = k(k+2)/[(k-3)(k-5)].                  (G)

These follow from E(chi-square_r)^z=2^z Gamma(r/2+z)/Gamma(r/2),
independence, and Gamma(x+1)=x Gamma(x). In particular the first formula
is exact; approximating its two gamma ratios separately is unnecessary.
Expansion in 1/k gives

    E(M-1)   =1/k+2/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^2 =1/k+5/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^3 =6/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^4 =3/k^2+O(k^-3).

For central binomial k,

    E[1/k; central]=2/n+2/n^2+O(n^-3),
    E[1/k^2; central]=4/n^2+O(n^-3).

For example expand around mu=n/2 with k-mu, whose odd central moments

    2/n+10/n^2+O(n^-3),
    2/n+22/n^2+O(n^-3),
    24/n^2+O(n^-3),
    12/n^2+O(n^-3).

S/k and R/k. There, M-1 is Lipschitz in their centered deviations and has
fifth absolute moment of this order. The chi-square exponential tails,
Holder, and higher inverse moments on central k bound the omitted part
exponentially. This is possible for all sufficiently large n, since k
then exceeds every fixed inverse-moment threshold used.

1/n in the scaled generator, exactly the same order as the signed third
moment term. Therefore a derivation using only a third-order Taylor term
cannot give the complete weak 1/n correction, even before ReLU flips.

This partial expansion does not upgrade C004's full O(n^-1/2) error to
O(1/n). The unresolved pieces are the mixed baseline/flip moments and
angular geometry terms, uniformly enough to match the singular entrance.

[Lemma area Lemma of arXiv:2605.29095, 'Asymptotics of the number of components of random polynomial lemniscates'] [Area Theorem] [Ahlfors], [crane-polynomialpreimage] 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item Let \( f \) be a univalent (injective holomorphic) function on a domain \( D \subseteq \mathbb{C} \), and let \( K \subset D \) be a measurable set. Then the area of the image \( f(K) \) is given by:
\[
\text{Area}\big(f(K)\big) = \int_K |f'(z)|^2 \, dA(z),
\]
where \( dA(z) = dx \, dy \) denotes the Euclidean area element in \( \mathbb{C} \).
\item Let \( p \) be a polynomial of degree \( n \) over \( \mathbb{C} \), and let \( K \) be any measurable subset of the complex plane. Let \( n(z, p, K) \) be the number of preimages of \( z \) under \( p \) that lie in \( K \) counted with multiplicity. Then,
\begin{align}
    \int_{\mathbb{C}} n(z, p, K)\, dA(z) = \int_K |p'(z)|^2\, dA(z).
\end{align}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition infinity squared of arXiv:2608.25889, 'Slope Inequalities for the Geography Problem of Spin Symplectic 4-Manifolds'] We say that a smooth oriented $4$-manifold $M$\/ has $\infty$-\emph{property}\/ if there exist infinitely many pairwise nondiffeomorphic irreducible smooth $4$-manifolds
that are all homeomorphic to $M$.  
We say that $M$\/ has $\infty^2$-\emph{property}\/ if there exist infinitely many pairwise nondiffeomorphic irreducible symplectic $4$-manifolds and infinitely many pairwise nondiffeomorphic irreducible nonsymplectic $4$-manifolds, all of which are homeomorphic to $M$.  
We also say that a symmetric bilinear form has $\infty$-\emph{property}\/ or $\infty^2$-\emph{property}\/ if it is the intersection form of a 
simply connected smooth $4$-manifold with $\infty$-\emph{property}\/ or $\infty^2$-property, respectively.

[Lemma L:basis-for-comparison of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take $x \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $y_1 \le y_2 \in \mathbb{Z}, t \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $[x,1]_{\textsf{L}}\le [y_1,t]_{\textsf{L}}$ and $[x,1]_{\textsf{L}}\le [y_2,t]_{\textsf{L}}$, and take $f:\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$. Then for any $E:\mathbb{Z}^2\to\mathbb{R}$,
$$
E[x, 1; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E[x, 1; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}} \le E^f[0,0; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E^f[0,0; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}},
$$
on the event where a geodesic in $E^f$ from $[0,0]_{\textsf{L}}$ to $[y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}}$ intersects $\{[r, 1]_{\textsf{L}} : r \ge x\}$. Similarly, 
$$
E[x, 1; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E[x, 1; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}} \ge E^f[0,0; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E^f[0,0; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}},
$$
on the event where a geodesic in $E^f$ from $[0,0]_{\textsf{L}}$ to $[y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}}$ intersects $\{[r, 1]_{\textsf{L}} : r \le x\}$.

Let $X$ be $n$ i.i.d. rows in $\mathbb{R}^M$ with covariance $\Sigma$. Split the rows into two independent parts of sizes $m$ and $n - m$ with sample covariances $S_1 = V_1\Lambda_1 V_1^T$ and $S_2$. The nonparametric eigenvalue-regularised covariance estimator is $\hat\Sigma = V_1 \operatorname{diag}(V_1^T S_2 V_1)\, V_1^T$, averaged over $K$ random splits. Then: (i) $\mathbb{E}[V_1^T S_2 V_1 \mid V_1] = V_1^T \Sigma V_1$, so each diagonal entry $v_i^T S_2 v_i$ is an unbiased estimate of the population variance in the direction $v_i$ - the Ledoit-Peche oracle $d_i^* = v_i^T\Sigma v_i$ evaluated on independent data; (ii) as $M, n \to \infty$ with $M/n \to c > 0$ and $m/n \to r \in (0,1)$, $\hat\Sigma$ is asymptotically optimal in Frobenius loss among estimators of the form $V_1 D V_1^T$ with $D$ diagonal (Lam 2016, Theorem 1); (iii) $\hat\Sigma$ is positive semidefinite and carries no bandwidth, floor or shrinkage constant beyond the split fraction (Lam recommends choosing $m$ by minimising $\|\hat\Sigma_m - S\|_F$ over a grid; $m = n/2$ is the usual default). A population direction of genuinely small variance keeps a small estimate (its held-out variance is small too); a direction whose small sample variance was a finite-sample cancellation receives the variance it actually has out of sample.
rows i.i.d. with finite fourth moments
M/n -> c > 0, m/n -> r in (0,1)
the two parts of the split are disjoint (independence of V_1 and S_2 is what carries the argument)

Let X be a compact Hausdorff space and let A be a subalgebra of C(X, R), the continuous real functions with the supremum norm, such that A contains the constant functions and separates points (for x != y in X there is f in A with f(x) != f(y)). Then A is dense in C(X, R). Complex form: a subalgebra of C(X, C) that contains the constants, separates points, and is closed under complex conjugation is dense in C(X, C). The Weierstrass approximation theorem is the case X = [a, b] with A the polynomials: every continuous real function on [a, b] is a uniform limit of polynomials.

[Defi 59 of arXiv:2510.22783, 'Universality of Cutoff for Riffle Shuffling'] The string $s\in [k]_0^{K}$ is \textbf{collision-likely} (we write $s\in \CL$) if $s$ satisfies the following properties.
		\begin{itemize}
			\item The first $\alpha_{\tot}\log(N)$ digits of $s$ form a collision-likely prefix.
			\item $s[g_1]=\ileft^{(g_1)}$, $s[g_2]=\iright^{(g_2)}$. (Recall \eqref{def:ileft-right}.)
            \item $s[t]=l^{(t)}_{\Max}$ for all $t\in [\alpha_{\tot}+1,\cdots,\alpha_{\tot}+\lfloor2\rho\log N\rfloor]\backslash\{g_1,g_2\}$.
			\item For all $(i,l)\in T$, we have \[
            s \mbox{ contains } \beta_l^{(i)}\log(N) \mbox{ of } l\mbox{-digits in } \{\alpha_{\tot}+\lfloor2\rho\log N\rfloor+1\leq t\leq K: \bn^{(t)}/N\in D_i\}.
            \]
		\end{itemize}

Write $r_x\colon \mathbb{A}\to T_xM$ for the local representative of the anchor, \Cref{loctho}. In the trivialisation we identify
\begin{align} c(t)=(\gamma(t),a(t)),\quad b(t)=(\gamma(t),\beta(t)),  \text{ then define }  \notag\\ 
\mathcal{T}_c(b)(t) = \left( \gamma(t), a(t), r_{\gamma(t)}(\beta(t)), \frac{d\beta}{dt}(t)+C_{\gamma(t)}(a(t),\beta(t)) \right),

[Theorem KALOKAIRI of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $\varrho (N)$ be a sequence of probability measures on
  $\hat{U} (N)$ such that for every $r \in \mathbb{N}$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{N} \log \text{} S_{\varrho (N)}^{U
    (N)} (u_1, \ldots, u_r, 1^{N - r}) = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (u_i),
    
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi$ is an analytic function in a complex neighborhood of $1$ and the above
  convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $1^r$. Then the random measure
  $N^{- 1} \sum_{i = 1}^N \delta \left( \frac{\lambda_i + N - i}{N} \right)$, converges,
  as $N \rightarrow \infty$, in probability, in the sense of moments to a
  deterministic measure $\mathbf{m}$ on $\mathbb{R}$, whose moments are given
  by
  \begin{equation}
    \int_{\mathbb{R}} t^k \mathbf{m} (d \text{} t) = \sum_{m = 0}^k
    \frac{k!}{m! (m + 1) ! (k - m) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} (x^k
    (\Psi' (x))^{k - m}) \right|_{x = 1} . 
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let H be a Hilbert space. (a) If A and B in B(H) are Hilbert-Schmidt, then AB is trace class and ||AB||_1 <= ||A||_2 ||B||_2. (b) Conversely, every trace-class T factors as T = AB with A and B Hilbert-Schmidt: with the polar decomposition T = U|T| take A = U |T|^{1/2} and B = |T|^{1/2}, so that ||A||_2 ||B||_2 = ||T||_1. (c) More generally (Hoelder inequality for Schatten classes) if 1 <= p, q, r <= infinity with 1/r = 1/p + 1/q, and A is in S_p, B in S_q, then AB is in S_r with ||AB||_r <= ||A||_p ||B||_q, where ||X||_p = (sum_n s_n(X)^p)^{1/p} and S_infinity is the compact operators with the operator norm.
H is a Hilbert space
A, B are bounded operators on H, Hilbert-Schmidt in (a)
T is trace class in (b)
exponents satisfy 1/r = 1/p + 1/q with 1 <= p, q, r <= infinity in (c)

body: Bifurcation theory is the mathematical study of changes in the qualitative or topological structure of a given family of curves, such as the integral curves of a family of vector fields, and the solutions of a family of differential equations. Most commonly applied to the mathematical study of dynamical systems, a bifurcation occurs when a small smooth change made to the parameter values of a system causes a sudden "qualitative" or topological change in its behavior. Bifurcations occur in both continuous systems and discrete systems.

body:
Let $E$ be a symmetric $p \times p$ matrix with eigen-decomposition $E = \sum_k \lambda_k u_k u_k^T$ (for instance a sample covariance) and let $C$ be any symmetric $p \times p$ matrix (the population covariance). Among all estimators of the form $\Xi = \sum_k \xi_k u_k u_k^T$ - the same eigenvectors as $E$, free eigenvalues - the Frobenius loss $\|\Xi - C\|_F^2$ is minimized by the oracle choice $\xi_k^{\mathrm{or}} = u_k^T C u_k$, the projection of the population matrix onto the $k$-th sample eigenvector, with minimal loss $\|C\|_F^2 - \sum_k (u_k^T C u_k)^2$. In particular the oracle eigenvalues are convex combinations of the population eigenvalues (they lie between the smallest and largest population eigenvalue) and their sum equals $\operatorname{tr} C$: a rotationally invariant estimator that is optimal in Frobenius loss never moves the trace and always shrinks the spread of the sample spectrum toward the population spread.
E and C symmetric p x p; the estimator class is restricted to the eigenvectors of E

[Thm 11 of arXiv:2512.03884, '2512.03884'] Let $\alpha$ be a quadratic irrational, let $ax^2+bx+c$ be its minimal polynomial with $a,b,c \in \mathbb{Z}$, $\mathrm{gcd}(a,b,c)=1$ and $a>0$, and let $Q(x,y)=ax^2+bxy+cy^2$ be the corresponding binary quadratic form. For any constant $\theta>1$ and any integer $M \ge 1$, we have
\[ \sum_{m=1}^M \frac{1}{m^{\theta} \| m \alpha \|^{\theta}} = c(\alpha, \theta) \log M +O(1) \]
with an implied constant depending only on $\alpha$ and $\theta$. The constant $c(\alpha, \theta)$ is given by
\[ c(\alpha, \theta) = \frac{D^{\theta/2}}{\log \varepsilon} \sum_{\substack{n \in \mathbb{Z} \\ n \neq 0}} \frac{R_Q(n)}{|n|^{\theta}}, \]
where $D=b^2-4ac>0$ is the discriminant, $R_Q(n)$ is the number of primary representations of $n$, and $\varepsilon=(t_0+u_0\sqrt{D})/2$ with the smallest positive solution $(t_0,u_0)$ of Pell's equation $t^2-Du^2=4$.

Own work draft, proof (unaudited), no independent PASS; classical-method application with novelty unverified. Fix theta in (0,pi/2] and unit probe q; teacher w=cos(theta)q+sin(theta)u, u uniform on S^(ell-1) in q-perp, ell=d-1>=2. An unlabeled isotropic Gaussian pool and independent seed select m indices without teacher labels. The learner sees only those m teacher labels, plus q, theta and the unlabeled pool, and outputs a unit linear normal. Conditional on the pool and seed, at most (e*max(1,m/ell))^ell selected-label patterns occur. The latitude cap argument gives expected error at least sin(theta)*(2*(e*max(1,m/ell))^ell)^(-1/(ell-1))/(2*pi). For a rotation-equivariant protocol this applies to each fixed teacher-probe pair. If m/ell->alpha>0 in probability, liminf expected error>=sin(theta)/(2*pi*e*max(1,alpha)), independent of source-pool size. Threshold max-margin is equivariant. The same bound applies to each fixed-fraction deterministic limit and their infimum at retained alpha, excluding an asymptotic exponential envelope at fixed theta>0. No extra unselected labels, label-adaptive selection, or teacher-dependent side information are allowed. No matching upper rate or actual crossover is proved.

Own-work research draft, proof (unaudited). Fix k,D>=1, b>0, K>=0 and 0<lambda<=1<=Lambda. For all b-Lipschitz maps F:[0,1]^k to R^D and probability densities p with lambda<=p<=Lambda and Lip(p)<=K, a common scalar-input ReLU feedforward DAG with at most W charged edge weights and biases achieves sup_(F,p) inf_theta W1((G_theta)#Unif[0,1],F#(p dx))<=C W^(-2/k) for W>=W0. C,W0 depend only on these fixed constants. Depth O(W), unrestricted real weights, skip connections and discontinuous target-to-weight assignments are allowed; every fixed coefficient is charged. Exact inverse triangular sampling has Lipschitz constants bounded by L0=0, Lj=(1+B/c)L_(j-1)+1/c, where c=lambda/Lambda and B=K/lambda+Lambda*K/lambda^2. Apply the known Yarotsky-Zhevnerchuk arXiv:1906.09477 Theorem 3.3 p.5 at r=1,d=k to F composed with that sampler; a logarithmic-size tent-map conversion from scalar noise uses the Lipschitz constant of the exact map, not the coding network. For an (a,b)-bi-Lipschitz C1 chart with Lip(DF)<=M, its exactly uniform surface law satisfies the hypotheses with lambda=(a/b)^k, Lambda=(b/a)^k and K=k*b^(k-1)*M/a^k. This covers controlled C1,1 cube images with boundary. It does not cover arbitrary closed reach-bounded manifolds or merely bounded densities, establish finite-bit rates or optimality, or claim novelty. Independent review and priority assessment pending.
Fixed constants stated above, Euclidean Lipschitz norms, scalar uniform latent source, sparse DAG count including fixed coefficients. Uniform-surface corollary requires an injective bi-Lipschitz chart and a Lipschitz derivative.

body:
[Lemma lem:cesaro_ell of arXiv:2509.03048, 'Elephant random walks on infinite Cayley trees'] Let $p \in [0, 1)$ and $m \ge 1$. There is a constant $\tilde{C}_{p, d, m} > 0$, such that
    \[
        \mathbb{E}|\Xi_n|^m \le (\tilde{C}_{p, d, m})^m \cdot r_n^{-m}.
    \]
    In fact, for any $m \ge 2$, one may take $\tilde{C}_{p, d, m} = \tilde{C}_{p, d} \cdot m$ for some constant $\tilde{C}_{p, d} > 0$. Consequently, for any $u \ge \frac{2\tilde{C}_{p, d}\exp(1)}{r_n}$, one has
    \[
        \mathbb{P}(|\Xi_n| \ge u) \le \exp\bigg(-\frac{ur_n}{\tilde{C}_{p, d}\exp(1)}\bigg).
    \]
title: Lemma lem:cesaro_ell of arXiv:2509.03048

body:
[Thm 3 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional Finsler metric measure manifold. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$.
Then for $p>\frac{n}{2}$ and $K>0$, we have the following inequalities.
\ben
\item[{\rm (1)}] If $0< r\leq R\leq \frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{K}}$, then
\beq
& &\left[\frac{A(R)}{e^{\vartheta R} \sin^{n-1}(\sqrt{K} R)}\right]^{\frac{1}{2p-1}} -\left[\frac{A(r)}{e^{\vartheta r} \sin^{n-1}(\sqrt{K} r)}\right]^{\frac{1}{2p-1}} \nonumber\\
&&  \leq \left(\frac{n-1}{(2p-1)(2p-n)}\right)^{\frac{p-1}{2 p-1}}\left(\left\|{\rm Ric}_{\infty}^{K}\right\|_{p, R, \vartheta}(x_{0})\right)^{\frac{p}{2p-1}} \int_{r}^{R}\left(\frac{1}{\sin (\sqrt{K} s)}\right)^{\frac{n-1}{2p-1}} ds. 
\eeq

\item[{\rm (2)}] If $\frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{K}}<r \leq R <\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{K}}$, then
\beq
&& \left[\frac{A(R)}{e^{\vartheta R} \sin^{n-1}(\sqrt{K} R)}\right]^{\frac{1}{2p-1}}-\left[\frac{A(r)}{e^{\vartheta r} \sin^{n-1}(\sqrt{K} r)}\right]^{\frac{1}{2p-1}}\nonumber\\
&& \leq  \left(\frac{n-1}{(2 p-1)(2 p-n)}\right)^{\frac{p-1}{2p-1}}\left(\left\|{\rm Ric}_{\infty}^{K}\right\|_{p, R, \vartheta}(x_{0})\right)^{\frac{p}{2p-1}} \int_{r}^{R} \frac{1}{\sin^{2}(\sqrt{K} s)} ds. 
\eeq
\een

[Definition 66 of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For a sequence $f=(f_r)_{r\ge0}$ with values in $\Bbbk=\Q(q)$, let
\[
 (Lf)_r=f_{r+1},\qquad (Mf)_r=q^rf_r;
\]
then $LM=qML$.  In one discrete variable, the standard
$q$-Weyl-algebra definition of $q$-holonomicity is equivalent to the
existence of a nonzero recurrence
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a=0}^{d}p_a(q,q^r)f_{r+a}=0,
 \qquad p_a(q,M)\in\Q(q,M),
\end{equation}
after clearing denominators if necessary.  This equivalence and the
multivariate $q$-Weyl-algebra definition used below are recalled in
\cite[Section~3]{GLsurvey}.
title: Definition 66 of arXiv:2608.29585

[Lemma L:abstract-convergence of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $f_n:\mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$ be a sequence of functions satisfying (equation E:MC-lambda of the paper) which converge uniformly on compact sets to continuous limit $f:\mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow \to \mathbb{R}$ which also satisfies (equation E:MC-lambda of the paper). Suppose that additionally $f$ satisfies the following shape bound: 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item For all $c_0 > 0$, there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for all $u = (x, a, t; y, b; t + s) \in \mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow$ with $s < c_0$ we have that
		$$
		\left|f(u) + \frac{(x-y)^2}{s} \right|\le C s^{1/3} \log^2\left(\frac{{2\|u\|_2}}{s}\right).
		$$
	\end{itemize}
	Suppose $\pi_n$ is a sequence of continuous geodesics for $f_n$ between points $(u_n, s)$ to $(v_n, t)$, where the sequence $(u_n, s; v_n, t)$ is precompact in $\mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow$.
	Then:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The sequence $\pi_n$ is precompact in the uniform topology on functions from $[s, t] \to \Lambda$.
		\item If $\pi:[s, t] \to \Lambda$ is a subsequential limit of $\pi_n$, then $\pi$ satisfies (equation E:f-equality of the paper) for any finite set $\{s = t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_k = t\} \subset [s, t]$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma L:abstract-convergence of arXiv:2604.10020

[OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2609.02878 (conjecture environment labelled conj:intro-kpolystable-fibres).] Assume that every fibre \(F_y\) is K-polystable with respect to
\(-K_{F_y}\). Then the finite-time K\"ahler--Ricci flow is Type I:
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{0\le t<T}\sup_{x\in X}
 (T-t)|\Rm(g(t))|_{g(t)}(x)<\infty.
\end{equation}
Moreover, fix \(q\in Y\), and let
\(\omega_{q,{\rm KE}}\in2\pi c_1(F_q)\) be a normalized
K\"ahler--Einstein metric,
\[
 \Ric(\omega_{q,{\rm KE}})=\omega_{q,{\rm KE}}.
\]
Write \(g_{q,{\rm KE}}=2g_{\omega_{q,{\rm KE}}}\), so that
\(\Ric(g_{q,{\rm KE}})=\tfrac12g_{q,{\rm KE}}\). After forgetting the
conjugate heat measures, every Type-I-scale blowup at \(\xi\) based at
\(F_q\) is isomorphic, as a K\"ahler metric flow, to
\begin{equation}
 \left(
 \C^m\times F_q,\,
 J_0\oplus J_{F_q},\,
 g_{\rm E}+(-s)g_{q,{\rm KE}}
 \right)_{s<0}.
\end{equation}
Thus the residual factor is the central fibre with its own complex
structure. (Verbatim from the paper's TeX; symbols are the source paper's. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)
title: Open problem: K-polystable smooth fibres

[Thm 5 (Skorokhod representation theorem) of arXiv:2606.27078, 'Semimartingale Optimal Transport with Jumps: A General Framework and Equivalent Formulatio'] Let $\{\overline{\mathbb{P}}^{n}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq\overline{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}$ be a sequence of probability measures on the enlarged space $\overline{\Omega}$ introduced in Section~2.
Assume that $\overline{\mathbb{P}}^{n}\to \overline{\mathbb{P}}^{0}$ weakly in $\mathcal{P}(\overline{\Omega})$.
Then there exist a probability space $([0,1],\mathcal{B}([0,1]),\lambda)$, where $\lambda$ is the Lebesgue measure, and $\overline{\Omega}$-valued random variables $\{z^{n}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ defined on this space such that
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)] $\lambda\circ(z^{n})^{-1}=\overline{\mathbb{P}}^{n}$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}$.
\item[(2)] $z^{n}\to z^{0}$ pointwise (i.e., in the product topology of $\overline{\Omega}$) $\lambda$-a.s.\ as $n\to\infty$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Skorokhod representation theorem

A Strichartz estimate for a wave equation $\Box_{\bar{g}} \phi = F$ on a curved spacetime $(\bar{M}, \bar{g})$ is an inequality of the form $\|\phi\|_{L^p_t L^q_x(I \times \Sigma)} \le C (\|\phi(0)\|_{H^s(\Sigma)} + \|\partial_t \phi(0)\|_{H^{s-1}(\Sigma)} + \|F\|_{L^{\tilde{p}'}_t L^{\tilde{q}'}_x(I \times \Sigma)})$, where $(p, q)$ and $(\tilde{p}, \tilde{q})$ are wave-admissible exponents satisfying $2/p + (n-1)/q = (n-1)/2 - s$.
g_bar is a Lorentzian metric with bounded geometry
(p, q) is an admissible exponent pair
s is the Sobolev regularity of initial data
title: Strichartz Estimates on Curved Spacetimes

Let X and Y be Banach spaces and T in K(X,Y). If x_n -> x weakly in X, then ||T x_n - T x|| -> 0. Conversely, if X is reflexive and T in B(X,Y) maps every weakly convergent sequence to a norm convergent sequence, then T is compact. Without reflexivity the converse fails (the identity of l^1 maps weakly convergent sequences to norm convergent ones by Schur's property but is not compact).
X and Y are Banach spaces
T is bounded and linear
for the converse, X is reflexive

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C005 v1. Exact obstruction reduction for Target 3, not an escape theorem; no novelty claimed for Gaussian conditioning. Let d>=3, m>=1, eta>0, x_* a deterministic unit vector, A have iid N(0,1) entries, and independently x0~N(0,I_d/d). Use f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2 and unmodified GD. Set e1=x_*, q0=<e1,x0>, rho0=||x0-q0 e1||, e2=(x0-q0 e1)/rho0, E an orthonormal basis of their perpendicular space, g=Ae1, h=Ae2, B=AE, z0=q0*g+rho0*h, v0=z0*(z0^2-g^2) coordinatewise, s=||v0||, u=v0/s, P=I-u*u^T, w=B^T*u, q1=q0-eta*g^T*v0/m, p1=rho0-eta*h^T*v0/m. Excluding null events rho0*s=0, conditional on F1=sigma(x0,g,h,w), z1=A*x1 has Gaussian law with mean mu=q1*g+p1*h-eta*||w||^2*v0/m and covariance tau^2*P, where tau=eta*s*||w||/m. Also w is standard Gaussian in dimension d-2, independently of sigma(x0,g,h). Consequently E[q2|F1]=q1-eta/m sum_i g_i*mu_i*(mu_i^2+3*tau^2*(1-u_i^2)-g_i^2). This retains the residual-direction memory term; centering at q1*g+p1*h with conditionally mean-zero error for the same F1 is false. No claim rules out a different conditioning history or center. At m=ceil(alpha*d), ||w||^2/m converges in probability to 1/alpha for fixed alpha>0. Growing-horizon response and overlap-noise control, and random-start escape, remain open.
fixed deterministic unit signal
iid real standard Gaussian sensing matrix
independent N(0,I_d/d) initialization
d>=3, m>=1, eta>0
quartic loss normalized by 1/(4m)
specified history F1; first reuse only

Conditional counterexample, independent review pending: for kappa>=0, kappa!=6, fix 0<a<b<c and stop in 0<X<Y<Z. Solve locally dX=[2/X-beta]dt-sqrt(kappa)dB and dY=[2/Y-beta]dt-sqrt(kappa)dB with beta=(6-kappa)(1/X+1/Y)/3, X_0=a,Y_0=b. Set W=integral beta dt+sqrt(kappa)B and Z=g_t(c)-W. These X,Y are real Loewner marks for W. For C(u)=B(1/3,1/3)^(-1) integral_0^u [v(1-v)]^(-2/3)dv, C(X/Y) is a local martingale, although W has bracket kappa dt and nonzero drift. The second Cardy observable C(X/Z) has normalized drift (6-kappa)(1/Z-1/Y)/3, which is nonzero. This refutes only one-observable identification, not percolation conformal invariance.

[Defn d.omegatmixing-field of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] \ 
 \begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item  The random field $M=\{M(x)\}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}$ with values in $\mathbb {M} $  
satisfies  {\em $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing correlations}  if
there exists an increasing-decreasing family of 
 functions $\omega_k :  [0, \infty) \to [0,2]$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$, 
(called correlation decay functions), such that $\lim_{s \to \infty}\omega_k(s) = 0$ for all $k \in\mathbb{N}$ and for all $p,q \in \mathbb{N}$, $x_1,\ldots,x_{p+q} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and all $f \in \textnormal{BL}(\mathbb {M} ^p)$, and
  $g \in \textnormal{BL}(\mathbb {M} ^q)$ we have

\begin{align} 
\left| \mathbb {E} [f(\bk {M(x_i)}1{p}) \, g(\bk  {M(x_i)}{p+1}{p+q})] - \mathbb {E} [f(\bk  {M(x_i)}1p)] \, \mathbb {E} [g(\bk  {M(x_i)}{p+1}{p+q})] \right| \le \omega_{p+q}(s),
\end{align}

where $s := d(\bk x1p,\bk x{p+1}{p+q})$ is at (equation defs of the paper).
\item  The random field $M$
satisfies {\em $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations}  if~(equation e.field-mixing of the paper) holds when \textnormal{BL}\ is replaced by $\mathbb{B} $.
 \item  Under Item~(i)  (resp. Item (ii)), the random field  $M$  has  {\em fast $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing correlations}  (resp.  {\em fast $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations}) 
 if $(\omega_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ are fast decreasing. 
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary cor:NS of arXiv:2411.06838, 'Generalized Wasserstein Barycenters'] It holds
\begin{itemize}
	\item[\rm{(i)}] A sequence $(\mu_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ converges to $\mu$ in $\mathcal{P}_2^w(H)$ if and only if
	\[
		(\mu_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}} \text{ converges narrowly in }\mathcal{P}(H_w)\quad \text{and}\quad \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}\int_H |x|^2{\rm d}\mu_n(x) < \infty.
	\]	
	\item[\rm{(ii)}] A set $\mathcal K \subset \mathcal{P}_2(H)$ is relatively sequentially compact in $\mathcal{P}_2^w(H)$ if and only if
	\[
		\sup_{\mu \in \mathcal K}\int_H |x|^2{\rm d}\mu(x) < \infty.
	\]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (X_n)_{n >= 0} be a martingale for a filtration (F_n) and let F_infinity be the sigma-algebra generated by the union of the F_n. The following are equivalent: (i) the family {X_n} is uniformly integrable; (ii) X_n converges almost surely AND in L^1 to some X_infinity; (iii) there exists Y in L^1 with X_n = E[Y | F_n] almost surely for every n, that is the martingale is CLOSED. When these hold one may take Y = X_infinity, and X_infinity = E[Y | F_infinity]. Consequences: for a UI martingale, E[X_infinity] = E[X_0], and the optional stopping identity E[X_tau] = E[X_0] holds for EVERY almost surely finite stopping time tau, with no boundedness assumption on tau or on the martingale - this is a genuinely stronger conclusion than the standard three sufficient conditions (bounded tau, bounded martingale, or E[tau] finite with bounded increments). An L^1-bounded martingale need not be UI, and then only the almost sure half of (ii) survives. For p > 1, an L^p-bounded martingale is automatically UI by de la Vallee Poussin and converges in L^p as well; p = 1 is the exceptional case. [standard; e.g. Williams, Probability with Martingales, Theorems 13.3 and 14.1]
(X_n) a martingale with respect to (F_n)

[Proposition prop:stat of arXiv:2603.20078, '\bf \Large Gated Infinite Server Queues in Light Traffic'] When the condition $\mathbb{E} \sigma_1  = \int_0^\infty \big(1-G(t)\big)dt < \infty$ 
is satisfied then the discrete time Markov chain $\{K_n\}$ is positive recurrent 
and its stationary distribution $\pi$ has finite mean: 
$\sum_{k=1}^\infty k \pi_k < \infty$. Similarly, the sequence of service stages 
posesses a unique stationary distribution $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^+$ which has finite mean 
$\int_0^\infty y dF(y)<\infty$. 

Further, if for some $m>1$ 
$\mathbb{E}[\sigma_1^m]= \int_0^\infty m t^{m-1} \big(1-G(t)\big) dt <\infty$, then 
$\int_0^\infty y^m dF(y)<\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let C be a convex subset of a real vector space X and f: C -> R. f is convex if f(lambda x + (1-lambda) y) <= lambda f(x) + (1-lambda) f(y) for all x, y in C and lambda in [0,1]. If X is a normed space with dual X*, the subdifferential of f at a point x_0 in C is the set partial f(x_0) = {v in X* : f(x) >= f(x_0) + v(x - x_0) for all x in C}, whose elements are called subgradients of f at x_0; partial f(x_0) may be empty, a single point, or contain more than one point. [standard, e.g. Rockafellar, Convex Analysis]

[Definition 8 (Windowed Microcanonical Ensemble) of arXiv:2607.23526, 'Equivalence of Canonical and Microcanonical Ensembles for Euclidean Lattices'] Let $\Delta>0$. For $E\in\R$ and $N\geq1$, denote
\[\Omega_N(E,\Delta):=\{x\in\Lambda^N:E\leq H_N(x)<E+\Delta\},\quad G_N(E,\Delta):=\#\Omega_N(E,\Delta).\]
Whenever $G_N(E,\Delta)>0$, define the windowed microcanonical ensemble as the uniform measure
\[\mu^{\mc}_{N,E,\Delta}(x):=G_N(E,\Delta)^{-1}\one_{\Omega_N(E,\Delta)}(x)\]
on $\Omega_N(E,\Delta)$, and define its entropy as $R_{N,E,\Delta}^{\mc}:=\log G_N(E,\Delta)$.
title: Windowed Microcanonical Ensemble

[Corollary 7 (\textsf{Law of small chaotic blocks}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Fix an order $r\geq1$.  For each $n$, let
$F_{n,1}$, $\ldots$, $F_{n,K_n}$ be independent centered variables in
order-$r$ chaoses
over mutually independent component spaces, 
and
suppose that

\noi
\begin{align}
 X_{n,k}:=F_{n,k}+\theta_{n,k}\in\N_0.
\notag
\end{align}
Put
$F_n:=\sum_{k=1}^{K_n} F_{n,k}$,
$\theta_n:=\sum_{k=1}^{K_n}\theta_{n,k}$, and
$X_n:=F_n+\theta_n$.
In the Poisson setting, assume

\noi
\begin{align}
 \theta_n\to\lambda,
 \quad
 \sum_km_2(F_{n,k})\to\lambda,
 \AND
 \sum_k\cP(F_{n,k})\to0.
\notag
\end{align}
Then $X_n$ converges to $\Pois(\lambda)$ in total variation.  In the
Rademacher setting, the same conclusion holds with $\cP$ replaced by
$\cR$, provided that the maximal coordinate influence $\cM(F_n)$ of $F_n$ tends
to zero. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsf{Law of small chaotic blocks}

body: [Theorem 1.2 (Colorful Tverberg theorem) of arXiv:2607.29403, 'Strong invariants and Tverberg numbers in convexity spaces'] Let $d,t\geq 1$, let $(X,\mathcal{C})$ satisfy $\textup{VC}(\mathcal{C})\leq d$, and let $S_{1},\ldots,S_{d+1}\subseteq X$ be pairwise disjoint finite sets. If $|S_{i}|\geq d(t-1)+1$ for every $i\in[d+1]$, then there exist pairwise disjoint transversals $T_{1},\ldots,T_{t}$ of the color classes whose convex hulls have a common point; that is, $\bigcap_{j=1}^{t}\operatorname{conv}(T_{j})\neq\varnothing.$

[Definition 2 (Cauchy hypersurfaces and Globally hyperbolic regions) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $\mathcal{M} \subset \R^{1+3}$ be an open subset of spacetime on which the fluid variables
	$\vec{\Psi} := \{s,\uprho,v^1,v^2,v^3\}$ are defined and $C^1$,
	and let $\gfour(\vec{\Psi})$ be the acoustical metric defined in \eqref{E:ACOUSTICALMETRICANDMATERIALDER}.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item  We say that a surface $\Sigma \subset \mathcal{M}$ is a \emph{Cauchy hypersurface} for $\mathcal{M}$ (with respect to $\gfour$) if every $\gfour$-timelike inextendible curve in $\mathcal{M}$ intersects $\Sigma$ exactly once.
		\item We say that $(\mathcal{M},\gfour(\vec{\Psi}))$ is \emph{globally hyperbolic} whenever $\mathcal{M}$ contains a Cauchy hypersurface.
	\end{itemize}
title: Cauchy hypersurfaces and Globally hyperbolic regions

\[

[Theorem 10 (Oracle bound over the three fixed statistical comparators) of arXiv:2609.00402, '2609.00402'] Let \(T\geq5\) and let \(\mathcal D_N=\{(\bm X^{(i)},Y^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^N\) consist of independent copies of \((\bm X,Y)\). Before observing \(\mathcal D_N\), fix fully specified deterministic comparators \(\overline h_S,\overline h_V,\overline h_{AR}\) of the forms introduced above. Their specifications include every threshold and calibration constant, the clipping radius, and the selected approximation networks. There exists a fixed CNN classifier class with parallel branches \(\mathcal H\), with the head specification fixed as in Definition~\ref{def:cnn}, such that \(\overline h_S,\overline h_V,\overline h_{AR}\in\mathcal H\). Let \(d_{\mathcal H}=\operatorname{VCdim}(\mathcal H)\), where \(1\leq d_{\mathcal H}\leq N\), and let \(\widehat h_{\mathrm{ERM}}\in\arg\min_{h\in\mathcal H}N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbb I\{h(\bm X^{(i)})\neq Y^{(i)}\}\). Then, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[
\operatorname{err}(\widehat h_{\mathrm{ERM}})
\leq\inf_{h\in\mathcal H}\operatorname{err}(h)+2r_N(d_{\mathcal H},\delta)
\leq\min_{G\in\{S,V,AR\}}\operatorname{err}(\overline h_G)+2r_N(d_{\mathcal H},\delta).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let d,q be positive finite integers. Let H be a constant symmetric positive
definite q by q matrix with extreme eigenvalues 0<m<=M. Let
A:R^d -> R^{q x q} be C^1, A(u)^T A(u)=H, and

    sup_u sum_i ||partial_i A(u)||_op^2 <= D^2 < infinity.

Let z_k be iid R^q-valued labels, independent of the past, with
E z_k=0 and E z_k z_k^T=I_q. No symmetry or higher moment is assumed.
Fix sigma>=0, 0<rho<2, 0<eta<=rho/M, deterministic u_0 and v_0=0.
Consider label-noise SGD

    h_{k,i}:=u_{k+1,i}-u_{k,i}=-eta sigma z_k^T partial_i A(u_k)v_k,
    v_{k+1}=B v_k-eta sigma A(u_k)^T z_k, B=I-eta H.       (1)

For F in C_b^2(R^{d+q}) define f(u)=F(u,0), a(u)=D_v F(u,0), and

    F_2=sup_u ||D^2 f(u)||_op,
    F_vv=sup_{u,v} ||D_v^2 F(u,v)||_op,
    F_uv=sup_u ||D_u a(u)||_op,
    c=sigma^2 q/(2-rho),
    gamma=min{m, M(2-rho)/rho} > 0.

For every T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=k<=T/eta^2}
      |E F(u_k,v_k)-F(u_0,0)| <= eta C(T),               (2)

    C(T)=c [F_vv/2 + T sigma^2 D^2 F_2/2
                       + F_uv sigma D/gamma].         (3)

Thus the slow-clock weak rate is a=1 with an explicit constant linear
in T, with only centered second-moment labels. Covariance proportionality
to the loss Hessian is asserted ON the minimizing manifold v=0, where
the noise covariance is sigma^2 diag(0,H). No off-manifold covariance
proportionality is asserted. The ambient loss is L=v^T H v/2.

The limiting constant tangential process is the known trace-Hessian

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:9083f936c5e3ced10dc9868d11471944fb2b39b9201756769b0343b81377d989","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/90/9083f936c5e3ced10dc9868d11471944fb2b39b9201756769b0343b81377d989.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:72e6c47061681d409a6cdffe53c1ceb42a9775bfbd5b9b0fc9a02f2e8c6f7c82","bundle_entry_key":"t355-centered-nonsymmetric-second-moment","bundle_id":"population.t355-centered-asymmetric-labels-second-moments-003","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"probability","draft":"w730/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.stochastic_approximation:t355-constant-hessian-centered-nonsymmetric-labels-weak-order-one","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Constant normal Hessian: centered labels need not be symmetric

Claim w730-T355-C005, version 1. Kind: narrowed. Target: 1.
Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unestablished; independent review required.

## Statement

Let d,q be positive finite integers. Let H be a constant symmetric positive
definite q by q matrix with extreme eigenvalues 0<m<=M. Let
A:R^d -> R^{q x q} be C^1, A(u)^T A(u)=H, and

    sup_u sum_i ||partial_i A(u)||_op^2 <= D^2 < infinity.

Let z_k be iid R^q-valued labels, independent of the past, with
E z_k=0 and E z_k z_k^T=I_q. No symmetry or higher moment is assumed.
Fix sigma>=0, 0<rho<2, 0<eta<=rho/M, deterministic u_0 and v_0=0.
Consider label-noise SGD

    h_{k,i}:=u_{k+1,i}-u_{k,i}=-eta sigma z_k^T partial_i A(u_k)v_k,
    v_{k+1}=B v_k-eta sigma A(u_k)^T z_k, B=I-eta H.       (1)

For F in C_b^2(R^{d+q}) define f(u)=F(u,0), a(u)=D_v F(u,0), and

    F_2=sup_u ||D^2 f(u)||_op,
    F_vv=sup_{u,v} ||D_v^2 F(u,v)||_op,
    F_uv=sup_u ||D_u a(u)||_op,
    c=sigma^2 q/(2-rho),
    gamma=min{m, M(2-rho)/rho} > 0.

For every T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=k<=T/eta^2}
      |E F(u_k,v_k)-F(u_0,0)| <= eta C(T),               (2)

    C(T)=c [F_vv/2 + T sigma^2 D^2 F_2/2
                       + F_uv sigma D/gamma].         (3)

Thus the slow-clock weak rate is a=1 with an explicit constant linear
in T, with only centered second-moment labels. Covariance proportionality
to the loss Hessian is asserted ON the minimizing manifold v=0, where
the noise covariance is sigma^2 diag(0,H). No off-manifold covariance
proportionality is asserted. The ambient loss is L=v^T H v/2.

The limiting constant tangential process is the known trace-Hessian
flow: Li-Wang-Arora, arXiv:2110.06914v4, Corollary 5.2, pp.8-9 and 33.
The quantitative estimate and removal of symmetry are candidate results,
not a verified priority claim. General T355 remains open.

## Proof

### Normal second moments and tangential martingale increments

These calculations are the same as C004 v2, equations (2)-(5); they use
centering and unit covariance, not central symmetry. They are included
to make this version independently readable. Conditional expectation
in (1), with the fresh label independent of (u_k,v_k), gives

    Q_{k+1}=B Q_k B+eta^2 sigma^2 H, Q_0=0,
    Q_k=eta sigma^2 (I-B^{2k})(2I-eta H)^{-1},
    E|v_k|^2=tr Q_k<=eta c.                             (4)

The middle formula follows by diagonalizing H and summing a finite
geometric series. For each eigenvalue lambda, its contribution is
eta sigma^2[1-(1-eta lambda)^{2k}]/(2-eta lambda), whose bracket is
in [0,1] and denominator at least 2-rho. Finite second moments follow
inductively from the first equality; no fourth moments enter.

Similarly conditional mean zero and unit covariance give

    E[h_k|past]=0,
    E[|h_k|^2|past]
      =eta^2 sigma^2 sum_i |partial_i A(u_k)v_k|^2,
    E|h_k|^2<=eta^3 sigma^2 D^2 c.                     (5)

All states are finite almost surely at finite k. These bounds also give
the integrability needed below. Taylor expansion of f and conditional
centering imply, for K eta^2<=T,

    |E f(u_K)-f(u_0)|<=T eta sigma^2 D^2 c F_2/2.       (6)

Here the first-order term has zero expectation since grad f is bounded
and adapted, and the second-order remainder is bounded by F_2|h_k|^2/2.

### Mixed normal-linear observable: the new step

Set r=||B||_op=max_lambda |1-eta lambda|<1. For lambda in [m,M],

    1-|1-eta lambda|=min{eta lambda, 2-eta lambda}
       >=min{eta m, 2-rho}>=eta gamma.

The last inequality uses eta<=rho/M. Thus 1-r>=eta gamma.

Let a:R^d->R^q be any bounded globally Lipschitz function with Lipschitz
constant L_a. Define the q by q matrix N_k=E[v_k a(u_k)^T]. Since v_0=0,
N_0=0. Add and subtract a(u_k) in N_{k+1}. Conditional centering of z_k
then gives the exact recurrence

    N_{k+1}=B N_k+R_k,
    R_k=E[v_{k+1}(a(u_{k+1})-a(u_k))^T].               (7)

Every matrix entry is integrable by boundedness of a and (4). For the
remainder, Lipschitz continuity and Cauchy-Schwarz give

    E[|v_{k+1}| |a(u_{k+1})-a(u_k)|]
      <=L_a sqrt(E|v_{k+1}|^2 E|h_k|^2)
      <=L_a sigma D c eta^2.                          (8)

No factorization of these correlated factors is used. Iterate (7) as
a finite matrix identity and take its trace. For any j>=0,

    |tr(B^j R_k)|
      =|E[(a(u_{k+1})-a(u_k))^T B^j v_{k+1}]|
      <=r^j L_a sigma D c eta^2.

Consequently, for every integer K>=0,

    |E[a(u_K)^T v_K]|=|tr N_K|
      <=L_a sigma D c eta^2 sum_{j=0}^{K-1} r^j
      <=L_a sigma D c eta/gamma.                      (9)

The empty sum handles K=0. This reusable bound replaces the exact
cancellation by central symmetry used in C004. It is uniform in K.

### Finish the ambient observable estimate

For the particular a(u)=D_v F(u,0), boundedness and the mixed derivative
bound imply L_a<=F_uv. Taylor's theorem in v yields

    |F(u,v)-f(u)-a(u)^T v|<=F_vv |v|^2/2.

Take expectations and use (4), (9), and (6). The resulting sum is
exactly eta times (3). This proves (2). Sigma=0, D=0 and T=0 require
no division by these quantities; gamma is strictly positive regardless.
Only finite second moments and fresh-label independence were used.

## Scope and hardest step for review

The hardest new step is the matrix recurrence (7), followed by taking
the trace AFTER its finite iteration. Replacing N_k by the scalar
E[a(u_k)^T v_k] before iterating would be unjustified for general H.
The proof keeps the matrix until the final trace.

The constant-Hessian target is addressed in its dossier's on-manifold
covariance interpretation, including rotating output frames. Fixed
off-manifold initial conditions, general curved manifolds and a
general nonconstant-Hessian second-moment theorem remain open.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:08b3aa9336b41d073eb6de91b15afd0d66f6d3fd85b3e933c0f173755e184645","revision_digest":"sha256:f352559210980586d3a503006032dcc6bc9cc4a6393ff741b69c4afe3aa09c8e","source_id":"own-work:w730:T355:w730-T355-C005:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem 1 (Representative lifts and quotient geodesics) of arXiv:2608.26961, 'Gromov--Monge Flow Matching for Equivariant Graph Generation'] Let \(\bmu,\bnu\in\mP_2(Q)\), fix \(\mu\in[\bmu]\), and let
\(\Gamma\in\mathrm{c}_Q(\bmu,\bnu)\). There exist
\(\nu_\Gamma\in[\bnu]\) and
\(\gamma_\Gamma\in\mathrm{c}_{\R^D}(\mu,\nu_\Gamma)\) such that
\((\mathfrak q,\mathfrak q)_\sharp\gamma_\Gamma=\Gamma\) and
\[
\int_{\R^D\times\R^D}\|x-y\|^2\,\d\gamma_\Gamma(x,y)
=
\int_{Q\times Q}d_Q(\bx,\by)^2\,\d\Gamma(\bx,\by).
\]
If \(\Gamma\) is optimal, then \(\gamma_\Gamma\) is optimal between its
representative marginals. Moreover, in this case, with
\(\pr^t(x,y)=(1-t)x+ty\) and
\(\mu_t\coloneqq\pr^t_\sharp\gamma_\Gamma\), the projected curve
\(\bmu_t\coloneqq\mathfrak q_\sharp\mu_t\) is a constant-speed
\(\W_{2,Q}\)-geodesic, and the flow-matching field associated with the lifted
coupling \(\gamma_\Gamma\) satisfies
\[
\int_I\int_{\R^D}\|v_t^{\gamma_\Gamma}(z)\|^2
\,\d\mu_t(z)\,\d t
=\W_{2,Q}^2(\bmu,\bnu).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Representative lifts and quotient geodesics

[Lem 13 (Endpoint residual estimates) of arXiv:2607.28865, 'First-Passage Percolation on Spread-out line graphs: Microscopic Regime'] Assume $\ell\ge2$. Recall the residual terms $\sfRT_n$ and $\sfRH_n$ defined in~\eqref{eq:residual-def}.
\begin{enumeratei}
    \item Under Condition~\textup{B.\ref{ass:B1}}, the sequence $\{\sfRT_n\}_{n\ge1}$ is tight, and the sequence $\{\sfRH_n\}_{n\ge1}$ is uniformly bounded in $L^q$ for every $q\ge1$.
    \item Under Condition~\textup{B.\ref{ass:B2}}, both residual sequences have uniformly bounded moments of all orders. That is, for every $q\ge1$,
    \[
        \sup_{n\ge1}\E\left[\big(\sfRT_n\big)^q+\big(\sfRH_n\big)^q\right] < \infty.
    \]
\end{enumeratei}

Let f_n : [a,b] -> R be Riemann integrable, uniformly bounded (|f_n| <= M for all n), and suppose f_n -> f pointwise on [a,b] where f is ALSO Riemann integrable. Then integral_a^b f_n -> integral_a^b f. The Riemann integrability of the limit must be ASSUMED and does not follow: enumerate the rationals of [0,1] as q_1, q_2, ... and let f_n be the indicator of {q_1, ..., q_n}. Each f_n is Riemann integrable with integral 0, the family is bounded by 1, and f_n increases pointwise to the indicator of the rationals, which is not Riemann integrable. This is the essential defect that the Lebesgue integral repairs: the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem needs only measurability of the limit, which is automatic for a pointwise limit of measurable functions. Historically Arzela proved this in 1885 by a direct and rather delicate covering argument, before the Lebesgue theory existed. [Arzela (1885); see e.g. Luxemburg, 'Arzela's dominated convergence theorem for the Riemann integral', Amer. Math. Monthly 78 (1971)]

[Theorem th:main of arXiv:2504.11107, 'An Invariance Principle for some\\% Reaction-Diffusion Equations with a Multiplicative Ran'] Suppose that Assumption (ass:par of the paper) holds, and
	recall the definition of the constant ${\rm L}_g$ from part (2) of 
        that assumption. Suppose that
	\begin{equation}
		\sup_{z>0} |f(z)/z|<  {\rm L}_g^2/64.
	\end{equation}
	Then, for every $\varepsilon\in(0\,,1)$
	there exist nonrandom numbers $S=S(\varepsilon)>0$ and $\beta
	=\beta(\varepsilon) \in (0\,, 1)$, 
	and a coupling $(u\,,w)$ -- that depends on the choice of $\varepsilon$ --
	where the space-time random field $w = \{w(t\,,x)\}_{t\geqslant0,x\in\mathbb{T}}$ solves (equation SHE of the paper) and 
	the space-time random field $u=\{u(t\,,x)\}_{t\geqslant S,x\in\mathbb{T}}$ is a solution to (equation PAM of the paper)
	shifted by $S$ time units and started at $w(S)$; that is,
	\begin{equation}\left[\begin{split}
		&\partial_t u = \partial^2_x u + \mu u  + \sigma u\dot{W}_0
			\hskip.45in\text{on $(S\,,\infty)\times\mathbb{T}$},\\
		&\text{subject to }u(0)=w(S)\hskip.9in\text{on $\mathbb{T}$},
	\end{split}\right.\end{equation}
	for a suitably constructed
	space-time white noise $\dot{W}_0$, such that
	\[\textstyle
		\mathrm{P}\left\{ \| \log w(t) - \log u(t) \|_{C(\mathbb{T})} 
		=O( t^{-\beta})\text{\ as $t\to\infty$} \right\} \geqslant 
		1 - \varepsilon. 
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorema 4 (\Cref{GPS-to-ANV}) of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(k\) be a perfect field of characteristic \(p > 0\) and let \(X\) be a smooth projective
scheme over \(W(k)\).
If \(X\) is globally \(+\)-regular, then its closed fiber $X_k \defeq X\times_{W(k)}k$ is HT-split.
Furthermore, we obtain the following Akizuki--Nakano-type vanishing in mixed characteristic: for every ample line bundle \(L\) on \(X\),
\[
R^i\Gamma_{(p)}R\Gamma\left(
X,
\Omega^j_{X/W(k)}\otimes L^{-1}
\right)
=0
\qquad
\text{whenever }i+j<\dim X.
\]
In particular, this vanishing implies \(H^i(X, \Omega^j_{X/W(k)} \otimes L^{-1}) = 0\) for \(i + j < \dim X - 1\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \Cref{GPS-to-ANV}

For n>=2, let J_n be the nilpotent matrix with ones on the superdiagonal, and C_n=J_n+e_n e_1^T. Their difference has rank one, but the empirical eigenvalue laws differ by one on the bounded 1-Lipschitz test f(z)=min(|z|,1): J_n has only zero eigenvalues and C_n has all nth roots of unity. Thus a Hermitian-style rank/n bound cannot control nonnormal empirical eigenvalue laws in general. This deterministic example is not an iid circular-law lower bound.

[Definition 49 (Trunk paths and vertices) of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] Under $\q^m_n$, we have 
\[
X_j = m, \quad \text{for all } \bar{h} \le j \le \bar{h} + \lfloor c_0 n \rfloor.
\]
In other words, for each $j$ between $\bar{h}$ and $\bar{h}+\lfloor c_0 n\rfloor$, there are exactly $m$ vertices in $\cX_j$. These vertices belong to $m$ distinct ancestral lineages that remain separate at height $\bar{h}$. 
Let $\mathsf{T}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{T}_m$ be the $m$ coalescent subtrees at height $\bar{h}$.  
For $\bar{h}\le j \le \bar{h}+\lfloor c_0 n \rfloor$ and $1\le i\le m$, denote by 
\(z^j_i \in V(\mathsf{T}_i)\)
the unique vertex of $\mathsf{T}_i$ at height $j$. 
The sequence
\[
Z_i := \big(z^{\bar{h}+\lfloor c_0 n \rfloor}_i, z^{\bar{h}+\lfloor c_0 n \rfloor-1}_i, \ldots, z^{\bar{h}}_i\big)
\]
is called the trunk path of $\mathsf{T}_i$, and its elements are referred to as the trunk vertices of $\mathsf{T}_i$.  
The remaining $q_n(j)-m$ non-trunk vertices at height $j$ are denoted by $y^j_1, \ldots, y^j_{q_n(j)-m}$, where the subscripts are assigned arbitrary.
title: Trunk paths and vertices

[Definition 9 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] For $\bs{q}\in\Delta_d$, $\pi\in\on{Sym}(d)$, and $t\in[d]$, define
the {suffix mass}
\[
  s_t^\pi(\bs{q})
  :=\sum_{r=t}^d q_{\pi(r)}.
\]
Thus, $s_t^\pi(\bs{q})$ is the total $\bs{q}$-mass of the elements in
position $t$ or later in the ordering $\pi$. Define
\begin{align*}
  F(\bs{q})
  &:=\E_\pi\left[
       \sum_{t=1}^d q_{\pi(t)}
       \log\frac{s_t^\pi(\bs{q})}{q_{\pi(t)}}
     \right]
     -S(\bs{q})
  =\E_\pi\left[
       \sum_{t=1}^d q_{\pi(t)}
       \log s_t^\pi(\bs{q})
     \right]
     +H_{\mr c}(\bs{q}),
\end{align*}
where $\pi$ is uniformly distributed on $\on{Sym}(d)$.
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2609.02017

Let d>=2, N>=2, and let C be a set of N distinct points on the unit sphere S^(d-1). Let t_1<...<t_m<1 be exactly the distinct inner products between distinct points of C, m>=1, and assume C is a spherical (2m-1)-design: every polynomial on R^d of degree<=2m-1 has the same average over C as under normalized uniform surface measure. Put F(t)=product_(i=1)^m(t-t_i). Let p_j be the monic orthogonal polynomials for the nonnegative measure (1-t)(1-t^2)^((d-3)/2)dt on [-1,1]. There is a real alpha such that F=p_m+alpha p_(m-1). Equivalently F is orthogonal to every polynomial of degree<=m-2 for this modified measure. For m=1 this orthogonality condition is empty and the displayed representation still holds. No sign condition on alpha is asserted. This is Lemma6.3 of Cohn-Kumar.

[Definition d:chart of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] A \emph{chart of dimension $n$} on a metric measure space $(X,d,\mu)$ is a pair $(U,\phi)$ where:
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item $U \subset X$ is measurable, $m(U) >0$, and $\phi:X \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is Lipschitz.
			\item For every Lipschitz function $f: X \to \mathbb{R}$, there exists a measurable function $\partial_\phi f: U \to \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $f$ is differentiable with respect to $\phi$ at $m$-almost every $x_0 \in U$ and with derivative $\partial_\phi f(x_0)$.
		\end{enumerate}
		A \textbf{measurable differentiable structure}	on $(X,d,\mu)$ is a  countable collection $\{(U_\alpha,\phi_\alpha)\}$ of charts with uniformly bounded dimension such that $$\mu \left( X \setminus \bigcup_{\alpha} U_\alpha\right)=0.$$
title: Definition d:chart of arXiv:2510.13659

[Proposition pro: refinement JSQ of arXiv:2603.14163, '\LARGE \bf Tail Bounds for Queues with Abandonment: Constant, Moderate, Large Deviations, '] Under the assumption (ass:heavy_overload of the paper), with $\gamma\leq \gamma_1$ defined in (equation eq: gamma assumption for JSQ W-p of the paper), and same notations as in Theorem (thm: JSQ Tail bound of the paper). Let $\boldsymbol{\phi}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\|\boldsymbol{\phi}\|=1$ and $\boldsymbol{\phi}\geq 0$ coordinate-wise. Then, for any $a \geq e^2n\sqrt{\lambda}/\sqrt{\gamma}$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{P}(\langle \tilde{\mathbf{q}},\boldsymbol{\phi}\rangle > a) \leq \exp\left( - \left(\frac{1}{\langle \boldsymbol{\phi}, \boldsymbol{1}\rangle} \frac{\sqrt{\lambda}}{2n\sqrt{\gamma}}a + \frac{\lambda-\mu}{n\gamma} \right) \log\left( \frac{1}{\langle \boldsymbol{\phi}, \boldsymbol{1}\rangle} \frac{\sqrt{\gamma}}{n\sqrt{\lambda}}a + \frac{\lambda-\mu}{n\sqrt{\lambda\gamma}}  \right) \right).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem theorem ethier kurtz modes of convergence of arXiv:2512.20338, 'Up-down chains and scaling limits: \\ application to permuton- and graphon-valued diffusio'] Let 
    $ T_n $ be the transition operator of $ Y_n $, 
    $ \{ T( t ) \}_{ t \ge 0 } $ a Feller semigroup on $ C( E ) $, 
    $ A $ the generator of $ \{ T( t ) \}_{ t \ge 0 } $,
    and 
    $ D $ a core for $ A $.
    For any positive sequence $ \{  \varepsilon _n \}_{ n \ge 1 } $ converging to zero, the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}[ label = (\roman*) ]
    
      \item 
        $
        	T_n^{  \lfloor  t/ \varepsilon _n  \rfloor  }
        	\pi_n
        	f
        		\to
        			T( t ) f
        $
        for every $ f \in C( E ) $ and $ t \ge 0 $,
  
      \item 
        $
        	e^{ ( T_n - I ) t / \varepsilon _n }
        	\pi_n
        	f
        		\to
        			T( t ) f
        $
        for every $ f \in C( E ) $ and $ t \ge 0 $,
     
    	\item
    	the above convergences hold uniformly in $ t $ on bounded intervals,
    
    	\item
    	for each $ f \in D $, there exists a sequence $ \{ f_n \}_{ n \ge 1 } $ with $ f_n \in C( E_n ) $ such that
        $$
        	f_n \to f
    			\qquad
    			\text{ and }
    			\qquad
    		 \varepsilon _n^{ -1 } 
    		( T_n - I )
        	f_n
        		\to
        			A f
        		.
        $$
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 2 of arXiv:2605.23659, '2605.23659'] For each \(i\in I\), define the restricted point process
\[
N^{(i)} := N(\cdot\cap ([0,\infty)\times D_{0}^{(i)})),
\]
and let
\[
n^{(i)} := n(\cdot \cap D_{0}^{(i)}).
\]
Then \(\{N^{(i)}\}_{i\in I}\) is a family of independent Poisson point processes with intensity measures \(dt\otimes n^{(i)}\). Moreover,
\[
N=\sum_{i\in I} N^{(i)}
\]
as random measures, almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 2 of arXiv:2605.23659

[Lemma lem:hill-paths of arXiv:2608.08375, 'Algebraic formulas for first-passage times of Markov processes in the linear framework: ge'] Under the conditions stated previously, if $k \in \overline{Z}$, then $u \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} k$ if, and only if, $u \leadsto_G k$.

\proof If $u = k$, the conclusion is trivial, so assume that $u \neq k$. If $u \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} k$, then there is a path, $u = j_1 \to \dotsb \to j_n = k$, of edges in $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$. We may assume that this path does not revisit $u$, so that $u \neq j_2, \dotsc, j_{n-1}$, for otherwise we can simply consider the portion of this path starting from the last visit to $u$. Since none of these edges now enter $u$, it follows from Definition~(def:hill of the paper).1 that they must have arisen from edges in $G$, so that $u \leadsto_G k$. Now suppose that $u \leadsto_G k$, so that there exists a directed path, $u = i_1 \to \dotsb \to i_m = k$, of edges in $G$. As before, we may assume that $u \neq i_2, \dotsc, i_m$, so that none of the edges enter $u$. Since $k$ is non-terminal, each vertex along the path must also be non-terminal. It then follows from Definition~(def:hill of the paper).1 that each edge must also exist in $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$, so that $u \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} k$.
\hfill \qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn eq:Ae-def of arXiv:2609.00110, 'Phase Transition and Fluctuation Results for First-Passage Percolation on Spread-Out Cycle'] Let $e=\{u,v\}$ be a bridge, where $u$ has label $1$ and $v$ has label $2$. 
Its original activation time and the lower bound recorded at activation are
\begin{align*}
 \gt_e^{\mathrm{act}}
 &:=
 \max\{\widehat\mathsf{T}_1(u),\widehat\mathsf{T}_2(v)\},\\
 L_e^{\mathrm{act}}
 &:=
 \big(\gt_e^{\mathrm{act}}-\widehat\mathsf{T}_1(u)\big)
 +
 \big(\gt_e^{\mathrm{act}}-\widehat\mathsf{T}_2(v)\big).
\end{align*}
The corresponding residual in the cumulative-hazard scale is
\begin{align*}
 R_e
 := H(\go_e)-H(L_e^{\mathrm{act}}) 
 = \go_e^\theta-(L_e^{\mathrm{act}})^\theta.
\end{align*}

For $q\geqslant\gt_e^{\mathrm{act}}$, define the collision threshold
\begin{align*}
 L_e(q)
 :=
 \big(q-\widehat\mathsf{T}_1(u)\big)
 +
 \big(q-\widehat\mathsf{T}_2(v)\big).
\end{align*}
In particular, $L_e(\gt_e^{\mathrm{act}})=L_e^{\mathrm{act}}$.

For $s\geqslant\mathfrak{a}_\ell\gt_e^{\mathrm{act}}$, define the rescaled bridge age by
\begin{align}
 A_e(s)
 :=
 \big(s-\mathfrak{a}_\ell\widehat\mathsf{T}_1(u)\big)
 +
 \big(s-\mathfrak{a}_\ell\widehat\mathsf{T}_2(v)\big).
\end{align}
Then $ L_e(s/\mathfrak{a}_\ell)=\frac{A_e(s)}{\mathfrak{a}_\ell}$.

The cumulative bridge hazard at rescaled time $s$ is
\begin{align}
 \gL_s
 &:= \sum_{e\in\mathcal{B}_s}
 \left[ H\left(\frac{A_e(s)}{\mathfrak{a}_\ell}\right) - H(L_e^{\mathrm{act}}) \right]
 =\sum_{e\in\mathcal{B}_s}\left[\left(\frac{A_e(s)}{\mathfrak{a}_\ell }\right)^\theta
 -(L_e^{\mathrm{act}})^\theta\right]
 \notag\\
 &=\int_0^s \frac{2\theta}{\mathfrak{a}_\ell ^\theta}
 \sum_{e\in\mathcal{B}_q} A_e(q)^{\theta-1}\,\mathrm d q.
\end{align}
title: Bridge thresholds, residuals, and cumulative hazard

		\begin{enumerate}[label=(S\arabic*),ref=S\arabic*]
			\item for every $\alpha\in I$, $S_\alpha$ is a connected, smooth, finite--dimensional
			manifold without boundary, equipped with a Riemannian metric $g_\alpha$;
			\item the inclusion $\iota_\alpha: S_\alpha \hookrightarrow E$ is a homeomorphism onto its image
			and this image is a Borel subset of \(E\).
		\end{enumerate}
		We call $(E,\{S_\alpha,g_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ a stratified Riemannian state space in the Borel sense.

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: an interior ball touching the boundary at the point x0 in question (and, for the strong maximum principle, the fact that such a ball can always be produced inside the open set where the solution is strictly below its maximum). Without it the conclusion 'the inward derivative at a boundary minimum is strictly positive' is false. Counterexample at a convex corner: in the plane let Omega be the sector {0 < theta < beta, 0 < r < 1} with 0 < beta < pi and u(r, theta) = r^{pi/beta} sin(pi theta/beta). Then u is harmonic in Omega, continuous on the closure, u > 0 inside and u = 0 on both straight edges, so 0 is a strict boundary minimum of u; but pi/beta > 1, so for every direction e pointing into Omega the difference quotient (u(te) - u(0))/t = O(t^{pi/beta - 1}) tends to 0: there is no Hopf gain at the vertex. No interior ball touches the vertex, exactly as the hypothesis requires. How far the hypothesis can be relaxed: the interior sphere condition may be replaced by an interior C^{1,Dini} (or interior paraboloid/cone-with-Dini) condition, but not by mere C^1 regularity of the boundary; there are C^1 domains where a positive harmonic function vanishing on the boundary has vanishing gradient at a boundary point - for instance the image of the upper half-plane near 0 under the conformal map z -> z log(1/z), whose boundary is C^1 but not Dini smooth at 0, and for which the inverse map has derivative tending to 0. Practical rule for an auditor: a proof that invokes Hopf's lemma (to get strict inequality, strict monotonicity, a sign of the normal derivative, simplicity of the first eigenvalue, or the strong maximum principle at the boundary) must say why the domain has the interior ball property at the relevant point; convex corners and cusps of the domain are where this silently breaks.
title: Pitfall: The Hopf Lemma Needs an Interior Sphere Condition
